_**A Special Message from our Sponsor**_ _Please note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of_ _Free Speech Daily_ _and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily_ _._
---
| Doing the right thing whether it's popular or not. John Fetterman Doing the right thing whether it's popular or not. | | | | | [](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjQsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2yZkkzE7DfoXdXWZn_Bc7lXbOtYhrhaKDrHedMV2y6Or95Sw_PbqpvHWduhlsAkUlma7n9dzQJkN7di1GJP4tiAMyZtDHHbEIL07Bdx)
---
Dear Fellow Patriot, I’ll bet you’re more than a little surprised to get this email from me. But please set aside party affiliation for a second and hear me out. You see, I’m not a progressive. And I’m __definitely__ not a Democratic Socialist. I’m just a senator with a big mouth who happens to stand with Israel. Today, I’m asking you to do the same by signing your **[“Stand with Israel” Emergency Declaration.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjQsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2yZkkzFoMOS9OsPcJ74cU6D0PVINFPENIYLxl_8-jqmkBjwjX0ysNMR04mN0IZVGye9uXDlDEVplpmkJF2cd4H6ZoHktHvTsKqGvuf7)**
---
[ **STAND WITH ISRAEL** ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjQsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2yZkkzGaWJwrpZL2wYH_VPx3lqdHYLciWO-cbrYLIzLghDVV6EyolqK1_p_D8doDa2dc5sAbTVwc6EVZjnEScw6ifKUFz9tri4WOFBb)
---
You see, when I heard about October 7th and how they tortured, mutilated, and murdered Israeli families, I thought to myself that if that was my family, I’d say that that kind of evil should not be allowed to endure. It has to be destroyed. And I can’t imagine why the entire world wouldn’t be appalled by that kind of barbarism. Yet, too many on the radical left are siding against Israel. I mean... why? Why would you stand with the kind of regimes that force their people to live under values that so-called progressives in America would never live? They’ve lost any kind of moral bearings. Whenever I’m in a situation to be called on to take up the cause of enhancing the security of Israel or deepening our relationship between the United States and Israel, I’m going to lean in. One group that always has my back and is making the biggest impact in this fight is Americans for Israel. I am really thankful for them. Because this crazy Democratic Socialist movement is:
---
* ****Denying Israel the right to protest itself, let alone fight back against those who wish to destroy it****
* ****Pro-Iran, Pro-Hamas and Pro-Hezbollah****
* ****Supporting a Palestinian, “one-state solution”****

---
Heck, one of the DSA’s “rising stars” – Abdul El-Sayed – is campaigning in Michigan with radical influencer Hasan Piker who thinks _“ _America deserved 9/11_.”_ This isn’t just radical, it is dangerous. And that is why you need to sign your **[“Stand with Israel” Emergency Declaration](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjQsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2yZkkzHEW1C87sCbRhGlvFZy2PGeboKVm_ffremM09Iop0nhySVh-6SSZB_gG_1kKl80HYsAmRgJaB0gYgX95r6NH_wnG5XctnnF0Sp)** and submit it to _Americans for Israel_ today to help them in their mission to _educate_ , _advocate_ , and _activate_ Americans of all political affiliations to unite and stand for Israel. I am proud to support them. What about you? Will you? Please hurry. This kind of evil cannot be allowed to endure.
---
| | | Thank you very much, **John Fetterman,**
**United States Senator (PA)**
---
| | [](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjQsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2yZkkzICOAwscmCMyreprnUp0IUaHdtDyabLX5JhjlJRvdVok7BhW-q3CJRL9VKTMikBJmvLb6fexjmItVZmvsorxJeGXsreCqFlqOw)
---
| | | P.S. If I’m the last on my side of the aisle to have this kind of a view, so be it. I’m sticking with Israel. It might not be considered a political winner, but like, so what? _Judge me_. And, in the meantime, do whatever you can do to help our brothers and sisters in Israel.
---
[ **STAND WITH ISRAEL** ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjQsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA2yZkkzJ2uO-bQnijMOmji1UnDBOYdnRNFy1Un26V31C3j5pnhk_mCM2rbJ8l5sWC4lmWgn9Uc2qRK4z84u6UjCspA4A6bdMtvBZqW2h)

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261009-61892&t=1001&akid=61892%2E1407376%2EU5c8EF ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261009-61892&t=1002&akid=61892%2E1407376%2EU5c8EF ]Demand Justice PAC

A Senate
investigation into the Supreme Court uncovered decades of ethical
misconduct: lavish gifts from billionaires, violations of federal
disclosure law, and justices ruling on cases despite clear conflicts of
interest.

And not one justice has faced a consequence.

Let's start with the gifts. Billionaire Harlan Crow has flown Justice
Clarence Thomas on private jets, hosted him on a superyacht, and paid
tuition for the grandnephew Thomas was raising... most of which Thomas never
disclosed.

Justice Samuel Alito did it too. He flew to a luxury Alaska fishing trip
on a billionaire's private jet, in a seat worth about $23,776, and
reported nothing.

Hiding gifts is one problem. Ruling on cases they’re legally required to
sit out is another.

Ginni Thomas helped push to overturn the 2020 election, and the law says a
justice must sit out cases where their spouse has a real stake. Justice
Thomas sat on all but one of the Court's cases about 2020 and January 6
anyway.

Days after January 6, a "Stop the Steal" symbol was outside Justice
Alito's home. He still refused to step aside from Trump's immunity case.

So who's holding them accountable? Not Chief Justice Roberts, who refused
to testify. Not the Court's own ethics code, which has no enforcement or
penalties.

These justices decide whether you can vote, what happens to your body, and
whether a president is above the law. Right now, they answer to no one.

That leaves Congress. Only Congress can write an enforceable ethics code
into law, and the Senate's own investigators concluded it has to.^1

That's where Demand Justice PAC comes in. We're making Supreme Court
accountability an issue no Senate candidate can dodge, and that takes
serious resources.

Thank you,

name: Gabby Giffords

disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
#

Can I show you something?
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261009-1-b&refcode2=11905.3935704.fTUYeV&t=1&akid=11905%2E3935704%2EfTUYeV)
This is a replica of my skull after being shot in the head. I was at a constituent event in 2011 when I was the target of a politically motivated shooting. The gunman killed six people and wounded 12 others.
The doctors made a replica of my skull to create the titanium plate that was used to replace the part of my skull that had to be removed due to swelling. I keep it to remind myself of what I survived on that awful day in January 2011.
It’s been fifteen years since my shooting, but not a week goes by when I don’t think about it. Some days are harder than others, but I never stop fighting.
I see our fight to end gun violence the same way. There may be setbacks, but we can never lose sight of our work to save lives from the gun violence crisis.
**But too many politicians have shown that they’d rather cave to the gun lobby than fight for our families. As I write this, Donald Trump and his allies are working to roll back our progress and help their gun CEO buddies profit. Enough is enough.**
Everything is at stake in the midterm elections. I am working to rally voters and elect gun safety champions across the country, but the only way we can continue sharing our message is with your support.
**So before logging off for the weekend, I am personally asking:** [**Will you pitch in $10 or more to help GIFFORDS PAC elect leaders in the most competitive of races and power our work to end gun violence?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261009-1-b&t=2&akid=11905%2E3935704%2EfTUYeV)

clean_body: Can I show you something? This is a replica of my skull after being shot in the head. I was at a constituent event in 2011 when I was the target of a politically motivated shooting. The gunman killed six people and wounded 12 others. The doctors made a replica of my skull to create the titanium plate that was used to replace the part of my skull that had to be removed due to swelling. I keep it to remind myself of what I survived on that awful day in January 2011. It’s been fifteen years since my shooting, but not a week goes by when I don’t think about it. Some days are harder than others, but I never stop fighting. I see our fight to end gun violence the same way. There may be setbacks, but we can never lose sight of our work to save lives from the gun violence crisis. But too many politicians have shown that they’d rather cave to the gun lobby than fight for our families. As I write this, Donald Trump and his allies are working to roll back our progress and help their gun CEO buddies profit. Enough is enough. Everything is at stake in the midterm elections. I am working to rally voters and elect gun safety champions across the country, but the only way we can continue sharing our message is with your support. Hello – it’s Eileen Laubacher, the Democrat and retired U.S. Navy Rear Admiral running against Lauren Boebert here in Colorado. **I’m emailing to ask if you can make your first donation to my campaign today to help me defeat Lauren Boebert and take back the House for Democrats.**
Here’s why: When I retired from the Navy, I was looking forward to more time with my husband, our five kids, and our three grandchildren. But I guess service to country is in my blood.
My father served 37 years in the Navy, and my grandfather fought fascism as a frogman in WWII. Since preschool, I was determined to go to the Naval Academy to follow in their footsteps – well before women could even attend.
When I look now at how Donald Trump and Lauren Boebert are trying to tear up our Constitution, I shudder at what my grandfather would think. Many of the same dangerous forces that he and his shipmates risked their lives to defeat are taking root here at home.
**I am running to defeat Lauren Boebert because I took an oath in the Navy to defend our Constitution against all threats, foreign and domestic – even when those threats are sitting members of Congress.**

| | | Friend, Bishop Michael Burbidge of Arlington, Virginia wrote an official letter urging Catholics to **vote ****against** the Right to Reproductive Freedom Amendment and the Remove Constitutional Same-sex Marriage Ban Amendment. He then asked all priests in the Diocese to read the letter aloud at Mass, which serves more than 430,000 Catholics in 70 different parishes. **We join our partners at Catholics for Choice to call out this blatant religious overreach.** We see no need to give the fearmongering and unchecked disinformation the light of day. Instead, let’s set the record straight. The claims in Bishop Burbridge’s letter are nothing more than the bishop’s spin and not the truth. The hierarchy’s position does not reflect what ordinary Catholics know to be just. In reality:
* 6 in 10 Catholics believe abortion should be legal in all or most cases.
* Only 1 in 10 Catholics is aligned with the bishop’s extreme, total anti-abortion views.
* 68% of Catholics did not want to see _Roe v. Wade_ overturned.
* 1 in 4 abortion patients is Catholic.

Contrary to what the Catholic hierarchy wants you to believe, pro-choice Catholics are not alone. Far from it. Catholic history indicates that true Catholicism is based on a deep respect for each individual’s conscience — not a bishop’s demands — when making moral decisions. **With only 25 days until voting concludes in Virginia, we need to stop the spread of misinformation and make sure Virginians know how important it is to vote Yes on 1.** **[Can we count on you to chip in just $10 to the YES on 1 campaign today?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141019610/652280663/241827350?refcode=100926&sourceid=1052158&ms=100926&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNMDEvMS8xMTg5NjAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzE1NWZlMzgtZThjMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=j9UJBZHE-hs01Exni2rCVa02Zrdf5A4w8Dtu_Kk9rgs=)**

clean_body: We won't let them spin the truth.| | | | | | | | | | | | | Friend, Bishop Michael Burbidge of Arlington, Virginia wrote an official letter urging Catholics to vote against the Right to Reproductive Freedom Amendment and the Remove Constitutional Same-sex Marriage Ban Amendment. He then asked all priests in the Diocese to read the letter aloud at Mass, which serves more than 430,000 Catholics in 70 different parishes. We join our partners at Catholics for Choice to call out this blatant religious overreach. We see no need to give the fearmongering and unchecked disinformation the light of day. Instead, let’s set the record straight. The claims in Bishop Burbridge’s letter are nothing more than the bishop’s spin and not the truth. The hierarchy’s position does not reflect what ordinary Catholics know to be just. In reality: 6 in 10 Catholics believe abortion should be legal in all or most cases. Only 1 in 10 Catholics is aligned with the bishop’s extreme, total anti-abortion views. 68% of Catholics did not want to see Roe v. Wade overturned. 1 in 4 abortion patients is Catholic. Contrary to what the Catholic hierarchy wants you to believe, pro-choice Catholics are not alone. Far from it. Catholic history indicates that true Catholicism is based on a deep respect for each individual’s conscience — not a bishop’s demands — when making moral decisions. With only 25 days until voting concludes in Virginia, we need to stop the spread of misinformation and make sure Virginians know how important it is to vote Yes on 1. = = Thank you for being in this fight. Hey again,

$5 – does that sound doable?

I know my team and I ask a lot. We wish we didn’t have to.

But unfortunately, this is what comes with the territory of running a battleground Senate race like this. Especially with the polls showing a tight race with Jon Husted. Especially with the Senate GOP’s top super PAC spending more here than anywhere else.

The difficult reality is that these final 25 days will be our most challenging yet. We cannot take our foot off the gas. We cannot give Republicans an inch. We cannot take a single day off.

Peter,
**In just 25 days, Randy Villegas will be going up against Republican incumbent David Valadao in the midterms.**
This seat is absolutely **critical** to flip the House in November — and Randy is the best person to do it. Ballots are already being mailed out in California, and it’s critical that Randy has as much support as possible in this final stretch.
**[Split a $5 contribution between Randy’s campaign and Leaders We Deserve now to help get Randy over the finish line.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261009_1_randy.cUl14-&refcode=em20261009-4124&amount=5&t=2&akid=4124%2E587540%2E1qZirx)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261009_1_randy.cUl14-&amount=5&refcode=em20261009-4124&t=3&akid=4124%2E587540%2E1qZirx)**
CA-22 is one of the most competitive districts in the country. Flipping this seat is essential to flipping the House and fighting back against the Trump Administration’s reckless policies. Randy will not only stand up for his constituents in the Central Valley, but all working families across the country.
Randy’s opponent, David Valadao, is supported by AIPAC and various other corporate PACs. Under his leadership, prices in the Central Valley have continued to increase and he’s stood by while corporations buy up houses and price working families out of the market.
Randy is fighting for a future built by and for working people. He’s ready to deliver a lower cost of living, Medicare for All, and a fair tax system that holds billionaires and corporations accountable.
This is going to be a tight race. Trump won this district by only about 2% and in 2022 the Democratic candidate lost to Valadao by just 3,132 votes, out of the more than 102,000 cast. But that just makes the stakes even higher in these last few weeks leading up to Election Day. It will come down to how much grassroots support we can get behind his campaign to reach as many voters as possible in this final stretch.
**Randy has what it takes to win, Peter.** It’s a very close race — and we need to ensure a win in order to take back the House. Randy has the kind of fire and grassroots energy that makes people believe something better is actually possible, and in this critical moment, he needs a surge of grassroots support.
**[Will you split a $5 contribution between Randy’s campaign and Leaders We Deserve to help him win and flip the House next month?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261009_1_randy.cUl14-&refcode=em20261009-4124&amount=5&t=4&akid=4124%2E587540%2E1qZirx)**

David Hogg

Team, **Something remarkable is happening in Idaho.** In one of the reddest states in the country, a grassroots coalition of 1700 volunteers gathered signatures to put reproductive freedom on the ballot this November. Idahoans from every corner of the state came together to say politicians should not be making the most personal medical decisions for women and families. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141029506/652302620/-1911448607?refcode=AU_FLHP_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20261009_PM1_V1_S3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY0NjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2Y1YTVhNTYtZjBjMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=RD4FeknJBpGOc-neqmLjJjl6OxHELQv2dGG7kt4GVug=&emci=725a5a56-f0c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=7f5a5a56-f0c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1028753) That courage deserves our support. Idaho has one of the strictest abortion bans in the country, with no exception for the health of the mother. The consequences have been devastating: doctors leaving the state, pregnant patients being sent elsewhere for medically necessary care, and families forced to navigate heartbreaking decisions without the freedom, privacy, or dignity they deserve. But Idahoans are fighting back. **Idahoans United for Women & Families is leading the campaign to pass the _Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act,_** a ballot initiative that would restore access to abortion care up to fetal viability, protect access to birth control and fertility treatments like IVF, and keep private medical decisions between women, their families, and their doctors. Now they need help making sure voters hear the truth. **Anti-choice extremists are not going to sit this out.** They will spend whatever they can to protect Idaho’s current ban and stop this grassroots campaign in its tracks. [**So I’m asking you to join me in supporting Idahoans United for Women & Families today. 100% of your contribution to this email will go directly to their campaign to help reach voters, fight back against misinformation, and win this November. clean_body: Support Idahoans United for Women & Families today → | Team, Something remarkable is happening in Idaho. In one of the reddest states in the country, a grassroots coalition of 1700 volunteers gathered signatures to put reproductive freedom on the ballot this November. Idahoans from every corner of the state came together to say politicians should not be making the most personal medical decisions for women and families. That courage deserves our support. Idaho has one of the strictest abortion bans in the country, with no exception for the health of the mother. The consequences have been devastating: doctors leaving the state, pregnant patients being sent elsewhere for medically necessary care, and families forced to navigate heartbreaking decisions without the freedom, privacy, or dignity they deserve. But Idahoans are fighting back. Idahoans United for Women & Families is leading the campaign to pass the Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act, a ballot initiative that would restore access to abortion care up to fetal viability, protect access to birth control and fertility treatments like IVF, and keep private medical decisions between women, their families, and their doctors. Now they need help making sure voters hear the truth. Anti-choice extremists are not going to sit this out. They will spend whatever they can to protect Idaho’s current ban and stop this grassroots campaign in its tracks. | | Thank you for joining with Idahoans in this important fight, Gretchen Whitmer Fight Like Hell PAC PO BOX 15093 Lansing, MI 48901 United States ** | mailto:info@fightlikehellpac.org| | Paid for by Fight Like Hell PAC. |
Peter,
Earlier this week, it was revealed that the Trump admin is deploying nearly 1,000 armed guards from Prosegur, a private security firm accused of human rights abuses, to postal facilities across the country ahead of the November election.
The DOJ has already confirmed that they will deploy over one thousand "election monitors" to polling sites this November.
Now a video showing National Guard troops standing guard outside of a ballot drop-box in Washington, D.C. is going viral on social media.
---
---
| | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001SVXkioljnhCw_HQCH-5GjBxvLzgol86F2w_7qM2rj3q4odMNUlHfd96bWG6_T3wgUJ3S9FVVCFfbICd1CtR08soqn9_qga0IqRPF43ieH4UyWFarPcwfNJiBhUTpFV3Cyc4WDhf0RbEw4O6hkBu6fd-zDMDS1vjxEz2AtgtwfhEqi2ZaQPCN5-mkBX98sA88xNQe7ugbTbh0b2dpK6AWN8YqflLuKfmxgZ9_Tf--nl0=&c=VEiMMrM9aG4dd6zSUlqkZndI7T0sVn--wIwgo0reNF4fOcfGy8UMZg==&ch=6-3R6Pc2TQbaWKqI3lcvRWZe03p0oHK0My5l_38AHHlPo6NkghgaBQ==)

And this would not be the first time. In June, videos showed armed National Guard troops gathered around a ballot drop box in Washington, D.C., ahead of the city's primary. D.C. Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton demanded answers from the Guard, warning that troops stationed around ballot boxes create "the appearance of voter intimidation."
This latest report has not been confirmed yet. But if it is, it means Trump is now sending the National Guard, alongside DOJ monitors and armed private security guards, to intimidate voters and election workers.
Here is what you should do if you find yourself in a similar situation when voting this fall:
Walk right past them and cast your ballot.
Do not engage, do not be rude, and do not take the bait. Refuse to be intimidated and exercise your most important right as a citizen.
If anyone tries to stop you from voting, call the Democratic Party's voter protection hotline at 833-DEM-VOTE (833-336-8683) or the nonpartisan Election Protection hotline at 866-OUR-VOTE (866-687-8683).
Trump is betting these tactics will stop us from voting. We cannot, will not let him succeed. We must turn out in unprecedented numbers this November and leave no room for Trump's rigging plot to succeed. We will make this election too big to rig.
And our courts must hold. States run elections, not the feds. State Supreme Courts will be the first and last line of defense against Trump's election rigging plot.
This is exactly why Defend Our Courts exists. We're fighting Trump's election rigging plots on two fronts: building a firewall of state courts to protect elections and turning Dems out in battleground states with key House and Senate races.

name: NEGOP
subject: 🚨 Your Weekly Update From The NEGOP
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Nebraska Republican Party 1610 N St
body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair
---
| Friends,
In 2008, Al Franken won Minnesota's U.S. Senate seat by 312 votes. Out of nearly 2.9 million ballots cast, 312 votes decided it. That's fewer people than would fill a high school gym on a Friday night.
That seat gave DC Democrats their 60th vote. Months later, they used it to force Obamacare through the Senate without a single Republican vote. Every family that watched premiums climb and lost the plan they were promised they could keep lived with the result of 312 people who didn't bother to show up.
It can happen here. Too many Republicans believe Nebraska is so red that our vote doesn't matter. But our Second District electoral vote went to Kamala Harris in 2024, just as it went to Joe Biden in 2020 and Barack Obama in 2008. Every time, Republicans told themselves Nebraska was safe.
This November, the stakes are even higher.
Senator Pete Ricketts is facing Dan Osborn, the same "independent" who came within a few points of beating Senator Deb Fischer two years ago. Democrats are putting everything behind Osborn because they know a Nebraska seat could decide control of the U.S. Senate, just like Minnesota did.
Governor Jim Pillen is on the ballot: a businessman and family man who holds Nebraska's conservative values. He's facing a sweet-talking but big-spending liberal who has a record of advocating gender-mutilating surgery on children and keeping boys in girls' sports.
Don Bacon is retiring, leaving the Second District wide open. Our nominee, Brinker Harding, is facing Dark Money Denise Powell, who is heavily funded by the most radical elements of the Democratic Party from outside our state.
We have close races for control of our State Board of Education. There are Board of Regents races that will determine whether conservative, commonsense voices have a say in our cherished University of Nebraska system.
Many seats in our Legislature are up for election. In our Unicameral, it takes 33 votes to break a filibuster. Lose even one or two seats, and real property tax relief stalls. So do our efforts to rein in government spending, protect your Second Amendment rights, and keep parents in charge of their kids' education.
Lower on the ballot, but still important, are public power board seats, Natural Resources District seats, and other races that determine our utility rates and how we spend on Nebraska's land and water resources.
None of that is lost all at once. It slips away one seat, one skipped election at a time.
Make a plan to vote. In-person early voting is open now at your county election office, and mail ballot requests are due October 23. Then bring three people with you: a neighbor, a coworker, a family member.
312 votes changed the country. Yours can too.
Together we win!
In Liberty and in Truth,

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair | Friends, In 2008, Al Franken won Minnesota's U.S. Senate seat by 312 votes. Out of nearly 2.9 million ballots cast, 312 votes decided it. That's fewer people than would fill a high school gym on a Friday night. That seat gave DC Democrats their 60th vote. Months later, they used it to force Obamacare through the Senate without a single Republican vote. Every family that watched premiums climb and lost the plan they were promised they could keep lived with the result of 312 people who didn't bother to show up. It can happen here. Too many Republicans believe Nebraska is so red that our vote doesn't matter. But our Second District electoral vote went to Kamala Harris in 2024, just as it went to Joe Biden in 2020 and Barack Obama in 2008. Every time, Republicans told themselves Nebraska was safe. This November, the stakes are even higher. Senator Pete Ricketts is facing Dan Osborn, the same "independent" who came within a few points of beating Senator Deb Fischer two years ago. Democrats are putting everything behind Osborn because they know a Nebraska seat could decide control of the U.S. Senate, just like Minnesota did. Governor Jim Pillen is on the ballot: a businessman and family man who holds Nebraska's conservative values. He's facing a sweet-talking but big-spending liberal who has a record of advocating gender-mutilating surgery on children and keeping boys in girls' sports. Don Bacon is retiring, leaving the Second District wide open. Our nominee, Brinker Harding, is facing Dark Money Denise Powell, who is heavily funded by the most radical elements of the Democratic Party from outside our state. We have close races for control of our State Board of Education. There are Board of Regents races that will determine whether conservative, commonsense voices have a say in our cherished University of Nebraska system. Many seats in our Legislature are up for election. In our Unicameral, it takes 33 votes to break a filibuster. Lose even one or two seats, and real property tax relief stalls. So do our efforts to rein in government spending, protect your Second Amendment rights, and keep parents in charge of their kids' education. Lower on the ballot, but still important, are public power board seats, Natural Resources District seats, and other races that determine our utility rates and how we spend on Nebraska's land and water resources. None of that is lost all at once. It slips away one seat, one skipped election at a time. Make a plan to vote. In-person early voting is open now at your county election office, and mail ballot requests are due October 23. Then bring three people with you: a neighbor, a coworker, a family member. 312 votes changed the country. Yours can too. Together we win! # Palestine
* **Israeli attacks kill nine Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday and Friday:** Israeli forces killed at least nine Palestinians and wounded several others across the Gaza Strip on Thursday and Friday, according to WAFA.
* On Friday, Israeli troops [opened fire](https://substack.com/redirect/3342bc16-ae0d-48b8-b7d1-b4a9f83eb615?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Palestinians east of the Maghazi and Bureij refugee camps in central Gaza, killing one man who was shot in the neck and wounding others.
* On Thursday, eight Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks, including two men in a drone strike on a vehicle near the Jordanian field hospital in southwest Gaza City, a woman in artillery shelling northwest of the city, and two people, including a child, in a drone strike on a home in the Sabra neighborhood.
* **Israeli settlers carry out at least 19 attacks across the occupied West Bank, targeting olive harvesters and property:** Israeli settlers [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/7ba2c55b-83e2-4ceb-adfd-32048f0020b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 19 attacks across the occupied West Bank on Friday, assaulting olive harvesters, burning vehicles and trees, stealing livestock, and forcing farmers off their land, according to the Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. Israeli forces also fired live ammunition and tear gas at farmers, confiscated agricultural equipment, and conducted raids and arrests.
* **Nablus:** Settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/0729bc31-dd21-410a-b32c-f91b2cbdedff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olive harvesters across several villages, including Tal, Jamma'in, Qusra, Beita, Sebastia, Beit Furik, and Deir Sharaf, forcing farmers off their land. They burned a vehicle in Tal and uprooted more than 50 olive trees in Qusra, where Israeli soldiers fired tear gas and stun grenades, sparking fires.
* **Ramallah:** Settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/49782eea-7b06-48f3-9632-c90cff1358dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) farmers in Deir Sudan and Deir Ibzi, stealing crops and forcing them off their land. Armed settlers stole 20 sheep in Ein Qiniya under Israeli military protection, while a man and his child were assaulted and their vehicle stolen in Yabroud. Two people were injured in settler attacks in Deir Ibzi.
* **Salfit:** Israeli soldiers and settlers [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/516f3fc2-d672-403d-9245-6609c8a101a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) live ammunition to drive farmers from their land in Deir Ballut, while settlers injured a farmer in Kafr ad-Dik. Settlers also burned olive trees in Wadi Al-Shaer.
* **Hebron:** A 79-year-old woman was [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/806cff17-a43a-4357-9991-e5c6bc202db2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after settlers unleashed dogs on olive harvesters in Birin. Israeli forces confiscated a school transport vehicle, two tractors and animal feed in Masafer Yatta, and arrested nine Palestinians in Hebron, including the director of the Ibrahimi Mosque.
* **Jenin:** Settlers [cut down](https://substack.com/redirect/2c8e737f-d337-4df3-a893-101ef240e266?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 100 olive trees in Al-Mughayyir village overnight Thursday.
* **Palestinian Authority plans to postpone November elections until September 2027:** Palestinian Authority Vice President Hussein Al-Sheikh [informed](https://substack.com/redirect/632badd4-bbe9-4538-86f3-074319618204?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) France that legislative elections scheduled for November 28 will be postponed, potentially until September 2027, citing worsening political, security and economic conditions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, according to an October 8 letter seen by Reuters.
* The letter pointed to a number of causes for the postponement, including expectations of an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, the deployment of international forces and Palestinian police, curbs on Israeli annexation and settler violence, and the release of nearly $7 billion in Palestinian funds withheld by Israel, that had not materialized.
* Palestinians have not held legislative elections since 2006 or presidential elections since 2005, and Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas has ruled by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009. Hamas won a majority over Fatah in the January 2006 Palestinian parliamentary elections, prompting severe Israeli economic and military measures against the Hamas-led government.

* **Trump says U.S. will not attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterms** : President Donald Trump [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/ab01c091-13f7-406f-a6a1-419a412b80cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Truth Social Thursday that "we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd."

* **Putin tells Iran 's Pezeshkian Russia will "do everything" to help end the U.S.-led war: **Russian President Vladimir**** Putin [met](https://substack.com/redirect/2693cdf8-32c5-4c06-8875-f963a1b3d335?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan on Thursday, ahead of the Commonwealth of Independent States summit, and said, "On our part, we are ready to do everything we can to help you resolve this situation," according to the Interfax news service.
* The Russian president commended Iran for making "real efforts to end the conflict, which broke out through no fault of its own," and noted a "positive evolution" in Iran-Russia ties.
* On Wednesday, Putin told Pezeshkian in a call that Moscow is ready to mediate between the U.S. and Iran, Iran's IRNA reported.
* Pezeshkian said talks with the U.S. to end the war could succeed only if based on "mutual respect and reciprocal commitments" and free from "pressure and threats," speaking at the summit on Friday.
* **Iran 's IRGC strikes LPG tanker, threatens to target vessels beyond Strait of Hormuz: **Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) [said](https://substack.com/redirect/bec1748d-683a-40c4-9849-594ad2440fb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it struck a large LPG tanker named NV Sunshine attempting to transit an "illegal route" south of the Strait of Hormuz, causing a major fire in its engine room and propulsion system, according to Tasnim news agency.
* The IRGC subsequently warned that vessels using unauthorized routes would face "punitive measures" even outside the strait, threatening to pursue them "throughout the region" and warning against following "deception of the American aggressors."
* **At least 81 U.S. military aircraft lost or damaged in war against Iran, costing up to $3.3 billion:** At least 81 U.S. military aircraft were lost or damaged during Operation Epic Fury, Washington's military campaign against Iran launched on February 28, according to a Congressional Budget Office report.
* The report estimated losses of $1.9 billion to $3.3 billion as of August 1, including 12 F-15E fighter jets, one F-35A, seven KC-135 refueling aircraft and 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones.
* **U.S. sanctions 17 more vessels carrying Iranian oil:** The U.S. Treasury Department [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/54247f3e-64db-4655-be89-b53af61d93b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sanctions on 17 additional vessels linked to Iran's so-called "shadow fleet" as part of its "Operation Economic Outcast" campaign to cut Tehran's oil revenues amid the ongoing war.
* The vessels, registered across more than a dozen jurisdictions, have transported millions of barrels of Iranian crude and petroleum products, according to the Treasury.
* A U.S. official said Iran has stopped loading and unloading oil because of the American blockade of its ports, while shipping data firm Kpler reported no Iranian crude loaded for export since August 25.

* **ICE agent shoots and wounds man in New York City with 5-year-old in car:** An ICE agent [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/60ebff6b-20cc-4e08-a4ac-748472c277d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) seven rounds into a car around 4 p.m. Thursday in New York City's Marble Hill neighborhood, wounding **Oscar Belgal** , 28, in the neck below the left ear, according to New York City Police Commissioner **Jessica Tisch**. Mamdani also claimed that during a two hour call with President **Donald Trump** and Homeland Security Secretary **Markwayne Mullin** they refused to release Belgal, whom ICE took away in an unmarked vehicle. New York Governor **Kathy Hochul** said she urged Trump and Mullin to halt ICE operations in New York and asked that any body-camera footage be released.

Darializa Avila Chevalier [was on the frontlines of the protest and thrown to the ground](https://substack.com/redirect/a55773b0-1c07-406c-a2c0-732409a1ae99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Two days later, he signed a national space transportation policy calling for more than 1,000 launches and reentries a year by 2030. SpaceX is a major Pentagon contractor and NASA launch provider.

* **FBI deletes video attacking Democrats** : An FBI video [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/96273efb-1031-4ad0-ad2d-998a1cac915a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday on its rapid response X account labeled prominent Democrats, among them **Kamala Harris** , Reps. **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** and **Ilhan Omar** , former Rep.**Cori Bush** and Michigan Senate nominee **Abdul El-Sayed** , as part of "the DEFUND THE POLICE crowd," and accused them of seeking to "let criminals run wild while cops take a backseat." * On Thursday, rioters torched 14 vehicles in Durban and 10 in Johannesburg's Soweto township, and foreign-owned shops were looted. A months-long surge in anti-immigrant protests in South Africa has strained its relations with other African countries and forced thousands of foreign nationals to leave.
* **ICC judges rule Duterte fit to stand trial; trial opens Nov. 30:** International Criminal Court judges [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/b7ab7435-64ab-4529-bce5-2d8cc1356058?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a September 28 decision, announced Thursday, that former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, 81, is fit to stand trial on crimes against humanity charges tied to his drug war. An independent expert panel found he "has the capacity to understand the charges," follow proceedings, understand the evidence, and discuss his defense with lawyers. He will be asked to enter a plea when the trial opens November 30.

Drop Site Daily: October 9, 2026 | | | Oct 9 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- South African lawyer Navanethem "Navi" Pillay speaks at the Nuremberg Forum in Nuremberg following the announcement that she will be awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. Photo by Daniel Karmann/picture alliance via Getty Images. Friday, October 9, 2026 -** Palestine : Israeli attacks kill nine Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday and Friday. Israeli settlers carry out at least 19 attacks across the occupied West Bank, targeting olive harvesters and property. Palestinian Authority plans to postpone November elections until September 2027. Nearly 22,000 Palestinian children killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza over three years, with more than 71,000 orphaned. Israeli military actions linked to deaths of at least 24 captives in Gaza, CNN investigation finds. Colombia to open Israel embassy in Jerusalem next week. Yemen : Three killed in Ansarallah attacks on Saudi airport. Saudi-led coalition destroys three Ansarallah missile launchers as airstrikes reported in Sana'a. Iran : President Donald Trump says U.S. will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms. Russian President Vladimir Putin tells Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian Russia will "do everything" to help end the U.S.-led war. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps strikes LPG tanker, threatens to target vessels beyond Strait of Hormuz. At least 81 U.S. military aircraft lost or damaged in war against Iran, costing up to $3.3 billion. U.S. sanctions 17 more vessels carrying Iranian oil. Lebanon: Israeli forces uproot olive trees in southern Lebanon amid airstrikes and artillery shelling. U.S. : ICE agent shoots and wounds man in New York City with 5-year-old in car. Trump disclosed 517 securities trades in August, including up to $25 million in Meta and SpaceX debt bought two days before a space policy signing. Pentagon to livestream firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter. FBI deletes video attacking Democrats. Trump administration suspends Microsoft, seven other firms from green card program, alleging fraud. Michigan Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers leaves door open to AIPAC support in Michigan Senate race. International: Navi Pillay, who led UN inquiry finding Israel committed genocide in Gaza, wins Nobel Peace Prize. Ukrainian strikes kill two in Russia's Belgorod; Russian bombs kill one in Zaporizhzhia. No survivors from sunken ship off Bulgaria. Ethiopia tells UN Security Council it will defend itself against Eritrean "all-out invasion." Drone strikes hit Eritrean forces inside northern Ethiopia, conflict monitor says. Brazilian justice issues arrest warrant for Eduardo Bolsonaro weeks before runoff. France pledges 3,000 extra teachers as student protests continue; stun grenades banned from marches. Prison fight in Sinaloa kills 10, including a minor. U.S. judge orders Trump administration to facilitate return of Egyptian man deported to Equatorial Guinea. UN Security Council extends Sudan sanctions by two months. South Africa withdraws asylum intake directive after anti-migrant protests turn violent. International Criminal Court judges rule former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte fit to stand trial; trial opens November 30. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Israeli attacks kill nine Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday and Friday: Israeli forces killed at least nine Palestinians and wounded several others across the Gaza Strip on Thursday and Friday, according to WAFA. On Friday, Israeli troops on Palestinians east of the Maghazi and Bureij refugee camps in central Gaza, killing one man who was shot in the neck and wounding others. On Thursday, eight Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks, including two men in a drone strike on a vehicle near the Jordanian field hospital in southwest Gaza City, a woman in artillery shelling northwest of the city, and two people, including a child, in a drone strike on a home in the Sabra neighborhood. Israeli settlers carry out at least 19 attacks across the occupied West Bank, targeting olive harvesters and property: Israeli settlers at least 19 attacks across the occupied West Bank on Friday, assaulting olive harvesters, burning vehicles and trees, stealing livestock, and forcing farmers off their land, according to the Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. Israeli forces also fired live ammunition and tear gas at farmers, confiscated agricultural equipment, and conducted raids and arrests. Nablus: Settlers olive harvesters across several villages, including Tal, Jamma'in, Qusra, Beita, Sebastia, Beit Furik, and Deir Sharaf, forcing farmers off their land. They burned a vehicle in Tal and uprooted more than 50 olive trees in Qusra, where Israeli soldiers fired tear gas and stun grenades, sparking fires. Ramallah: Settlers farmers in Deir Sudan and Deir Ibzi, stealing crops and forcing them off their land. Armed settlers stole 20 sheep in Ein Qiniya under Israeli military protection, while a man and his child were assaulted and their vehicle stolen in Yabroud. Two people were injured in settler attacks in Deir Ibzi. Salfit: Israeli soldiers and settlers live ammunition to drive farmers from their land in Deir Ballut, while settlers injured a farmer in Kafr ad-Dik. Settlers also burned olive trees in Wadi Al-Shaer. Hebron: A 79-year-old woman was after settlers unleashed dogs on olive harvesters in Birin. Israeli forces confiscated a school transport vehicle, two tractors and animal feed in Masafer Yatta, and arrested nine Palestinians in Hebron, including the director of the Ibrahimi Mosque. Jenin: Settlers 100 olive trees in Al-Mughayyir village overnight Thursday. Palestinian Authority plans to postpone November elections until September 2027: Palestinian Authority Vice President Hussein Al-Sheikh France that legislative elections scheduled for November 28 will be postponed, potentially until September 2027, citing worsening political, security and economic conditions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, according to an October 8 letter seen by Reuters. The letter pointed to a number of causes for the postponement, including expectations of an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, the deployment of international forces and Palestinian police, curbs on Israeli annexation and settler violence, and the release of nearly $7 billion in Palestinian funds withheld by Israel, that had not materialized. Palestinians have not held legislative elections since 2006 or presidential elections since 2005, and Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas has ruled by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009. Hamas won a majority over Fatah in the January 2006 Palestinian parliamentary elections, prompting severe Israeli economic and military measures against the Hamas-led government. Nearly 22,000 Palestinian children killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza over three years, with more than 71,000 orphaned: Israeli attacks killed at least 21,976 Palestinian children in Gaza over the past three years, an average of one child every 71 minutes, according to a report by Gaza's Health Ministry. Among those killed were 5,444 children under five and 1,125 infants under one year old. Another 45,569 children have been injured, including 1,134 who have undergone amputations, while 71,846 have been orphaned. The ministry also reported 612 children killed while seeking food or medicine, 466 deaths from malnutrition, including 157 children, and 2,027 patients who died while awaiting medical evacuation, including 264 children. The report found that all 38 hospitals and 158 primary healthcare centers in Gaza have been targeted, with 19 hospitals and 64 healthcare centers out of service. It also documented 1,723 healthcare workers killed and 216 ambulances targeted. Israeli military actions linked to deaths of at least 24 captives in Gaza, CNN investigation finds: At least 24 of the 40 Israeli captives who died in captivity in Gaza had , including airstrikes and ground operations, as well as military advances that prompted their captors to kill them, a CNN investigation found. At least 11 were killed directly by Israeli military operations. The investigation, based on interviews with captive families and Israeli officials, also found that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu repeatedly delayed ceasefire negotiations, including a potential deal in July 2024 that officials said could have saved lives. Colombia to open Israel embassy in Jerusalem next week: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar Thursday that Colombia will inaugurate its embassy to Israel in Jerusalem "next Wednesday," as he touted expanding ties with Latin America. A Colombian Foreign Ministry official told AFP that Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar will travel to Jerusalem on Sunday ahead of the opening. Abelardo De la Espriella, Colombia's new right-wing president, promised close relations with Israel during his campaign. Once elected, he restored diplomatic ties with Israel that left-wing President Gustavo Petro had severed as a result of Israel's genocide in Gaza. Israel occupied East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in 1980 in a move largely unrecognized internationally, claiming the entire city as its capital, while Palestinians seek Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state. Yemen Three killed in Ansarallah attacks on Saudi airport: Three Saudi citizens were killed and several others injured in two Ansarallah on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday, according to Saudi Arabia's Civil Aviation Authority. One attack targeted airport facilities, while the other struck a Saudi Airlines aircraft on the ground, killing an airline employee and damaging the plane, which had no passengers aboard. Hundreds of flights to Riyadh were cancelled, though flight cancellations fell from 335 on Thursday to at least 103 on Friday as the airport worked to restore normal operations. The EU Aviation Safety Agency also expanded its warning against flying over parts of Saudi Arabia, citing Ansarallah' demonstrated ability to strike targets deeper inside the kingdom, including Riyadh. Saudi-led coalition destroys three Ansarallah missile launchers as airstrikes reported in Sana 'a: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed three missile launch platforms used by Ansarallah, releasing of the strikes. Separately, Ansarallah-affiliated Al-Masira airstrikes on Yemen's capital, Sana'a, without immediately providing details on casualties or damage. Iran Trump says U.S. will not attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterms : President Donald Trump on Truth Social Thursday that "we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd." He justified this further in the post by claiming that Iran is "in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily." He has repeatedly tied the war to the midterms, saying he believes Iran's leaders are trying to hold out through November to hurt Republicans, and that he expects to win the war after the vote. Putin tells Iran 's Pezeshkian Russia will "do everything" to help end the U.S.-led war: Russian President Vladimir** Putin Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan on Thursday, ahead of the Commonwealth of Independent States summit, and said, "On our part, we are ready to do everything we can to help you resolve this situation," according to the Interfax news service. The Russian president commended Iran for making "real efforts to end the conflict, which broke out through no fault of its own," and noted a "positive evolution" in Iran-Russia ties. On Wednesday, Putin told Pezeshkian in a call that Moscow is ready to mediate between the U.S. and Iran, Iran's IRNA reported. Pezeshkian said talks with the U.S. to end the war could succeed only if based on "mutual respect and reciprocal commitments" and free from "pressure and threats," speaking at the summit on Friday. Iran 's IRGC strikes LPG tanker, threatens to target vessels beyond Strait of Hormuz: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) it struck a large LPG tanker named NV Sunshine attempting to transit an "illegal route" south of the Strait of Hormuz, causing a major fire in its engine room and propulsion system, according to Tasnim news agency. The IRGC subsequently warned that vessels using unauthorized routes would face "punitive measures" even outside the strait, threatening to pursue them "throughout the region" and warning against following "deception of the American aggressors." At least 81 U.S. military aircraft lost or damaged in war against Iran, costing up to $3.3 billion: At least 81 U.S. military aircraft were lost or damaged during Operation Epic Fury, Washington's military campaign against Iran launched on February 28, according to a Congressional Budget Office report. The report estimated losses of $1.9 billion to $3.3 billion as of August 1, including 12 F-15E fighter jets, one F-35A, seven KC-135 refueling aircraft and 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones. U.S. sanctions 17 more vessels carrying Iranian oil: The U.S. Treasury Department sanctions on 17 additional vessels linked to Iran's so-called "shadow fleet" as part of its "Operation Economic Outcast" campaign to cut Tehran's oil revenues amid the ongoing war. The vessels, registered across more than a dozen jurisdictions, have transported millions of barrels of Iranian crude and petroleum products, according to the Treasury. A U.S. official said Iran has stopped loading and unloading oil because of the American blockade of its ports, while shipping data firm Kpler reported no Iranian crude loaded for export since August 25. Lebanon Israeli forces uproot olive trees in southern Lebanon amid airstrikes and artillery shelling: Nabatieh: Israeli infantry accompanied by a D9 bulldozer advanced to within 50 meters of a Lebanese army position in Zawtar Al-Gharbiyeh, continuing to in an operation that began Thursday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli warplanes also struck the outskirts of Kfar Tebnit, following overnight shelling near Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, Kfar Tebnit and Mayfadoun. Marjayoun: An Israeli Merkava tank advanced from Khiam toward the Ibl al-Saqi spring, with Israeli forces firing machine guns toward the surrounding area. Artillery also struck Wadi Al-Salouqi. Tyre (Sour): Israeli forces shelled Mansouri, Majdal Zoun and surrounding valleys overnight. Bint Jbeil: Israeli shelling Wadi Zibqin and areas near Baraachit and Hadatha. U.S. News ICE agent shoots and wounds man in New York City with 5-year-old in car: An ICE agent seven rounds into a car around 4 p.m. Thursday in New York City's Marble Hill neighborhood, wounding Oscar Belgal , 28, in the neck below the left ear, according to New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch. A 5-year-old boy believed to be his son was in the back seat and was not injured. Surveillance video of the incident showed a plainclothes officer approaching the driver's window with his gun drawn before the car began to move, Tisch noted. DHS said agents were trying to arrest an undocumented Dominican immigrant with a grand larceny conviction, but did not name Belgal, explain why the agent fired, or whether the agent knew a child was in the car. The New York City Police Department said its officers were not involved. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the shooting "an outrage," saying "there is no justification for what we have seen today." Mamdani also claimed that during a two hour call with President Donald Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin they refused to release Belgal, whom ICE took away in an unmarked vehicle. New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she urged Trump and Mullin to halt ICE operations in New York and asked that any body-camera footage be released. Protesters gathered at the scene and outside Allen Hospital, where officers scuffled with them and at least one person was detained. Incoming Rep. Darializa Avila Chevalier . Immigration agents have shot at least two dozen people across the country since January 2025, killing six, including three U.S. citizens. Trump disclosed 517 securities trades in August, including up to $25 million in Meta and SpaceX debt bought two days before a space policy signing: Trump's August financial disclosure 517 purchases and sales totaling roughly $74.3 million to $273.3 million, according to a CNBC analysis, with purchases of at least $44.2 million and sales of at least $30.1 million. The largest was an August 21 purchase of $5 million to $25 million in Meta stock. On August 18, Trump's accounts bought $1 million to $5 million in senior unsecured SpaceX notes at 5.35 percent, maturing in 2031. Two days later, he signed a national space transportation policy calling for more than 1,000 launches and reentries a year by 2030. SpaceX is a major Pentagon contractor and NASA launch provider. On August 26, his portfolio bought $15,001 to $50,000 of Tyson Foods the same day he signed a proclamation expanding low-tariff imports of lean beef trimmings. The disclosure does not show whether the trade came before or after the signing. Trump's 2025 annual disclosure showed more than 21,000 trades across eight accounts holding at least $858 million, which contrasts starkly with the 86 stock transactions he made during the first year of his first term, in 2017. Pentagon to livestream firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter: War Secretary Pete Hegseth Real America's Voice on Thursday that Nidal Hasan , convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, "is gonna get a firing squad of soldiers. As it should be." He added, "We'll make sure that people are able to watch it. That it's public. Because people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things." Hasan is scheduled to be executed December 3 at Fort Hood. The Pentagon later released a statement confirming that the execution will be livestreamed. The U.S. hasn't held a public execution since 1936, when Rainey Bethea was hanged in Kentucky. It would be the first US military execution since 1961. The last military firing-squad execution was in 1945. FBI deletes video attacking Democrats : An FBI video Tuesday on its rapid response X account labeled prominent Democrats, among them Kamala Harris , Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Ilhan Omar , former Rep.Cori Bush and Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed , as part of "the DEFUND THE POLICE crowd," and accused them of seeking to "let criminals run wild while cops take a backseat." The FBI has since deleted the post and did not respond to a request for comment. Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) filed a complaint with the Office of Special Counsel, which investigates violations of the Hatch Act, which limits the partisan political activities of federal executive branch employees (excluding the President). CREW CEO Donald Sherman said in an X post on Thursday that although the video does not tell viewers how to vote, its message that the candidates' policies "failed" is "advocacy against their election." He added that tagging El-Sayed as "Progressive Democrat, Senate Nominee" "clearly invokes the election." Trump administration suspends Microsoft, seven other firms from green card program, alleging fraud : Vice President JD Vance Thursday that the administration is suspending Microsoft, Adobe and tech consulting firms Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini from the H-1B visa program that allows foreign workers to apply for green cards. Vance accused the firms of hiding the job offers they are required to first publicly announce in the U.S. in "small town newspapers." He also claimed that Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers last year while obtaining 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards. Microsoft said about 80 percent of its roughly 6,000 H-1B filings last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of existing employees, and that the rest were for people already legally in the U.S. Vance also singled out nine universities for investigation over J-1 visa use: Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Brown, Pittsburgh, UC Davis, Caltech, Arizona State and MIT. MIT, Brown and Pitt said they had received subpoenas related to this investigation. The announcement came hours before Trump awarded the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Rogers leaves door open to AIPAC support in Michigan Senate race : Michigan GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers at a Thursday debate that he would accept AIPAC's backing against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed , saying "anybody that wants to help my campaign stop" El-Sayed, "I'll take all of that help." AIPAC's super PAC, United Democracy Project, spent more than $30 million against El-Sayed in the Michigan Democratic primary. AdImpact data show the group does not appear to have bought TV ads since. An August Axios report said Rogers' allies had asked AIPAC not to advertise for him, and that the group scrapped an anti-El-Sayed video a day after Rogers spoke with AIPAC board Chair Michael Tuchin. Rogers believed, according to Axios, that the group might be a liability to him in the general election, though around the time of his initial rupture with the group, he reportedly attended AIPAC-hosted fundraisers in California in August. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Ukrainian strikes kill two in Russia 's Belgorod; Russian bombs kill one in Zaporizhzhia: A Ukrainian strike two people and injured four, including a child, in the Russian border region of Belgorod on Friday, the Russian news agency TASS reported. A separate drone attack on the central region of Kaluga injured nine. In Ukraine, Russian bombs reportedly killed one person and injured seven, including a child, in Zaporizhzhia, according to the region's governor. No survivors from sunken ship off Bulgaria: Bulgarian authorities said they had found no survivors from the recently sunken Alfa Watan ship, one of two commercial vessels sunk by a drone in the Black Sea on Tuesday. Both of the sunken ships were managed by Turkey-based companies, according to Equasis. A Syrian customs official AFP on Thursday nine of the ten missing crew members on the recently sunken Alfa Watan were Syrians and the tenth was Egyptian. Navi Pillay, who led UN inquiry finding Israel committed genocide in Gaza, wins Nobel Peace Prize: South African jurist Navi Pillay, 85, was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday as "as a driving force in the development of an international system of law and order." A former UN human rights chief, ICC judge and anti-apartheid advocate, Pillay chaired the UN inquiry that concluded last year that Israel committed genocide in Gaza. Pillay learned of the award at a legal conference in Nuremberg, Germany, where Nazi leaders were tried after World War II. "The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what's happening there as genocide," she . In response to the award, Israel's Foreign Ministry Pillay of spreading "lies, hatred, and blood libels" and promoting what it called the "genoLIE." "Now that the Nobel commission has rewarded the biggest lie of the 21st century, Joseph Goebbels is certainly applauding from hell," it added, invoking the Nazi propaganda minister. Ethiopia tells UN Security Council it will defend itself against Eritrean "all-out invasion": Ethiopia in a letter to the UN Security Council that it has no option but to defend itself against what it described as an "all out invasion" by Eritrea, in its first official statement on reported Eritrean incursions earlier this week, according to Reuters. Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos wrote that Eritrean forces, "including mechanized units," have deployed up to 60 km (37 miles) into northern Ethiopia. He called the Eritrean incursions a "matter of public record" and "a blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia's inherent right to self-defense." Witnesses told Reuters this week they saw Eritrean soldiers in northern Ethiopia, days after the two countries severed diplomatic ties. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing a rebel alliance fighting federal troops since September 23 in Tigray, Amhara and Afar. Drone strikes hit Eritrean forces inside northern Ethiopia, conflict monitor says : Drone strikes, believed to have been carried out by Ethiopia's military, Eritrean military vehicles near Adigrat as they withdrew from positions in Tigray on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the U.S.-based conflict monitor ACLED. Eritrean soldiers crossed into Ethiopia on Wednesday, advanced dozens of kilometers, then pulled back under heavy bombardment, the conflict monitor added. Two sources, a diplomat and a conflict expert in contact with both sides, reported that Eritrean forces were moving north but said it was unclear whether they were leaving Ethiopia or redeploying within it. Brazilian justice issues arrest warrant for Eduardo Bolsonaro weeks before runoff : Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes an arrest warrant Thursday for Eduardo Bolsonaro, brother of presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, ordering him to begin serving a four-year sentence immediately. Moraes cancelled Bolsonaro's passport and told federal police to arrest him should he return from Texas, where he currently resides, The Supreme Court convicted Eduardo in June of lobbying the U.S. to interfere in the trial of his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, alleging that he lobbied for the U.S. to impose sanctions on Brazilian officials and tariffs on Brazilian exports. Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced in September 2025 to 27 years for plotting a coup, in an investigation chaired by de Moraes, whom the Bolsonaro family regards as a political enemy. The presidential election runoff between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro is set for October 25. France pledges 3,000 extra teachers as student protests continue; stun grenades banned from marches: French Education Minister Edouard Geffray on Thursday that 3,000 teachers would be sent to high-priority schools by Tuesday, with a "few hundred more" to be recruited, after weeks of mass protests that have gripped the country. Nearly 71,500 people protested across France on Thursday, with 24,500 protesters reported in Paris alone, France's Interior Ministry said. More than 500 people were arrested. Economy Minister Roland Lescure added, following the 1.4% increase in money allocated for education in France's 2027 budget, that there was "room" to meet the demands of the protesters for more resources. The protests began September 21 at a school in a deprived Paris area. Initiated by high school students, the demonstrations have grown to include university students and trade unions. Demands have included more teachers, renovated buildings and fewer classroom hours. Police have been accused of using excessive force, with the use of stun grenades being banned after a teenager lost his hand to a police stun grenade earlier this week. Prison fight in Sinaloa kills 10, including a minor: A fight inside the El Castillo Penitentiary Centre in Mazatlan, Sinaloa, nine prisoners and a family visitor dead and 16 prisoners injured, state authorities said Thursday. A state official also added that the family visitor killed in the fight was a minor. Mexican security forces reportedly moved into the prison, and officials report that the prison is now "under control." Sinaloa is a battleground for warring factions of the Sinaloa drug cartel, and the State Department advises Americans not to visit it. Officials have not said whether the violence was linked to that conflict. U.S. judge orders Trump administration to facilitate return of Egyptian man deported to Equatorial Guinea : U.S. District Judge John C. Hinderaker Thursday that the Department of Homeland Security must facilitate the release of Ahmed Soliman from custody in Equatorial Guinea and his return to the U.S., Reuters reported. Soliman was deported to the central African country this year under a third-country deportation deal. Last month he said Equatorial Guinean police treated him roughly, and video obtained by Reuters showed officers pulling firearms on migrants, including him. After Reuters published this story, he was taken into custody and has been held incommunicado at a gendarmerie station. Soliman told an immigration judge last year he feared being killed in Egypt because he is gay. Reuters has documented 40 cases of migrants granted U.S. protection over persecution for their LGBT status who were deported to African countries that criminalize same-sex relations or have been described by the State Department as hostile to LGBT people. UN Security Council extends Sudan sanctions by two months: The Security Council unanimously on Thursday to extend sanctions on arms sales to warring factions in Darfur until December 11, 2026, after the United States withdrew a draft that would have broadened the scope of the sanctions to cover the whole of Sudan and all of its warring parties. Several member states reportedly wanted a standard one-year renewal of the Darfur embargo, which date back to 2005, without changes. Russia, which holds a veto, notably opposed the U.S. proposal to widen the sanctions regime. South Africa withdraws asylum intake directive after anti-migrant protests turn violent: South Africa's Home Affairs Department Friday it had withdrawn a directive allowing it to resume processing asylum applications, a day after anti-migrant protests turned violent in Johannesburg and Durban. The directive would have implemented a July 7 Constitutional Court ruling that found that asylum seekers could not be denied access to the system solely on "procedural grounds," meaning primarily that those who had entered the country illegally would not be automatically disqualified from asylum. The department said the proposed directive was withdrawn after the number of asylum applications overwhelmed refugee reception offices within days of its announcement, putting officials at risk and threatening public safety and order On Thursday, rioters torched 14 vehicles in Durban and 10 in Johannesburg's Soweto township, and foreign-owned shops were looted. A months-long surge in anti-immigrant protests in South Africa has strained its relations with other African countries and forced thousands of foreign nationals to leave. ICC judges rule Duterte fit to stand trial; trial opens Nov. 30: International Criminal Court judges in a September 28 decision, announced Thursday, that former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, 81, is fit to stand trial on crimes against humanity charges tied to his drug war. An independent expert panel found he "has the capacity to understand the charges," follow proceedings, understand the evidence, and discuss his defense with lawyers. name: Office of the Governor
subject: 📬 Newsletter Exclusive Inside
body:
Plus: a $3.7B deal that'll support around 14K jobs
---
| | | | |
---
| My fellow Marylanders, We're moving Maryland forward on the issues that matter most to our people, including **building more housing, fighting for Maryland families, and strengthening our state’s economy.** Here’s how we've been taking on the housing crisis: I’ve signed two executive orders to [cut red tape, speed up permits, and make it easier to build homes](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv=UxQzQYfjVxg/1/010001a12141a71c-0c895b63-ba06-4126-bf77-106c82cff7ee-000000/MbJaiUcvY35kLnFMNqsRAM48ER3IcFsdcmHZJuvS6zI=452), and we announced $17.6 million to create or preserve hundreds of affordable rental homes in seven counties and Baltimore City. We also announced a record $32 million through our ENOUGH Initiative to **fight child poverty** in communities across the state. In Frederick alone, this work has brought free vision screenings to over 1,000 students and set up almost 100 mobile produce markets for local families. In the face of the Trump-Vance Administration’s continued threats to benefits that families depend on, we’ve helped nearly [40,000 Marylanders maintain their access to SNAP](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress-releases%2Fgovernor-moore-reinforces-commitment-keep-marylanders%23:~:text=DHS%2520estimates%2520that,their%2520nutrition%2520benefits./1/010001a12141a71c-0c895b63-ba06-4126-bf77-106c82cff7ee-000000/weriKMHwoHpBX1fzhEaJZTLgltmuLxWvorHBafjqAy0=452). Maryland now ranks among the top 10 states for helping families on SNAP keep their nutrition benefits. And for the third year in a row, our **SUN Bucks program has helped feed more than 600,000 students this summer.** And [we just closed a deal with Anduril Industries](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv=f-nsWaH-cKE/1/010001a12141a71c-0c895b63-ba06-4126-bf77-106c82cff7ee-000000/z9JFHn7kw9MoCOwBKwtsIrEghAuEaxQHixzJyM8-kjU=452) to expand Maryland’s manufacturing industry. This deal will drive **$3.7 BILLION in private investment** and **support around 14,000 jobs** , making it the largest private investment our state’s seen in over a decade. This major win builds on the multiple new business expansions we’ve seen over just the last few weeks. Thank you for your continued support and all you do to make this state a stronger, safer, and better place for those around you. Your Governor,
Wes Moore

The steepest rise is in states with bans. | | | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/141036524/652322197/2141984067?sourceid=1151673&utm_campaign=27emcus-1001aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=repromatters&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NDJiMDU1OS1mNmMzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NSsOusMF7MrEFKSknAV_rKwM3Ilxrvo2mihNNQs-K90=&emci=3768093c-41c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=542b0559-f6c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=954237)

# ReproMatters

---|---
| Peter—

Kyleigh Thurman and Kelsie Norris-De La Cruz almost died because hospitals in Texas denied them care for ectopic pregnancies, and both suffered permanent damage to their reproductive organs. An ectopic pregnancy cannot survive, and the woman can die without emergency abortion care. But because of abortion bans, doctors have delayed care and even [turned away patients](https://click.everyaction.com/k/141036526/652322198/-1225299304?sourceid=1151673&utm_campaign=27emcus-1001aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=repromatters&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NDJiMDU1OS1mNmMzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NSsOusMF7MrEFKSknAV_rKwM3Ilxrvo2mihNNQs-K90=&emci=3768093c-41c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=542b0559-f6c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=954237) facing these life-threatening pregnancies, out of fear of prosecution.

Kyleigh and Kelsie survived their harrowing ordeals, but many women do not. A new [analysis](https://click.everyaction.com/k/141036527/652322199/1291451188?sourceid=1151673&utm_campaign=27emcus-1001aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=repromatters&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NDJiMDU1OS1mNmMzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NSsOusMF7MrEFKSknAV_rKwM3Ilxrvo2mihNNQs-K90=&emci=3768093c-41c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=542b0559-f6c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=954237) from ProPublica found the number of women dying due to ectopic pregnancies nearly doubled from 2020 to 2025 — and the spike is steepest in states that ban abortion. Ectopic pregnancies, in which the fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, are the leading cause of maternal death in the first trimester and require immediate treatment. In Texas, nearly 30% more patients experienced substantial blood loss following ectopic pregnancies in 2023 and 2024 than in 2018 and 2019.

These sobering numbers show just how dangerous abortion bans are and the devastating toll they are taking on women's health and lives.

The Center took legal action to hold the hospitals accountable for turning Kyleigh and Kelsie away, and we are fighting to ensure that people who experience ectopic pregnancy and other dangerous or life-threatening pregnancy complications are not denied the care they need. Through litigation in Texas, Idaho, and Tennessee, we're working to expand doctors' ability to provide emergency abortion care despite the states' abortion bans, and we're using a federal law to hold hospitals accountable for failing to provide care to patients who are endangered by pregnancy complications.

The Repro Rights Team
