Dear Friend, Politics today isn't Red versus Blue. It's the Swamp versus the Freedom Caucus. This week, Republicans in Illinois and South Dakota endorsed Democrats over conservative Freedom Caucus members, while the Daily Signal highlighted how our state caucuses are cutting budgets, exposing the establishment, and building a conservative majority in state capitols across the country.
---
|
---
**THE DAILY SIGNAL TAKES NOTICE** The _Daily Signal_ recently ran [a feature](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTju6jPLv4q1N-2FySkqtD2z7Uxrh63xD7sO0eOdSTBq-2BJqIElSm0k8K-2BOvfFszLK-2F7RXx4S00GXIt7AWhjookQebhwgapXgcnnN3tIufS3iEKSDYSBU_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerF1GYi3bczgJxmJEeQEn7O72sRH2kABrSaStWdITFK-2BDt2eJCgNu94aRfmw-2BKP1JjDWR3FtgThbWW1hRqi-2BXrdMy7hK1MGkIQbL09Sn3BvVwFoipCqKcsJUH7FOdFc00SyuhDhhShQCCLWT7qSszJBRC02T0GuVFPR5UMmw8RnNLsNR3RRLFsoZ0Oe7cCPpbgmfE2XIqsCBO1U1FNz2L08DAaquuQO6LSFnP2-2FWFhwqE-3D) on the State Freedom Caucus Network, and its headline says it well: we are the network of conservatives working for freedom in your state capital. Reporter Virginia Grace McKinnon laid out what supporters like you have built. We now have 180 lawmakers in 15 states, all working to cut spending, secure elections, and push state legislatures further to the right. The results she highlighted are concrete. Thanks to the Missouri Freedom Caucus, the Legislature cut its budget by nearly $4 billion, and it's now lower than it was two years ago. Wyoming and South Dakota have held their budgets as flat as they were two years ago.As I told the Daily Signal, "Imagine if Congress had that sort of fiscal discipline." The article also names the biggest obstacle we face, and it's not Democrats. It's Republicans in name only. As I put it, Democrats in red states know they can't win with a "D" after their name, so they put an "R" after it, get elected, and vote like Democrats. That's exactly why we build caucuses: to expose it, and to help our members be vocal about what's happening in their capitols. Read the whole thing [here](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTju6jPLv4q1N-2FySkqtD2z7Uxrh63xD7sO0eOdSTBq-2BJqIElSm0k8K-2BOvfFszLK-2F7RXx4S00GXIt7AWhjookQebhwgapXgcnnN3tIufS3iEKSDVF2j_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerF1GYi3bczgJxmJEeQEn7O72sRH2kABrSaStWdITFK-2BDt2eJCgNu94aRfmw-2BKP1JjDWR3FtgThbWW1hRqi-2BXrdMy7hK1MGkIQbL09Sn3BvVxKvE5BBtWszuwslGCp9w6-2FLFXvPvEnlI79NdAtewswNRqyPGjfjYWqXc1Ep-2F1mDMQCY3i1YU0fVxuQq00b3kKN67xdbWT3AySoK4wcvFuqhlRj1sDSRD5Q7-2BLZWCpt3nU-3D).

**GOP LEADERS ARE ENDORSING DEMOCRATS** As I pointed out in the Daily Signal article, Democrats often hide their true identity by putting an "R" after their name. Here are two recent examples: In Illinois, former House GOP Leader Jim Durkin endorsed Democrat Gov. JB Pritzker over Republican Darren Bailey. The **Illinois Freedom Caucus** called Durkin "a disgrace to the Republican Party." They pointed to his votes for gun control, the semi-auto rifle ban, and tax increases, and to the double-digit House seat losses under his leadership. ILFC member Rep. Adam Niemerg put it plainly: "The problem is not Trump or conservatives! It's Republicans who endorse the most woke progressive policies." In South Dakota, "Republican" Secretary of State Monae Johnson endorsed the Democrat against **SD Freedom Caucus member Rep. Heather Baxter** , the Republican nominee for Secretary of State. Baxter beat Johnson at the GOP convention. SDFC Vice Chair Sen. John Carley went on OANN to call this out and laid out what Baxter would protect: the SAVE SD Act, paper ballots, and no statewide vote centers. We are going to lose this country if we allow these fake Republicans to successfully defeat conservatives by siding with the Left.State Freedom Caucuses are exposing it and helping voters see the real divide.

| | This is the fight for your children’s future. The next two years of YOUR child’s life are on the ballot on November 3, 2026. Two parties. Completely different priorities. Who controls Congress decides which issues get hearings, votes, and become law — parental rights, girls’ sports, education, border security, free speech, the right to raise your kids according to your values, and whether the American Dream still belongs to families like yours. You cannot sit this one out.
---
| | | [**Check your Voter Status**](https://momsforamerica.us/so/83Q4XJQbj/c?w=iJRor0n1PU1p1Gyzcns5jLdN1LkVzA6Dk_O_oMOf9qU.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubW9tc2ZvcmFtZXJpY2EudXMvIiwiciI6IjA4NmUwYzJjLWY2NjUtNGIxOS1iN2RlLTVkOWQzMTQ2ZGIyMiIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6ImIzODM4YmY4LWZhYjAtNDFiOS05NjczLWU4YzZiZWZiNjU3NyJ9)
---
| | Your vote is your voice. Your voice is the only thing standing between the America you want for your kids and the one that is being pushed on them.
* Vote early if you can.
* Make a plan. Take someone with you.
* Confirm your registration.
* Cast an informed vote that protects the freedoms, the innocence, and the future of every child you love.

This is not about one candidate. This is about the parental authority, biological reality in sports, the right to speak without being silenced, the right to raise your children without fear, and the country our veterans fought and died for. Election Day is November 3, 2026. The window is open now. Do not wait. Do not assume someone else will carry the load. Moms who show up decide the next chapter. Your children are counting on you.Please Vote. Vote early. Make your voice heard. Encourage others. We cannot afford to lose this one.
---

| | Peter,
The students at Sumner Academy are a great example of what's possible when hard work, high expectations, and strong educators come together.
Jeff and I enjoyed visiting Sumner Academy in Wyandotte County and seeing firsthand the people and programs behind one of Kansas' top-performing schools. It was great to spend time with students and educators who are helping build a strong future for our state.
Kansas is at its best when we give the next generation every opportunity to learn, grow, and succeed.
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
On the Trail with Ty
---
| | It was great to visit the Community Health Center of Southeast Kansas and spend time with the people who work every day to provide care to families across the region.
Strong communities depend on having access to quality healthcare close to home, especially in rural areas. I appreciated the opportunity to hear directly from the team about the work they're doing, the challenges they face, and how we can continue strengthening communities across Southeast Kansas.
Thank you for having me!
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| Kansas Law Enforcement Endorses
---
| This week, the two largest law enforcement groups in the state of Kansas, the Kansas State Lodge Fraternal Order of Police and the Kansas State Troopers Association announced their endorsements of our campaign.
In their announcement, KSTA President Joel Dryden stated:
"Ty Masterson has consistently stood with Kansas law enforcement. He understands that supporting the men and women who protect our communities means listening to law enforcement, fighting for the resources officers need, and taking action when public safety is at stake... Ty Masterson has been there for Kansas law enforcement, and we know where he stands when it comes to supporting those who protect our state. The Kansas State Troopers Association is proud to endorse Ty Masterson for Governor."
\--
I'm honored to receive the endorsements of both the Kansas State Lodge Fraternal Order of Police and the Kansas State Troopers Association. Every day, law enforcement officers across Kansas put on the uniform and answer the call to keep our families, neighborhoods, and communities safe. Their service and sacrifice deserve our respect, our gratitude, and our support. I'm grateful to have their trust and proud to stand with the men and women who serve and protect Kansans every single day.

clean_body: We need your help. | | = Friend, Between our town hall kickoff this week and our new digital ads, we have a lot going on! Scroll down for the latest from the trail and find out how you can pitch in for the final stretch! Ways To Get Involved This Week 1. Our town hall series continues next week in Laceyville. You can find all the details — make sure you share with your friends, and we’ll see you out there! 2. Sign up to canvass! We are hitting the pavement nearly every day around the district to get out the word about Rachel. 3. Whether you come to our office in Pottsville or you choose to make calls from your couch, we need your help calling voters to make sure they have a plan to vote. Sign up to join us on Tuesdays at 6:00 PM for our team phone bank! What We’ve Been Up To We’ve been busy this past week! Here’s a recap: ** On Tuesday, Rachel sat down with seniors in Berks and Schuylkill Counties. Our seniors paid into Social Security and Medicare their whole lives, and they've earned every benefit. We need someone in Congress who is going to protect these programs and keep our promises. $152 million. 382 new jobs. 2,524 jobs staying put. Bell & Evans is expanding in Lebanon County, and that's great news for our farmers. More demand for their work means more opportunity for the family farms that keep our communities going. This is what investing in PA agriculture looks like. Proud to stand with our local farmers. The price at the gas pump has got to come down. Bloomsburg Fair: Fall is in the air, and we had a blast at the fair this past weekend talking to voters, and eating apple dumplings, of course. From Tremont to St. Clair: We don’t want our part of PA to be a dumping ground. We deserve better. It's beautiful in our part of Pennsylvania right now — but with the cost of fuel it's hard to even get around. On Tuesday night, we had 150 folks fill the Allen Theatre in Annville for our very first town hall. What I heard from folks in Annville is what I’ve been hearing all across the trail: We’re tired of feeling divided. It's time we had a representative who listens and works for us. Rachel’s second town hall in Shartlesville is in the books! We had over 60 people come out Wednesday night to talk about the high price of heating oil, the giant cut to Medicaid Dan Meuser voted for last year, and the political divisions in our country. We need representation that shows up, listens, and then fights for lower costs. For better health care. For our communities here, not a political party. We're back on the town hall trail next week in the northern tier. If you have events in your area you’d like to invite Rachel to, please get in touch with us atmailto:info@wallaceforcongress.com. Upcoming Events and Volunteer Opportunities Help us get the word out about our town hall series and meet and greet events. Join us to meet Rachel, share what’s on your mind, and get your questions answered. Make sure to RSVP at the link and share with your friends. October 14, 6-8PM: October 18, 3-5PM: October 19, 5:30-8PM: Canvass in your county! We have opportunities across the district — Make calls to get out the vote! No matter where you live, you can join the campaign by making calls every Tuesday until the election.** Join us from home or at the Pottsville office on Tuesdays from 6-8PM to make calls to voters across the district and get out the vote. The countdown to Election Day is on — and we appreciate your help getting over the finish line! Friends,

**25 days** —that is all we have left. Right now, polling shows we are 2 points ahead of Mike Lawler, but in a race this close, the outcome will come down to how many doors we knock, how many phone calls we make, and how many voters we turn out this November. For the next 25 days, we are asking everyone to leave everything on the field. Because this district deserves better, and this race is about something bigger than one seat. It is about the kind of country we are fighting to leave behind. Team Cait

# GOP challenger hammers Letitia James in heated debate
New York Attorney General Letitia James **[faced sharp attacks from Republican challenger Saritha Komatireddy](https://substack.com/redirect/268714b3-7455-40be-b2c5-7e6be686b798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during a debate Thursday night, as Komatireddy accused the incumbent of being soft on crime, mishandling Medicaid fraud enforcement and failing to adequately prosecute antisemitic hate crimes, while James largely responded by tying her opponent to President Trump.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/268714b3-7455-40be-b2c5-7e6be686b798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Komatireddy pressed James over New York's bail laws,** citing a recent stabbing of an NYPD officer by migrants with prior records, and proposed letting judges weigh a defendant's "dangerousness" before release -- a question James largely sidestepped in favor of attacking Komatireddy's Trump ties.
* **Komatireddy also criticized James over the Cornell gang-rape case** for publicly backing the alleged victim before being named special prosecutor, declining Medicaid fraud recoveries, and insufficient prosecution of antisemitic hate crimes, while James defended her record and cited limited authority and resources.
* **The two clashed sharply over handling mentally ill individuals in the subway system,** with Komatireddy pushing for a new "Office of Civil Commitment" and James defending expanded outpatient treatment funded through opioid settlement money.

Friend, when our "leaders" spread lies about our elections to further their own agenda and hand over more power to Trump, that's not service.
That's cowardice.
Over the course of this race, my Republican opponent's loudest messages have been debunked. He has repeated fringe conspiracy theories about our elections, called for changes that strip voters of their access to the ballot and secure drop boxes, and stayed silent in the face of Trump's mail-in voting attacks.

## **Find Your Ice Bucket: How Republicans Can Win the Final 30 Days**
In the lead-up to the 1994 midterm elections - when Republicans flipped the House of Representatives for the first time in over 40 years - Newt Gingrich carried a very simple prop with him to campaign stops across the country.
It was an ordinary ice bucket.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/26c5c0f2-1be2-42e7-bc67-f261bb477cad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
To the average voter, it looked like a random gimmick. But to Newt, it was a physical symbol of everything that was wrong with Washington.
Here's the backstory: for decades, House patronage rules dictated that a congressional staffer would deliver fresh ice to every member's office twice a day. By the 1990s, every single congressional office already had a modern refrigerator and freezer inside - making the ice delivery service completely obsolete. But because politicians love spending taxpayer money to preserve cushy patronage jobs, the daily ice delivery remained in place year after year.
Ending that program in the 1990's saved around $300,000 - a drop in the bucket compared to the federal budget. But that ice bucket became a stark, undeniable visual for working Americans: **Washington was burning your hard-earned tax dollars on useless, outdated nonsense.**
As we head into the final 30 days of this election cycle, every Republican running for Congress needs to find their own ice bucket.

It was an ordinary ice bucket. | | ---|---|--- To the average voter, it looked like a random gimmick. But to Newt, it was a physical symbol of everything that was wrong with Washington. Here's the backstory: for decades, House patronage rules dictated that a congressional staffer would deliver fresh ice to every member's office twice a day. By the 1990s, every single congressional office already had a modern refrigerator and freezer inside - making the ice delivery service completely obsolete. But because politicians love spending taxpayer money to preserve cushy patronage jobs, the daily ice delivery remained in place year after year. Ending that program in the 1990's saved around $300,000 - a drop in the bucket compared to the federal budget. But that ice bucket became a stark, undeniable visual for working Americans: Washington was burning your hard-earned tax dollars on useless, outdated nonsense. body:
Make your first gift today and receive a FREE “God's Children Are Not For Sale” t-shirt as our thank-you.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e5988934/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvZDlqR2N1NXBuNA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjEwMDk/LbmNsOVJEU0c1Nw/qP2hpZHM9bmNCNzBJMExQQ3g3WXJscw/gaskVgQ/s5s17d3de80)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| |
---
| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend, I want to start with two simple words. **Thank you.** Thank you for caring about children you may never meet. Thank you for believing that every child has value and for refusing to accept a world where innocent children can be bought and sold. Because that is exactly what is happening. **Every day.**
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**God's children are not for sale.** And today, I'd like to send you a shirt that boldly declares that truth. When you make your first gift to the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** today, we'll send you a FREE white **"God's Children Are Not For Sale"** t-shirt as our thank-you.
---
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | | This isn't a shirt you'll find in a store. You can't buy it online. It was created exclusively for supporters of the **Sound of Freedom Foundation.** People who believe children deserve safety, refuse to look away and are willing to stand up and say: **"No more."** Every time you wear it, you'll be sharing a message that matters. **A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity.** And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see. **Most of all Friend, I hope this shirt reminds you that you are part of something bigger than yourself.** A growing movement of people determined to protect vulnerable children. Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission. **Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color.**
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verástegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Every day, vulnerable children are targeted by traffickers who prey on poverty, instability, loneliness, and fear. And every day, we work to fight back. Jesus said, _"Let the little children come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."_ (Matthew 19:14) **Every child is precious in God's eyes.** **Every child is created with dignity, purpose, and worth.** And every child deserves someone willing to stand up and fight for them
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
When you make your first gift today, you help:
---
* **Prevent exploitation** by helping strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children.

* **Support intervention efforts** by equipping trusted partners working to help rescue children trapped in exploitation.

* **Educate parents and communities** about the warning signs traffickers use to target children.

* **Raise awareness** so more people understand the reality of this crisis.

* **Advocate for stronger protections** for vulnerable children and greater accountability for traffickers.

---
This is how change happens. **One person refuses to ignore the suffering, refuses to stay silent, and chooses to fight for a child they may never meet.** **Today, that person can be you.**
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Will you make your first gift now? **[Please make your most generous gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can today to help protect vulnerable children from exploitation and trafficking.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** Choose your shirt size and select a color. **And know that your generosity will help protect vulnerable children and bring hope to those who need it most.** Thank you for caring and for standing with vulnerable children. **Thank you for choosing action over silence**. With gratitude and prayer,
---
Eduardo Verástegui
Sound of Freedom, Producer
For the Sound of Freedom Foundation
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**P.S.** Your FREE "**God's Children Are Not For Sale** " t-shirt is available only for a limited time and only while supplies last. Please make your first gift today, choose your size, and join a growing movement committed to protecting vulnerable children. Every child matters. Every child deserves freedom.
---
[ Support the Sound of Freedom Foundation ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074
---

108 S Washington St. Suite 200
Alexandria, VA 22314

body:
From listening to neighbors across six counties to taking a stand for accountability in Washington, here's what I've been up to.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1CczDRIcjUV?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Hi friend,
It's been a busy few months, and I wanted to take a moment to share what's been happening.
I've been traveling across Northeast Ohio, meeting people in coffee shops, at county fairs, community events, and everywhere in between. And if there's one thing I've learned, it's that we have a lot more in common than Washington would have us believe.
People are worried about the cost of living, access to healthcare, their families' futures, and whether anyone in Congress is actually listening.
But I've also met so many people who haven't given up hope. People who care deeply about their neighbors and their communities. People who want something better than the division and dysfunction we've come to expect.
**That's the Massive Middle I've been talking about.
And that's who I'm running to represent.**

**TAKING ACTION**
My commitment to accountability recently took me to Washington, D.C., where I joined other congressional candidates calling on Congress to reclaim its constitutional responsibilities. I also signed the [Take Back Congress Pledge](https://us.list-manage.com/BZo_XIOkJs8?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261), a commitment to restoring Congress as an independent, coequal branch of government — one that serves the American people, not the interests of any president or political party.
****
Congress was never meant to be a rubber stamp for the White House. Our founders designed a system of checks and balances for a reason. And when elected representatives surrender their responsibility to hold power accountable, it's the American people who lose their voice.
**It's time for Congress to do its job again.**

**GAME TIME
** Now we're in the final weeks of this campaign, and things are moving fast. Early voting has begun, our campaign commercials are getting ready to launch, and our volunteers are working hard to reach voters across all six counties.
I hope you'll stay connected, share our message, and, most importantly, make a plan to vote.
I'm grateful you're here. We're building something together, and I'm excited about what these next few weeks can bring.
If nothing changes, nothing changes.
With gratitude,Maria Jukic

subject: This isn’t who we are in Colorado
body:
| | |

Friend,
One of the things I love most about Colorado is that we believe people should be free to live their lives and make the decisions that are right for them and their families.
As a dad to three daughters, I’ve spent a lot of my life thinking about the kind of world I want them — and every kid in Colorado — to grow up in: one where they are treated with dignity, where they can be themselves, and where their families are trusted to make deeply personal decisions together.
**That’s why I’m supporting the campaign to defeat two ballot measures, Propositions 134 and 135, targeting transgender kids and their families.**
These measures would put politicians in the middle of decisions that belong with parents, kids, and their doctors.
I don’t believe that’s who we are in Colorado.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I never planned to be in politics
body:
| | | | Gina here. I’ll be completely honest with you:

I never planned on running for Governor. I never planned on being in politics at all.

But after a decade of Greg Abbott abandoning our schools, families, and communities, it’s obvious: If we want change, we have to create it ourselves. [**I’d like to tell you more about my story and why I’m running. But if you’re ready to take action now, you can split a donation here between Equal Opportunity Now and my campaign to power our fight for Texas.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141044378/652349021/1593610140?refcode=261009_gina3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNTNkMDc1OS0wMWM0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=w9_y-1EzxWl4sWD8fQWBSzzPJxtdLe8qk-imOrymy5A=)

I loved my work as a civil rights and union lawyer. I fought every day for families, workers, and fairness. I represented Texans who had been pushed around or shut out, people who just wanted what they had earned: fair well-paying jobs, dignity, and a chance to build a better life. I thought I’d do that work forever.

But sometimes life puts a decision in front of you that you can’t ignore. For me, that moment came the day I learned my son’s elementary school was being closed because of budget cuts. It wasn’t failing or unsafe — just “in the way” of a plan to hand schools over to private interests looking to profit off our kids' futures. Families and teachers were shaken and uncertain of what would come next, and I realized something terrifying: No one was coming to save us.

So I stepped up. I ran for the Austin ISD’s Board of Trustees, won, and helped block a corporate takeover of our public schools.

**It taught me something powerful: When Texans stand up, we win big battles. **

But the fight was just starting. Neighborhood schools kept closing across Texas because Republican leaders kept diverting money away from classrooms. So I made another decision I never expected to make: I ran for the Texas House.

As a state representative, I secured billions in school funding. I passed a first-of-its-kind law so Texas businesses could do well financially and do good in our communities. I delivered nearly a billion dollars in healthcare funding to Travis County. I helped organize walkouts that blocked Abbott’s voter suppression bill and fought back against his school voucher scheme.

**_The same determination I’ve had my entire career is why I’m running for Governor of Texas today — to defend the Texas I grew up with and fight for every family who calls this state home. _**

Because Texas simply can’t afford another four years of Greg Abbott. For a decade, Abbott has sold out working families to enrich the wealthy and powerful at every step. He kicks children off Medicaid to save a few extra bucks for Big Pharma. He shuts down public schools so private interests can get rich on vouchers. He ignores families crushed by rising prices while he funnels nearly a billion of our taxpayer dollars into no-bid contracts for his donors.

With your help, I can become the next Governor of Texas. I’ve beaten Abbott before, and I’m ready to do it again. And right now, he’s the least popular he’s ever been — so this is our chance.

But defeating a three-term incumbent backed by right-wing billionaire money takes real people power. It takes Texans standing up together and saying: Enough.

**[So I’m asking you directly: Can I count on you to split $20 today between Equal Opportunity Now and my campaign to power the movement to take Texas back? ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141044379/652349022/1593610140?refcode=261009_gina3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNTNkMDc1OS0wMWM0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=w9_y-1EzxWl4sWD8fQWBSzzPJxtdLe8qk-imOrymy5A=)**

It is absolutely critical that we re-elect Justice Anita Earls to the North Carolina Supreme Court, and we have to do it by a margin that's too big to rig.
I'll explain why in a second. **[But if that's all you need to hear, please split a donation between my campaign and Anita's today.](https://substack.com/redirect/a36babb0-088e-4504-89b0-604c28a4eb91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/a36babb0-088e-4504-89b0-604c28a4eb91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b884f622-903a-42a3-a079-191bda3788de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Anita Earls and I in Concord, North Carolina
Back in 2024, North Carolinians elected Justice Allison Riggs to the NC Supreme Court by the slimmest of margins: **734 votes out of 5.5 million cast.** Her election took nearly six months and was the last race in the nation to be certified.
But that isn't because of the margin, at least not entirely. It's because her opponent and state Republicans asked the courts to throw out 60,000 legal ballots after the election. **In effect, they tried to change the rules after the game was already played.**
That meant that some North Carolinians registered to vote before the state changed our voter registration requirements; some cast their ballots from overseas; and active-duty military North Carolinians mailed their ballots from wherever they were stationed at the time.
All of these were legal ballots, and state Republicans tried to throw them out anyway. **Those are the lengths they were willing to go to flip a seat on our Supreme Court in 2024 and we must anticipate that it will be no different this time around.**
Justice Anita Earls stands for accountability, keeping our communities safe and equal justice for all under the law. It's imperative we re-elect her.
**[I hope you're with me. If you are, please chip in a donation between my campaign and hers today.](https://substack.com/redirect/a36babb0-088e-4504-89b0-604c28a4eb91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/a36babb0-088e-4504-89b0-604c28a4eb91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you.
Roy Cooper

I was 33 years old when I became an activist. Before that, my life felt meaningless – like I was living without a clear purpose. Joining the movement against the Vietnam War changed everything. I realized I wasn’t alone. There was an entire community of people willing to stand up for what’s right, even when it feels impossible. Movements are only as strong as the people who show up. When we stick together, they can’t pick us off one by one. It can be scary to speak out. Big Oil and its billionaire backers want us to feel isolated, overwhelmed, and exhausted. But in my decades of activism, I’ve learned one inescapable truth: **hope comes alive with action.** Hope isn’t optimism. It’s not sitting back and thinking everything will be okay. It comes from ordinary people deciding the status quo is unacceptable. It comes from people standing up to corporate greed. It comes from one person deciding our future is worth fighting for. It’s why I decided to dedicate my time to electing climate leaders at every level of government who have the moral courage to fight for our future. **JanePAC has already helped send 250 climate champions to the halls of power — and with your support, we can elect even more this November. clean_body: | I was 33 years old when I became an activist. Before that, my life felt meaningless – like I was living without a clear purpose. Joining the movement against the Vietnam War changed everything. I realized I wasn’t alone. There was an entire community of people willing to stand up for what’s right, even when it feels impossible. Movements are only as strong as the people who show up. When we stick together, they can’t pick us off one by one. It can be scary to speak out. Big Oil and its billionaire backers want us to feel isolated, overwhelmed, and exhausted. But in my decades of activism, I’ve learned one inescapable truth: hope comes alive with action. Hope isn’t optimism. It’s not sitting back and thinking everything will be okay. It comes from ordinary people deciding the status quo is unacceptable. It comes from people standing up to corporate greed. It comes from one person deciding our future is worth fighting for. It’s why I decided to dedicate my time to electing climate leaders at every level of government who have the moral courage to fight for our future. JanePAC has already helped send 250 climate champions to the halls of power — and with your support, we can elect even more this November. But our candidates are facing massive spending from corporate special interests, and they need us by their side now. = | = Thank you for joining this fight. xx Jane | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. You just need to open your eyes and look at what’s happening right here on the ground. People in our district are losing their shirts right now. Our military families are bearing the brunt of a massive conflict. There’s no big mystery or point of complication here—this war has been a disaster for working families, plain and simple. I don't need to check in with party bosses or divine what the White House is thinking to do my job. That's why I've voted against the president's war six times. I know who I work for. Not what I spent my time doing

|
Peter,
I’ll be honest with you... I’m not great at asking for money. It’s the part of this job I hate the most.
I didn’t spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf.
And when I came home, I didn’t become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals.
That’s really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it’s going in the wrong direction most days.
[I didn't run for Congress for the title. I ran because I looked at the country my children were inheriting, and I felt sick to my stomach. I couldn't just sit there.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMDlfWlEtTkcuMTE0NTEwX3QyMDUwMDI4LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDA5X1pRLU5HLjExNDUxMF90MjA1MDAyOC0yMDY4In0/Rq3_CG7_3OomEqJ3iddTZQ)
But here is the hard truth: fighting the radical Left and standing up for our values is incredibly expensive. I don’t have a massive machine behind me. I don’t have someone who can write blank checks on a whim.
[I just have normal folks like you.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMDlfWlEtTkcuMTE0NTEwX3QyMDUwMDI4LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDA5X1pRLU5HLjExNDUxMF90MjA1MDAyOC0yMDY4In0/iw7t4MDE-bA3Om64n55XPQ)

_In a Palestinian village surrounded by armed Israeli outposts, the olive trees still stand, the roads still exist, and the families still own their land. Increasingly, none of that means they can reach it._
_Qusra: The Geography of Dispossession is one part of a multi-part multimedia series I 'm publishing here on Mesoscale News._
_My trip to the West Bank and the work I do here is only possible through your support. Please consider upgrading to a paid subscription or[donating directly here.](https://substack.com/redirect/dc7923cf-dd51-4340-a92e-a8f6a12b4b38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..0duE3HAXGQEEfV0-HQp7V3IrT1RZQfIFJlgYb-GcNgA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=219615313)
* * *
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fb8b92b6-ac06-4d7c-bfc8-11c0d676f38b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Meeting the Qusra mayor, Abed Wadi (black striped shirt), in the municipal building in the West Bank.
QUSRA, WEST BANK, PALESTINE -- In the back room of an otherwise plain and colorless municipal building, the names and photos of twelve young men murdered by Israeli military and settler terrorists looked down on us as we arrived.
The memorials were hung over the meeting space as a reminder of the increasing violence against Palestinians, and of the freedom that has become an artifact of the past.
Palestinian Muslim families have been living in Qusra since at least the 1500's. In the 1882 _[Survey of Western Palestine](https://substack.com/redirect/b1ad71fb-4500-44b2-858b-7b29c6cf9906?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) , _Qusra was described a small village low in the valley, a few hundred inhabitants, with large olive and oak trees.
The 1922 _Census of Palestine_ showed 707 people in Qusra; by 1931, 851 people; and in 1961, the Jordanian survey counted 1,312 people.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2a4dbd38-6756-4301-a4d3-eef95976ef2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
During the 19 years of Jordanian rule, Qusra flourished. Then Israel began illegally occupying the West Bank in 1967, and families began living under siege.
Then in 1995, the Oslo II Accords took the 2,500 acres of Palestinian land in Qusra and cut it in half -- 50% would be in Area B and 50% in Area C.
Israeli stole another 50 acres to build the illegal settlement of Migdalim.
Migdalim, like most illegal Israeli settlements and outposts, was built on Palestinian agricultural lands -- mostly olive groves and orchards.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f2ac6564-56cb-40df-800c-44d2670564aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
By 2010, 50 homes had been built on the area. Today, Migdalim has a population of more than 800 people.
Earlier this year, Israel approved an expansion of 140 new homes for the illegal settlement.
Settlements like Migdalim surround Qusra today, isolating it from neighboring villages, putting them under constant surveillance, the theft of land creeping closer and closer every day.
Palestinian communities have become islands in a sea of bureaucratic violence, surrounded by sharks, never knowing if they're safe from an incursion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1c949e2e-665d-4c32-94d4-257ba5552090?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Qusra Mayor Abed Wadi recalled how there had once been olive trees and fig trees, weddings, children playing in the streets in the areas around the city. There were farmers who knew the surrounding hillsides not as disputed territory but as the land their families had cultivated for generations. There had been the ordinary pleasures of belonging somewhere, the unremarkable certainty that a person could leave home in the morning, work his fields, and return in the evening.
When our American delegation arrived in Qusra in September 2026, Wadi asked us to imagine visiting nearly twenty years earlier.
> "If you had come to visit the town before 2008 and 2009, I would have explained and introduced Qusra in a different way than what I'm doing today, because the circumstances were totally different."
He had prepared a different history for us now. It was a history of burned homes, destroyed olive groves, roads closed by the Israeli military, and relatives who had been killed.
Four of the young men, Hasan Abu Sorour, 16, Obayda Abu Sorour, 17, Moath Odeh, 21, and Musab Abu Reda, 25, were killed when a mob of Israeli settler terrorists began attacking family homes in Qusra on [October 11, 2023.](https://substack.com/redirect/c4dd87be-33d2-4db5-99f6-f9353ac7fa56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
As the funeral procession gathered the next day, Israeli settler terrorists open fired on the vehicles, killing two Palestinians.
The dead were Wadi's brother, Ibrahim, 63, who was a senior official in the Palestinian Ministry of Finance, and his brother's son, Ahmed, 26, who recently graduated law school and became engaged.
Wadi described the killings with the familiarity of someone who had repeated these details too many times, and with the grief of someone for whom repetition had made them no easier.
His account was also a geography lesson.
The destruction of Qusra is not measured only in the number of Palestinians killed, the homes attacked, or the olive trees destroyed. It is measured in the shrinking territory residents can safely occupy, the farmland they can no longer cultivate, the roads they can no longer travel, and the distances between communities that grow longer without the towns themselves moving an inch.
In Qusra, Palestinians are not simply losing land. They are being systematically separated from the means of living on it.
The process is sometimes described in the language of settlement expansion, as though the principal development were the construction of houses. The people we interviewed used considerably less forgiving language. They described armed Israeli terrorists, intimidation, dispossession, and the deliberate destruction of Palestinian life.
Their testimony, supported by years of human rights investigations and United Nations reporting, reveals a system in which violence does not merely accompany territorial expansion.
Violence is how the expansion happens.
The village remains on the map -- for now. The world around it is being taken away.
## A village measured in funerals
Wadi traced the transformation of Qusra to the years surrounding [2011](https://substack.com/redirect/ecbb5a12-3343-4f9d-8aa1-d67f26506d19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), when armed Israelis attacked agricultural property and [burned a mosque](https://substack.com/redirect/c30bfc24-a1a4-48c5-b367-b67ef24dc487?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He described thousands of olive trees damaged or destroyed, farming equipment confiscated, and residents increasingly prevented from reaching their fields.
> "They confiscated farming equipment. They confiscated tractors, bulldozers. They prevented us from accessing or farming. We started going to our own olive fields and olive trees as strangers."
[International calls for accountability and justice](https://substack.com/redirect/0df03948-76f9-4be0-b0ff-dbb8dd4445cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) went unanswered, and the [violence continued to escalate.](https://substack.com/redirect/2a5a7642-567b-4a28-a191-7ea9655e1de3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For a farming community, land is not merely property. It is memory made physical. Families inherit trees planted by parents and grandparents, terraces maintained across generations, and an intimate understanding of soil, rainfall, seasonal rhythms, and harvests. The landscape holds knowledge that cannot be transferred to another place.
To be denied access to it is to lose something long before the property records change.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8f729e6b-aa3e-405f-a6fe-919e27e6c6c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The view of the area around Qusra, taken from the home of an American-Palestinian in the West Bank, Palestine.
The killings came in succession. The mayor recounted deaths across multiple years, including the October 2023 attacks that devastated Qusra.
> "It was the darkest day for Qusra. Because the settlers killed six young men on that same day together."
A January 2024 investigation by The Washington Post reconstructed the attacks through witness accounts, video evidence, and other documentation. Its headline captured one of the investigation's central findings: ["Settlers killed a Palestinian teen. Israeli forces didn't stop it."](https://substack.com/redirect/593db890-7a0e-4018-8a92-21a3aa5436c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The investigation also reproduced a threat sent to Qusra residents before the attack. The message addressed Palestinians as animals and promised that revenge was coming.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1279ca71-e278-43fc-b267-3228838b602c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"Mohammad is a pig", graffiti by Israeli settlers from Esh Kodesh on the [al-Nurayn Mosque](https://substack.com/redirect/503e11f0-e119-4c92-925d-1f64627c7158?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Qusra.
What followed was not an unforeseeable eruption of anger. Residents had been threatened, armed attackers arrived, and Palestinian families were left to confront the consequences.
For the mayor, the losses were personal.
> "One of whom was my brother, my own brother"
His brother Ibrahim, he explained, had eleven children. A younger family member, twenty-four years old and studying law, was engaged to be married.
It is easy for the scale of Palestinian suffering to become obscured by numbers. Here, each number had a family attached to it: eleven children, a wedding that would never take place, an empty place at the table.
The attacks continued.
On April 13, 2024, roughly 180 to 200 armed Israelis descended on Qusra, burning agricultural buildings, homes, vehicles, and municipal property. Wadi described livestock killed and residents injured.
> "They burned houses that was already inhabited and houses that were under construction. They burned cars. They killed cows and sheep."
Then he added:
> "And one of the injured was one of my own children."
In August 2026, weeks before our visit, armed Israelis again attacked homes in Qusra.
Reuters reported that dozens of masked attackers threw stones at a house while seven Palestinians were trapped inside. [According to witnesses](https://substack.com/redirect/c7d54963-c19c-4e4f-aea3-5081e09b955e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Israeli forces subsequently fired tear gas into the home and detained its Palestinian occupants. The residents described being blindfolded, handcuffed, and beaten.
The violence had moved from the agricultural hillsides to the thresholds of people's homes.
## The small outpost and the enormous territory it controls
Driving toward Qusra, we passed Israeli settlements extending across the hilltops. Our Palestinian guide identified Shilo, Eli, and Ma'ale Levona, pointing toward agricultural land that Palestinian communities could no longer freely access.
Geography is not only about what occupies a place. It is also about who has been excluded from it.
Our guide pointed toward land associated with nearby Palestinian communities.
> "They've taken over the land."
Later, explaining the restrictions on movement, he told us:
> "We're only using this road because it's the only road connecting between north and south."
Palestinians could travel along the route, he explained, but entering the surrounding settlement areas was prohibited or dangerous.
The road had become a narrow corridor through a landscape over which others exercised control.
During our meeting in Qusra, a delegation member asked about the groups establishing themselves around Palestinian villages. Were these isolated attackers, or was there a larger structure behind the intimidation?
The municipal representative rejected the language of isolated misconduct.
> "First of all, I consider the the settlers, who Netanyahu calls outlaws, rioters, we call them terrorists."
The people burning homes, attacking farmers, and driving families from their land were not simply unruly neighbors. They were participating in a territorial campaign of terrorism and murder.
He described armed groups supplied with vehicles, weapons, and equipment, establishing themselves near Palestinian agricultural land and extending their influence through intimidation.
The result, he said, was the seizure of territory without the cost or visibility of a conventional military operation.
This is the fundamental geography of the Israeli outpost system.
A small number of structures can occupy a ridge while the armed men living there exercise control over an area many times larger. A Palestinian farmer may still possess a deed to the surrounding land, but that document offers little protection against someone waiting with a rifle.
Israeli organization Peace Now documented the proliferation of outposts in Area B in 2026, demonstrating that the expansion was no longer confined to land already under full Israeli civil administration. [Its investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/8398e9ea-462d-4900-a243-b92b4c0fee8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) described the establishment of outposts in territory formally assigned Palestinian civil authority.
The spatial consequences are enormous.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a52d1ce-8797-4741-8f9b-1681ace645aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Areas A and B are under the authority of democratically elected Palestinian local governments. The map above from Peace Now shows Area B illegal outposts built in 2025.
An outpost need not occupy an entire hillside to make the hillside inaccessible. It need only make the consequences of entering sufficiently frightening.
Once Palestinian farmers stop returning, the land becomes available for further encroachment.
What looks on a map like a small point of occupation becomes, in practice, a much larger zone of exclusion.
## Land theft without paperwork
A Palestinian representative from Turmus Ayya, whom we interviewed during the same trip, offered perhaps the clearest explanation of how this process works.
He described olive groves that families still owned but could no longer safely enter.
> "There's no such thing as formally seized because they do not give you a notice. They do not tell you that this land has been seized."
He called it:
> "de facto seizure by the conduct of the settlers."
There is no necessary announcement, no document handed to the owner, no single moment at which the land officially changes hands.
Instead, the farmer learns where he can no longer go.
> "You learn it. You become to learn it that this is a dangerous area. I I should not go there."
This is an especially effective form of coercive territorial control because it requires relatively little continuous enforcement. Once people have been attacked, or have watched their neighbors attacked, the threat becomes embedded in their understanding of the landscape.
The boundary is no longer simply a fence or checkpoint.
It is fear.
The farmer knows which road may be blocked, which grove may be watched, which hillside may conceal armed men. He adjusts his movements accordingly. His children learn the same geography.
Eventually, the prohibited territory becomes abandoned: a place everyone knows belongs to the village, and everyone knows they must avoid.
In geographic terms, legal ownership remains intact while practical access collapses.
The occupation creates two overlapping maps: one of property and another of power.
The second increasingly determines whether the first means anything.
## When the army arrives
Another representative from Turmus Ayya also described how armed Israelis exploit military authority to remove Palestinians from their own land.
He said attackers often approach in groups, with weapons displayed openly. They push or provoke Palestinian landowners while recording the confrontation on their phones.
> "They start pushing me, kicking me, you know, shouldering me, pushing me with their hands and with their phones."
Then, he explained:
> "When I raise my hand, they call the IDF and claim that I attack them."
Israeli soldiers then intervene against the Palestinian.
> "So they come and detain me and arrest me and take me somewhere so I can disappear for a week or two."
He described being detained for four hours with his wife and a news crew and said the crew was instructed to erase its footage before being released.
In October 2025, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs [confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/7a414c6f-aaa4-47ea-945f-abaed042c625?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that armed Israelis, accompanied by Israeli forces, had prevented Palestinian farmers from reaching olive groves across several West Bank communities.
In nearby Kobar, residents were [reportedly](https://substack.com/redirect/75c73b06-732b-4ec1-9022-2d253faeae6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) required to seek permission from an outpost guard to access agricultural land that had previously been freely accessible. Elsewhere, armed Israelis seized harvested olives while farmers were prevented from working their land.
This is a profound inversion of territorial authority.
The Palestinian farmer becomes the person required to explain why he is present.
The armed Israeli occupying or controlling the surrounding land becomes the person deciding whether he may stay.
In Qusra, residents described the same inversion at their homes. The August 2026 [Reuters investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/c7d54963-c19c-4e4f-aea3-5081e09b955e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) documented allegations that Israeli forces detained Palestinians after armed Israelis attacked the house in which they had sought refuge.
A system that repeatedly exposes Palestinian landowners to violence, detention, and exclusion while enabling armed groups to maintain territorial control cannot be understood simply through the language of sporadic criminality.
Its effects are geographic, cumulative, and political.
## The olive harvest, interrupted
The most revealing measure of Qusra's dispossession may be found not in a military map but in the village's olive oil production.
A Qusra official reported that Qusra produced approximately 123 metric tons of olive oil in 2023, falling to 115 in 2024 and just 58 in 2025. For 2026, he anticipated only 16 to 20 metric tons.
##### Qusra's disappearing olive harvest
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f1064792-c20d-4c47-9cec-4581d3e1741c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Figures provided by Qusra municipal representatives during the September 2026 interview.
If the projection holds, production will have fallen approximately 85% from its reported 2023 level.
Olive trees naturally experience fluctuations in productivity. Rainfall, temperature, disease, and alternate-bearing cycles influence harvests. These figures alone cannot isolate the effects of violence from environmental variability.
The interviews explain how farmers are being prevented from carrying out even the most basic agricultural work.
Another official from Turmus Ayya described three essential periods of access: preparing the soil in February, clearing vegetation around the trees in August, and harvesting the olives in October and November.
> "But the biggest attacks occur during harvest itself, because there's a time limit in in which you can harvest."
The timing matters. Olives cannot simply wait indefinitely for armed men to leave. Harvesting too late reduces quality and can destroy a season's economic value.
For farmers already operating with narrow margins, missing the harvest may mean losing an entire year's income.
He described how his household had once produced enough olive oil to give away to relatives and friends. Now, he said:
> "Right now, we buy our own. We have to go out and buy it."
A family that once cultivated, pressed, consumed, and shared its own olive oil had become dependent on purchasing it.
This is what agricultural dispossession looks like inside a household.
Across the West Bank, the scale of the destruction is staggering.
[OCHA documented ](https://substack.com/redirect/71574846-fb9d-4290-b640-13d3b501b014?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)1,680 Israeli attacks resulting in casualties or property damage across more than 270 communities during 2025. During October and November alone, the agency recorded 178 attacks associated with the olive harvest across 88 communities. More than 6,000 trees and saplings were vandalized that year.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2f80435c-a09d-4950-abc2-a8f78e1ea9cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
These figures do not capture every farmer who stayed home out of fear, every field that went untended, or every family that lost access to land without an incident recorded by international monitors.
The ecological consequences may also outlast the immediate violence. Agricultural terraces require maintenance. Soil needs protection against erosion. Trees require pruning and care. Traditional agricultural systems are sustained by repeated human labor across generations.
Denying farmers access to their land damages the relationship between people and the environment that makes cultivation possible.
An olive tree may survive the attack. The agricultural system surrounding it may not.
## The disappearance of Area B
Qusra's representatives described an increasingly aggressive expansion of armed Israeli activity from Area C into Area B, where Palestinians are formally assigned civil administrative authority under the Oslo framework.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/65a18025-feb8-4ff1-8909-c88bcf2d211c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Zones B (blue) surrounded by illegal Israeli outposts and settlements (red circles). Map current as of January 2026.
> " The violence and the intimidation have reached houses that fall in area B."
Wadi described three families living in houses that had become effectively separated from the rest of the village.
Armed Israelis, he said, had established tents near their homes, obstructed access roads, and interfered with essential services.
> "Electricity and water has been cut to some of the residents."
The families included young children.
The municipality could no longer reliably reach them with supplies.
> "It prevented us as a municipality and as a town from getting their needs of electricity, water, food, and supplies."
This is more than land encroachment. It is the isolation of Palestinian families within their own community.
The distinction between Areas A, B, and C was intended to define different administrative arrangements within an already illegal occupation. Yet the expansion of armed outposts and intimidation across those boundaries reveals how little protection such divisions provide when control over movement and security is exercised unequally.
A family may live within an area designated for Palestinian civil administration and still be unable to receive water, electricity, or food from its own municipality.
The boundary exists in law. It is disregarded in practice.
## The road that takes hours
The geography of dispossession extends beyond farmland.
Wadi described the closure of the village's main entrance since October 2023. The journey to Nablus, once approximately twenty minutes, could now take hours.
> "The passenger fare to get to Nablus used to be 8shekels. Now it's 22 shekels."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcf3c6d0-5bbf-4a41-b576-2f2895b612ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/92d03841-51a9-442d-b70a-98b4d2b96bc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e81d36b0-a25a-440a-87aa-777b6c8ef1f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4c2ff81a-4f79-4c64-927b-68c00fef7c54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Israeli gate closures cut off primary arteries connecting Palestinian towns, isolating them from each other._
The cost of a journey had nearly tripled.
The physical distance, of course, had not changed.
This is the distinction between geometric distance and functional accessibility. Two communities may remain separated by only a few kilometers, yet checkpoints, roadblocks, military closures, and detours can make traveling between them exhausting, expensive, or impossible.
The consequences ripple through daily life.
A hospital becomes harder to reach. A farmer loses access to markets. A student spends hours traveling to school. Families become isolated from relatives living in neighboring villages.
Wadi explained that visiting nearby Turmus Ayya could require planning an entire day.
The roads still existed, but their purpose had been transformed.
Rather than connecting Palestinian communities, they had become instruments through which access could be restricted and controlled.
## The geography of fear
During our trip, we also interviewed a Palestinian journalist who described being attacked while reporting near Nablus.
In one incident, she said armed Israelis fired live ammunition toward her and a colleague. In another, she was alone in a vehicle when armed men approached from a hillside.
She fled.
> "The first thing I did is left the car, and I start running, run and run and start screaming to my colleague to hear me."
She described how the terror continued long after the immediate danger had passed.
> "You don't discover it in the first days, but you have some trauma because you will dream"
Yet she refused to abandon her work.
> "I will never give up."
Her determination speaks to a broader reality: Palestinians are forced not only to survive the occupation but to document it, often at enormous personal risk.
On October 6, 2026, AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh [was beaten ](https://substack.com/redirect/cd69e970-dcf9-403e-8d45-784b5786b7a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)by armed Israelis while covering violence against Palestinian olive farmers near Aqraba. His camera equipment was stolen, and he was hospitalized with injuries. The attack occurred near Israeli soldiers, who, according to witnesses, did not intervene.
The risks facing journalists are part of the same landscape of intimidation confronting farmers and residents.
The violence regulates who may enter a place, who may remain there, and who may record what happens.
Fear becomes a method of territorial governance.
## The architecture of dispossession
The processes unfolding around Qusra are consistent with decades of scholarship examining the spatial organization of Israeli occupation.
In _Ethnocracy: Land and Identity Politics in Israel/Palestine_ (2006), geographer Oren Yiftachel analyzes how territorial policies and unequal access to land can reproduce political domination.
Eyal Weizman's _Hollow Land: Israel 's Architecture of Occupation_ (2007) examines the ways settlements, roads, military installations, and planning systems reorganize Palestinian space.
Both provide important frameworks for understanding why dispossession cannot be measured solely by the number of buildings constructed or acres formally confiscated.
Territorial control is also exercised through [mobility, infrastructure, access, and fear](https://substack.com/redirect/95b29eff-edec-4b8b-b416-90ede9861231?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
An armed outpost on a ridge can deny farmers access to surrounding valleys.
A closed gate can separate a village from its regional economy.
A blocked road can prevent a municipality from reaching families who live within its own boundaries.
An attack during olive harvest can destroy a year's income without damaging a single property deed.
The result is a landscape in which Palestinians may retain formal claims to land while losing the practical ability to inhabit and use it.
The International Court of Justice's July 2024 advisory opinion found Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territory unlawful and addressed the legal consequences of settlement expansion, land appropriation, and discriminatory restrictions on Palestinians. [The Court's opinion](https://substack.com/redirect/ee1a175d-67f1-4076-a3ea-d78f0d8d9dce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) placed these territorial practices within the broader framework of international law.
The geography of Qusra reveals how such violations become part of ordinary life.
The occupation is experienced not only through soldiers and weapons, but through the impossibility of reaching a field, the expense of traveling to a nearby town, and the uncertainty of whether a family can safely sleep in its own home.
## What remains of Qusra
Toward the end of our meeting, Wadi returned to the contradiction between the language of democracy and human rights, and the conditions his community was enduring.
He had described murdered relatives, destroyed farms, families isolated from their neighbors, and children living under armed intimidation.
He was not asking us to imagine some distant political possibility.
He was describing what it takes for a village to remain alive.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/480441d0-869b-4092-8bf3-8e52bf0b9ae9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A functioning community requires more than buildings and boundaries. It needs access to water, electricity, agricultural land, schools, hospitals, markets, and the surrounding landscape.
It needs the freedom to move.
It needs the ability to cultivate the soil and harvest what grows from it.
And it needs the reasonable expectation that its residents can return home without being attacked.
Qusra still possesses its name, its history, and its people. Its olive trees still stand on the hillsides. The agricultural terraces remain etched into the landscape.
But those physical remnants conceal the destruction taking place around them.
The land has not moved. The villages have not moved. The distances between them have not changed.
What has changed is who can cross those distances, who can cultivate the fields, and who can live without fear.
That is the geography of dispossession.
It is not only the theft of Palestinian land. It is the deliberate destruction of the relationships between people and place that make a homeland possible.
And in Qusra, the evidence is everywhere: in the groves left unharvested, the roads made impassable, the families trapped in their homes, and the names of the dead recited by a man who once would have welcomed visitors with stories about weddings and olive trees.
Qusra remains on the map for now, but increased violence and land seizures may one day lead to its destruction.
