QUSRA, WEST BANK, PALESTINE -- In the back room of an otherwise plain and colorless municipal building, the names and photos of twelve young men murdered by Israeli military and settler terrorists looked down on us as we arrived. The memorials were hung over the meeting space as a reminder of the increasing violence against Palestinians, and of the freedom that has become an artifact of the past. Palestinian Muslim families have been living in Qusra since at least the 1500's. In the 1882 , Qusra was described a small village low in the valley, a few hundred inhabitants, with large olive and oak trees. The 1922 Census of Palestine showed 707 people in Qusra; by 1931, 851 people; and in 1961, the Jordanian survey counted 1,312 people. | | ---|---|--- During the 19 years of Jordanian rule, Qusra flourished. Then Israel began illegally occupying the West Bank in 1967, and families began living under siege. Then in 1995, the Oslo II Accords took the 2,500 acres of Palestinian land in Qusra and cut it in half -- 50% would be in Area B and 50% in Area C. Israeli stole another 50 acres to build the illegal settlement of Migdalim. Migdalim, like most illegal Israeli settlements and outposts, was built on Palestinian agricultural lands -- mostly olive groves and orchards. | | ---|---|--- By 2010, 50 homes had been built on the area. Today, Migdalim has a population of more than 800 people. Earlier this year, Israel approved an expansion of 140 new homes for the illegal settlement. Settlements like Migdalim surround Qusra today, isolating it from neighboring villages, putting them under constant surveillance, the theft of land creeping closer and closer every day. Palestinian communities have become islands in a sea of bureaucratic violence, surrounded by sharks, never knowing if they're safe from an incursion. | | ---|---|--- Qusra Mayor Abed Wadi recalled how there had once been olive trees and fig trees, weddings, children playing in the streets in the areas around the city. There were farmers who knew the surrounding hillsides not as disputed territory but as the land their families had cultivated for generations. There had been the ordinary pleasures of belonging somewhere, the unremarkable certainty that a person could leave home in the morning, work his fields, and return in the evening. When our American delegation arrived in Qusra in September 2026, Wadi asked us to imagine visiting nearly twenty years earlier. "If you had come to visit the town before 2008 and 2009, I would have explained and introduced Qusra in a different way than what I'm doing today, because the circumstances were totally different." He had prepared a different history for us now. It was a history of burned homes, destroyed olive groves, roads closed by the Israeli military, and relatives who had been killed. Four of the young men, Hasan Abu Sorour, 16, Obayda Abu Sorour, 17, Moath Odeh, 21, and Musab Abu Reda, 25, were killed when a mob of Israeli settler terrorists began attacking family homes in Qusra on As the funeral procession gathered the next day, Israeli settler terrorists open fired on the vehicles, killing two Palestinians. The dead were Wadi's brother, Ibrahim, 63, who was a senior official in the Palestinian Ministry of Finance, and his brother's son, Ahmed, 26, who recently graduated law school and became engaged. Wadi described the killings with the familiarity of someone who had repeated these details too many times, and with the grief of someone for whom repetition had made them no easier. His account was also a geography lesson. The destruction of Qusra is not measured only in the number of Palestinians killed, the homes attacked, or the olive trees destroyed. It is measured in the shrinking territory residents can safely occupy, the farmland they can no longer cultivate, the roads they can no longer travel, and the distances between communities that grow longer without the towns themselves moving an inch. In Qusra, Palestinians are not simply losing land. They are being systematically separated from the means of living on it. The process is sometimes described in the language of settlement expansion, as though the principal development were the construction of houses. The people we interviewed used considerably less forgiving language. They described armed Israeli terrorists, intimidation, dispossession, and the deliberate destruction of Palestinian life. Their testimony, supported by years of human rights investigations and United Nations reporting, reveals a system in which violence does not merely accompany territorial expansion. Violence is how the expansion happens. The village remains on the map -- for now. The world around it is being taken away. A village measured in funerals Wadi traced the transformation of Qusra to the years surrounding , when armed Israelis attacked agricultural property and . He described thousands of olive trees damaged or destroyed, farming equipment confiscated, and residents increasingly prevented from reaching their fields. "They confiscated farming equipment. They confiscated tractors, bulldozers. They prevented us from accessing or farming. We started going to our own olive fields and olive trees as strangers." went unanswered, and the For a farming community, land is not merely property. It is memory made physical. Families inherit trees planted by parents and grandparents, terraces maintained across generations, and an intimate understanding of soil, rainfall, seasonal rhythms, and harvests. The landscape holds knowledge that cannot be transferred to another place. To be denied access to it is to lose something long before the property records change. | | ---|---|--- The view of the area around Qusra, taken from the home of an American-Palestinian in the West Bank, Palestine. The killings came in succession. The mayor recounted deaths across multiple years, including the October 2023 attacks that devastated Qusra. "It was the darkest day for Qusra. Because the settlers killed six young men on that same day together." A January 2024 investigation by The Washington Post reconstructed the attacks through witness accounts, video evidence, and other documentation. Its headline captured one of the investigation's central findings: The investigation also reproduced a threat sent to Qusra residents before the attack. The message addressed Palestinians as animals and promised that revenge was coming. | | ---|---|--- "Mohammad is a pig", graffiti by Israeli settlers from Esh Kodesh on the of Qusra. What followed was not an unforeseeable eruption of anger. Residents had been threatened, armed attackers arrived, and Palestinian families were left to confront the consequences. For the mayor, the losses were personal. "One of whom was my brother, my own brother" His brother Ibrahim, he explained, had eleven children. A younger family member, twenty-four years old and studying law, was engaged to be married. It is easy for the scale of Palestinian suffering to become obscured by numbers. Here, each number had a family attached to it: eleven children, a wedding that would never take place, an empty place at the table. The attacks continued. On April 13, 2024, roughly 180 to 200 armed Israelis descended on Qusra, burning agricultural buildings, homes, vehicles, and municipal property. Wadi described livestock killed and residents injured. "They burned houses that was already inhabited and houses that were under construction. They burned cars. They killed cows and sheep." Then he added: "And one of the injured was one of my own children." In August 2026, weeks before our visit, armed Israelis again attacked homes in Qusra. Reuters reported that dozens of masked attackers threw stones at a house while seven Palestinians were trapped inside. , Israeli forces subsequently fired tear gas into the home and detained its Palestinian occupants. The residents described being blindfolded, handcuffed, and beaten. The violence had moved from the agricultural hillsides to the thresholds of people's homes. The small outpost and the enormous territory it controls Driving toward Qusra, we passed Israeli settlements extending across the hilltops. Our Palestinian guide identified Shilo, Eli, and Ma'ale Levona, pointing toward agricultural land that Palestinian communities could no longer freely access. Geography is not only about what occupies a place. It is also about who has been excluded from it. Our guide pointed toward land associated with nearby Palestinian communities. "They've taken over the land." Later, explaining the restrictions on movement, he told us: "We're only using this road because it's the only road connecting between north and south." Palestinians could travel along the route, he explained, but entering the surrounding settlement areas was prohibited or dangerous. The road had become a narrow corridor through a landscape over which others exercised control. During our meeting in Qusra, a delegation member asked about the groups establishing themselves around Palestinian villages. Were these isolated attackers, or was there a larger structure behind the intimidation? The municipal representative rejected the language of isolated misconduct. "First of all, I consider the the settlers, who Netanyahu calls outlaws, rioters, we call them terrorists." The people burning homes, attacking farmers, and driving families from their land were not simply unruly neighbors. They were participating in a territorial campaign of terrorism and murder. He described armed groups supplied with vehicles, weapons, and equipment, establishing themselves near Palestinian agricultural land and extending their influence through intimidation. The result, he said, was the seizure of territory without the cost or visibility of a conventional military operation. This is the fundamental geography of the Israeli outpost system. A small number of structures can occupy a ridge while the armed men living there exercise control over an area many times larger. A Palestinian farmer may still possess a deed to the surrounding land, but that document offers little protection against someone waiting with a rifle. Israeli organization Peace Now documented the proliferation of outposts in Area B in 2026, demonstrating that the expansion was no longer confined to land already under full Israeli civil administration. described the establishment of outposts in territory formally assigned Palestinian civil authority. The spatial consequences are enormous. | | ---|---|--- Areas A and B are under the authority of democratically elected Palestinian local governments. The map above from Peace Now shows Area B illegal outposts built in 2025. An outpost need not occupy an entire hillside to make the hillside inaccessible. It need only make the consequences of entering sufficiently frightening. Once Palestinian farmers stop returning, the land becomes available for further encroachment. What looks on a map like a small point of occupation becomes, in practice, a much larger zone of exclusion. Land theft without paperwork A Palestinian representative from Turmus Ayya, whom we interviewed during the same trip, offered perhaps the clearest explanation of how this process works. He described olive groves that families still owned but could no longer safely enter. "There's no such thing as formally seized because they do not give you a notice. They do not tell you that this land has been seized." He called it: "de facto seizure by the conduct of the settlers." There is no necessary announcement, no document handed to the owner, no single moment at which the land officially changes hands. Instead, the farmer learns where he can no longer go. "You learn it. You become to learn it that this is a dangerous area. I I should not go there." This is an especially effective form of coercive territorial control because it requires relatively little continuous enforcement. Once people have been attacked, or have watched their neighbors attacked, the threat becomes embedded in their understanding of the landscape. The boundary is no longer simply a fence or checkpoint. It is fear. The farmer knows which road may be blocked, which grove may be watched, which hillside may conceal armed men. He adjusts his movements accordingly. His children learn the same geography. Eventually, the prohibited territory becomes abandoned: a place everyone knows belongs to the village, and everyone knows they must avoid. In geographic terms, legal ownership remains intact while practical access collapses. The occupation creates two overlapping maps: one of property and another of power. The second increasingly determines whether the first means anything. When the army arrives Another representative from Turmus Ayya also described how armed Israelis exploit military authority to remove Palestinians from their own land. He said attackers often approach in groups, with weapons displayed openly. They push or provoke Palestinian landowners while recording the confrontation on their phones. "They start pushing me, kicking me, you know, shouldering me, pushing me with their hands and with their phones." Then, he explained: "When I raise my hand, they call the IDF and claim that I attack them." Israeli soldiers then intervene against the Palestinian. "So they come and detain me and arrest me and take me somewhere so I can disappear for a week or two." He described being detained for four hours with his wife and a news crew and said the crew was instructed to erase its footage before being released. In October 2025, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs that armed Israelis, accompanied by Israeli forces, had prevented Palestinian farmers from reaching olive groves across several West Bank communities. In nearby Kobar, residents were required to seek permission from an outpost guard to access agricultural land that had previously been freely accessible. Elsewhere, armed Israelis seized harvested olives while farmers were prevented from working their land. This is a profound inversion of territorial authority. The Palestinian farmer becomes the person required to explain why he is present. The armed Israeli occupying or controlling the surrounding land becomes the person deciding whether he may stay. In Qusra, residents described the same inversion at their homes. The August 2026 documented allegations that Israeli forces detained Palestinians after armed Israelis attacked the house in which they had sought refuge. A system that repeatedly exposes Palestinian landowners to violence, detention, and exclusion while enabling armed groups to maintain territorial control cannot be understood simply through the language of sporadic criminality. Its effects are geographic, cumulative, and political. The olive harvest, interrupted The most revealing measure of Qusra's dispossession may be found not in a military map but in the village's olive oil production. A Qusra official reported that Qusra produced approximately 123 metric tons of olive oil in 2023, falling to 115 in 2024 and just 58 in 2025. For 2026, he anticipated only 16 to 20 metric tons. Qusra's disappearing olive harvest | | ---|---|--- Figures provided by Qusra municipal representatives during the September 2026 interview. If the projection holds, production will have fallen approximately 85% from its reported 2023 level. Olive trees naturally experience fluctuations in productivity. Rainfall, temperature, disease, and alternate-bearing cycles influence harvests. These figures alone cannot isolate the effects of violence from environmental variability. The interviews explain how farmers are being prevented from carrying out even the most basic agricultural work. Another official from Turmus Ayya described three essential periods of access: preparing the soil in February, clearing vegetation around the trees in August, and harvesting the olives in October and November. "But the biggest attacks occur during harvest itself, because there's a time limit in in which you can harvest." The timing matters. Olives cannot simply wait indefinitely for armed men to leave. Harvesting too late reduces quality and can destroy a season's economic value. For farmers already operating with narrow margins, missing the harvest may mean losing an entire year's income. He described how his household had once produced enough olive oil to give away to relatives and friends. Now, he said: "Right now, we buy our own. We have to go out and buy it." A family that once cultivated, pressed, consumed, and shared its own olive oil had become dependent on purchasing it. This is what agricultural dispossession looks like inside a household. Across the West Bank, the scale of the destruction is staggering. Israeli attacks resulting in casualties or property damage across more than 270 communities during 2025. During October and November alone, the agency recorded 178 attacks associated with the olive harvest across 88 communities. More than 6,000 trees and saplings were vandalized that year. | | ---|---|--- These figures do not capture every farmer who stayed home out of fear, every field that went untended, or every family that lost access to land without an incident recorded by international monitors. The ecological consequences may also outlast the immediate violence. Agricultural terraces require maintenance. Soil needs protection against erosion. Trees require pruning and care. Traditional agricultural systems are sustained by repeated human labor across generations. Denying farmers access to their land damages the relationship between people and the environment that makes cultivation possible. An olive tree may survive the attack. The agricultural system surrounding it may not. The disappearance of Area B Qusra's representatives described an increasingly aggressive expansion of armed Israeli activity from Area C into Area B, where Palestinians are formally assigned civil administrative authority under the Oslo framework. | | ---|---|--- Zones B (blue) surrounded by illegal Israeli outposts and settlements (red circles). Map current as of January 2026. " The violence and the intimidation have reached houses that fall in area B." Wadi described three families living in houses that had become effectively separated from the rest of the village. Armed Israelis, he said, had established tents near their homes, obstructed access roads, and interfered with essential services. "Electricity and water has been cut to some of the residents." The families included young children. The municipality could no longer reliably reach them with supplies. "It prevented us as a municipality and as a town from getting their needs of electricity, water, food, and supplies." This is more than land encroachment. It is the isolation of Palestinian families within their own community. The distinction between Areas A, B, and C was intended to define different administrative arrangements within an already illegal occupation. Yet the expansion of armed outposts and intimidation across those boundaries reveals how little protection such divisions provide when control over movement and security is exercised unequally. A family may live within an area designated for Palestinian civil administration and still be unable to receive water, electricity, or food from its own municipality. The boundary exists in law. It is disregarded in practice. The road that takes hours The geography of dispossession extends beyond farmland. Wadi described the closure of the village's main entrance since October 2023. The journey to Nablus, once approximately twenty minutes, could now take hours. "The passenger fare to get to Nablus used to be 8shekels. Now it's 22 shekels." | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Israeli gate closures cut off primary arteries connecting Palestinian towns, isolating them from each other. The cost of a journey had nearly tripled. The physical distance, of course, had not changed. This is the distinction between geometric distance and functional accessibility. Two communities may remain separated by only a few kilometers, yet checkpoints, roadblocks, military closures, and detours can make traveling between them exhausting, expensive, or impossible. The consequences ripple through daily life. A hospital becomes harder to reach. A farmer loses access to markets. A student spends hours traveling to school. Families become isolated from relatives living in neighboring villages. Wadi explained that visiting nearby Turmus Ayya could require planning an entire day. The roads still existed, but their purpose had been transformed. Rather than connecting Palestinian communities, they had become instruments through which access could be restricted and controlled. The geography of fear During our trip, we also interviewed a Palestinian journalist who described being attacked while reporting near Nablus. In one incident, she said armed Israelis fired live ammunition toward her and a colleague. In another, she was alone in a vehicle when armed men approached from a hillside. She fled. "The first thing I did is left the car, and I start running, run and run and start screaming to my colleague to hear me." She described how the terror continued long after the immediate danger had passed. "You don't discover it in the first days, but you have some trauma because you will dream" Yet she refused to abandon her work. "I will never give up." Her determination speaks to a broader reality: Palestinians are forced not only to survive the occupation but to document it, often at enormous personal risk. On October 6, 2026, AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh armed Israelis while covering violence against Palestinian olive farmers near Aqraba. His camera equipment was stolen, and he was hospitalized with injuries. The attack occurred near Israeli soldiers, who, according to witnesses, did not intervene. The risks facing journalists are part of the same landscape of intimidation confronting farmers and residents. The violence regulates who may enter a place, who may remain there, and who may record what happens. Fear becomes a method of territorial governance. The architecture of dispossession The processes unfolding around Qusra are consistent with decades of scholarship examining the spatial organization of Israeli occupation. In Ethnocracy: Land and Identity Politics in Israel/Palestine (2006), geographer Oren Yiftachel analyzes how territorial policies and unequal access to land can reproduce political domination. Eyal Weizman's Hollow Land: Israel 's Architecture of Occupation (2007) examines the ways settlements, roads, military installations, and planning systems reorganize Palestinian space. Both provide important frameworks for understanding why dispossession cannot be measured solely by the number of buildings constructed or acres formally confiscated. Territorial control is also exercised through . An armed outpost on a ridge can deny farmers access to surrounding valleys. A closed gate can separate a village from its regional economy. A blocked road can prevent a municipality from reaching families who live within its own boundaries. An attack during olive harvest can destroy a year's income without damaging a single property deed. The result is a landscape in which Palestinians may retain formal claims to land while losing the practical ability to inhabit and use it. The International Court of Justice's July 2024 advisory opinion found Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territory unlawful and addressed the legal consequences of settlement expansion, land appropriation, and discriminatory restrictions on Palestinians. placed these territorial practices within the broader framework of international law. The geography of Qusra reveals how such violations become part of ordinary life. The occupation is experienced not only through soldiers and weapons, but through the impossibility of reaching a field, the expense of traveling to a nearby town, and the uncertainty of whether a family can safely sleep in its own home. What remains of Qusra Toward the end of our meeting, Wadi returned to the contradiction between the language of democracy and human rights, and the conditions his community was enduring. He had described murdered relatives, destroyed farms, families isolated from their neighbors, and children living under armed intimidation. He was not asking us to imagine some distant political possibility. He was describing what it takes for a village to remain alive. A functioning community requires more than buildings and boundaries. It needs access to water, electricity, agricultural land, schools, hospitals, markets, and the surrounding landscape. It needs the freedom to move. It needs the ability to cultivate the soil and harvest what grows from it. And it needs the reasonable expectation that its residents can return home without being attacked. Qusra still possesses its name, its history, and its people. Its olive trees still stand on the hillsides. The agricultural terraces remain etched into the landscape. But those physical remnants conceal the destruction taking place around them. The land has not moved. The villages have not moved. The distances between them have not changed. What has changed is who can cross those distances, who can cultivate the fields, and who can live without fear. That is the geography of dispossession. It is not only the theft of Palestinian land. It is the deliberate destruction of the relationships between people and place that make a homeland possible. And in Qusra, the evidence is everywhere: in the groves left unharvested, the roads made impassable, the families trapped in their homes, and the names of the dead recited by a man who once would have welcomed visitors with stories about weddings and olive trees. Qusra remains on the map for now, but increased violence and land seizures may one day lead to its destruction. If you want to continue reading this series, please be sure to subscribe! # [Socialist France may beyond saving....because of socialism, says Economist who evangelized Socialism ](https://substack.com/redirect/4168bcd8-7d9e-4c8c-9185-594ae89d5bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

---|---|---
Paul Krugman **[warned that France may have grown too large for the European Central Bank to rescue,](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd77369-775d-470e-b346-4cd6d0f454f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as Sebastien Lecornu tries to pass a 2027 budget while migrant protests continue.
* **Ugly-crisis sketch** : Krugman wrote Thursday that a loss of confidence could replay 2009-2012, first Greece, then Portugal, Spain and Italy. He also flagged a relatively low retirement age as the population ages.
* **Draghi 's old bargain**: He said Draghi's 2012 pledge to do "whatever it takes" held partly because southern Europe made "massive spending cuts." Rescuing France would be "extremely expensive," and politically fraught.
* **Budget and the chart** : CNBC's chart shows the French 10-year at the highest level since 2002. Lecornu's 2027 budget seeks tens of billions of dollars in fiscal consolidation while students protest education underfunding.
* **Trichet 's condition**: Trichet said Friday, "The ball is in the camp of the French government and parliament," and "you first have to help yourself."

Grain Management is[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/94603c1a-ca19-4069-b159-52ea7d05557a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[selling SpaceX a nationwide 800 MHz license block,](https://substack.com/redirect/94603c1a-ca19-4069-b159-52ea7d05557a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/94603c1a-ca19-4069-b159-52ea7d05557a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)up to 14 megahertz paired, and **[the three national carriers sold off](https://substack.com/redirect/f475a9cf-63b4-481c-91e5-d12aeb7eca7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as Starlink Mobile aimed at indoor phone coverage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4168bcd8-7d9e-4c8c-9185-594ae89d5bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Price still undisclosed:** The package **[rumored to be $8 Billion](https://substack.com/redirect/5890ef5d-3988-4d58-91bf-48290a816d94?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** is up to 14 megahertz of paired licenses in the 800 MHz band. Neither side put a number on the sale, and the transfer still needs FCC approval.
* **Indoor reach is point:** SpaceX said the **[low-band layer will reach handsets through walls and buildings,](https://substack.com/redirect/6238ab28-d89e-44aa-a1ab-c6e3905cb6cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** paired with its satellite-to-mobile constellation, including dead zones. The FCC recently cleared 15,000 more next-generation Starlink satellites.
* **Musk calls it done:** Musk wrote that this is "the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America," and called the purchase a "very big deal." In August, COO Gwynne Shotwell said Starlink would build a terrestrial network and go after the big three's customers, with second-generation satellites in 2027.
* **Towers rose, carriers fell:** Crown Castle, American Tower and SBA Communications gained 8.2%, 6.4% and 5.6% respectively in premarket. Verizon is down 9%, AT&T nearly 10% and T-Mobile more than 13%.

# [Jet fuel up 62%. Delta's 2026 target just collapsed](https://substack.com/redirect/4168bcd8-7d9e-4c8c-9185-594ae89d5bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A $6 billion jump in the fuel bill forced Delta[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/2b842b20-c95a-4736-a18c-422dc141eff7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[to drop its 2026 profit range](https://substack.com/redirect/2b842b20-c95a-4736-a18c-422dc141eff7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to $5.10-$5.60 a share, the carrier's first estimate miss in two years, even as cabins stayed full.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4168bcd8-7d9e-4c8c-9185-594ae89d5bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Profit range cut sharply:** Adjusted full-year earnings were lowered to $5.10-$5.60 a share from July's $6.50-$7.50. Free cash flow was cut to $2.5 billion from as much as $4 billion.
* **First miss in years:** Adjusted earnings were $1.72 a share on $17.59 billion of revenue, versus $1.75 and $17.67 billion. Net income fell 47% to $756 million, or $1.15 a share, from $1.42 billion, or $2.17.
* **Cabins still filling up:** Premium revenue rose 18% to $6.82 billion. Main-cabin sales rose 12% to $6.8 billion. Fourth-quarter revenue is guided up 20%, above the third quarter's 16% adjusted gain, but the quarter's outlook is still below estimates.
* **Starlink snub still open:** Musk wrote last week that Ed Bastian would "lose his job over this" after a report that Bastian told staff, "We do not want to be with Elon Musk. Trust me." Bastian said "There's no tit-for-tat." Delta is adding Amazon Leo. United, American, Southwest and Alaska use Starlink for in flight wifi.

# [Apple slides 3% after cutting iPhone 18 Pro orders 15%](https://substack.com/redirect/4168bcd8-7d9e-4c8c-9185-594ae89d5bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Apple was down 3% at $331.22 Friday after Nikkei said **[October parts orders for both premium iPhone 18 models](https://substack.com/redirect/4f3528d3-fc25-4877-b8a5-b4404baecc23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** were cut 15% to 20%.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4168bcd8-7d9e-4c8c-9185-594ae89d5bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **October orders cut hard:** **[A Nikkei report](https://substack.com/redirect/d0fd4119-3605-41bf-ad98-e1d12e7ad623?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** said October parts orders for both premium models were cut at least 15% from the original plan, with one supply-chain executive putting the reduction at 15% to 20%. Skyworks slipped 2% to $78.95. Qualcomm rose 0.4% to $176.64.
* **Prices jumped a hundred:** The Pro starts at $1,199 and the Pro Max at $1,299, each $100 above the prior generation. One supply-chain source called the new handsets "just too expensive." The standard iPhone 18 is not due until spring 2027.
* **Analysts already flagged softness:** Bernstein's Mark Newman wrote Monday that U.S. Pro and Pro Max demand is down low single digits from a year ago, while China launch-week sales rose 12%. Jefferies' Edison Lee pointed to weak resale prices versus the 17 lineup.
* **Memory costs still rising:** Tim Cook said in July that "we see the market pricing for memory continuing to increase, which could drive an increasing impact on our business." Management has projected supply constraints will worsen in fiscal Q4 2026 across iPhone, Mac and iPad.

# ["Success is not villainy" Bezos says Socialism on the rise because of Econ 101](https://substack.com/redirect/4168bcd8-7d9e-4c8c-9185-594ae89d5bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Jeff Bezos told Bret Baier that **[socialism is gaining ground because](https://substack.com/redirect/462be0a3-fc30-4f79-b1d4-5ab4d46506db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** housing and other costs are genuinely high, and because politicians point at villains instead of supply.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4168bcd8-7d9e-4c8c-9185-594ae89d5bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Interview on factory floor:** Bezos spoke Wednesday on the Blue Origin Space Coast floor. The conversation aired on Special Report. He was asked what is pulling some voters toward socialism.
* **Housing called econ 101:** He said programs that "subsidize demand and constrain supply" produce high prices, and that blaming "greedy landlords" misses the cause. "Housing is a simple supply and demand situation. It's econ 101."
* **Austin as the counter:** Over the last 10 years, he said, Austin policies that made building easier have sent housing prices down. He argued the affordability problem is real and should not be waved off.
* **Success is not villainy:** "If there's a politician who's picking villains and pointing fingers, that probably means they don't have a solution." He rejected an oppressor-oppressed frame and said "Success is not villainy."

Bitcoin **[steadied near $82,500](https://substack.com/redirect/e0332181-121b-4d9f-aa88-f7feb06f4830?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Trump said the U.S. will not strike Iran before the Nov. 3 midterms. It is still down 2.2% this week, the weakest stretch since the week ended Sept. 11.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4168bcd8-7d9e-4c8c-9185-594ae89d5bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The Thursday post** : In a Truth Social post, Trump said the U.S. will not attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterms. Brent fell about 1.5% to around $103. Bitcoin was up 0.9% over 24 hours to $82,474.54.
* **Still a soft week** : The 2.2% weekly drop is the worst since the week ended Sept. 11, when Bitcoin fell 3.2%. Last week the coin hit $86,000 after Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson urged patience on rates.
* **Strategy and the brokers** : Strategy rose 2.2% premarket to $154.80 and is still on pace for its worst week since Sept. 11. Barclays raised that target to $175 from $160. Robinhood rose 1.7% to $108.82 and Coinbase 1.9%.
* **Targets moved up** : Morgan Stanley raised Robinhood to $160 from $150 and Coinbase to $258 from $250. Both broker stocks are still down on the week, Robinhood 3.5% and Coinbase 4.4%.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Bear with me for a moment
body:
I know we have what it takes to flip this seat – the right way.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&source=&t=1&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ) | | | |
---
Peter,
If your inbox looks anything like mine, you’re probably wading through a sea of fundraising emails from campaigns each time you check it – so I’m sorry for all we’re adding to the pile!
It can be tough to filter the truth from the noise and determine which causes are worth investing your time, attention and money into.
So please understand that I’m not exaggerating when I say I need your help now more than ever: **Our very last FEC campaign fundraising deadline before the election is five days away – the last chance we’ll have to show the strength of our grassroots campaign – and early in-person voting starts in North Carolina the very next day.**
[**_This deadline is a very real legal requirement for campaigns like ours, and just as big of a deal as we make it out to be, which is why I'm hoping you’ll chip in $5, or whatever you can today. Grassroots donations are the backbone of this movement, and yours will help ensure this public fundraising report demonstrates the true extent of our strength. So Peter – _what do you say?__**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&amount=5&t=8&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&amount=5&t=9&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ)
---
| | [DONATE $25](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&amount=25&t=10&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ)
---
| | [DONATE $50](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&amount=50&t=11&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ)
---
| | [OTHER AMOUNT](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&t=12&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ)
---
With just 25 days left in this race, we can’t afford to lose an ounce of momentum – and truth be told, that means sending you far more appeals over email and text than I would like.
**Because of the way MAGA politicians and the big-money interests behind them have upended our political landscape in the wake of Citizens United, I have no choice.**
I’m running a grassroots campaign in the race that will decide Senate control, so folks like you donating to messages like these are the only way I stand a chance against the GOP’s massive spending to defeat me.
They’ve already pummelled me with dark-money attacks on all fronts, and it’s worked pretty well so far: Over the last few months, our lead has tightened. The Whatley campaign attacks will increase in these last few weeks – and even more so if they detect any signs of weakness once our report goes live.
I know we have what it takes to flip this seat blue for the first time since 2008, and I’m determined to do it the right way. So Peter, I’m personally asking:
[**_Will you please consider chipping in $5 now to help us prove that no amount of money is enough to buy North Carolina’s seat (or Senate control) when we WIN on Election Day?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&amount=5&t=13&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ)
| | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&amount=5&t=14&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ)
---
Thanks for bearing with me, and everything else you do.
Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&t=2&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1579&source=&t=3&akid=4262%2E124072%2EnuavgJ)

Peter,
Let me lay this out, clear as day:
I am the _only_ Democratic Senator up for reelection in a state Trump won in 2024.
That makes me **MAGA’s #1 target.** They are going to do anything and everything to replace me with a MAGA puppet.
If you’re outraged by what’s happening to our country — and you’re ready to fight back — please rush $5 to my reelection campaign today.

And now, again, Peter, I need you with me.

subject: Final Volunteer Meetup — Let’s Knock Doors for Virginia!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY Virginia McIntyre for Congress
body:
Join us Sunday, October 11 at 6 PM for pizza, planning, and our final canvassing push.
|
---
# One Final Meetup.
Let’s Make Every Door Count!
Team McIntyre, we’re heading into the final weeks of the campaign, and **your time and energy can make a difference.** Join us on Sunday, October 11 for our **last volunteer meetup before Election Day!** We’ll get organized for the final canvassing push, coordinate door-knocking teams, and walk through the canvassing app so you feel ready to head out and talk with voters. **New to door-knocking? Come join us!** Whether you’re a longtime volunteer or getting involved for the first time, there’s a place for you on Team McIntyre. Bring your phone, your enthusiasm, and a friend who wants to help. | **Date:** Sunday, October 11 **Time:** 6:00 PM **Location:**
MCRC Headquarters
144 Metro Park, Suite 3
Rochester, NY 14623
---
**Pizza and beverages will be provided!**
Every door we knock and every conversation we have is an opportunity to introduce Virginia and hear what matters to our neighbors. **Even a few hours of your time can help us reach more voters.**
Let’s turn our enthusiasm into action and finish strong together. We look forward to seeing you Sunday!
Questions? Contact the campaign:
**Email:** [info@virginiamcintyreforcongress.com](mailto:info@virginiamcintyreforcongress.com)
**Phone:** [(585) 519-5297](tel:5855195297)

Case File No DRT-ED-STRIKE · Special File · The Quiet Edge
The Headlines Show the Fires. The Real Story Is the American Technology Guiding the Drones.
Ukraine says its strikes have knocked out half of Russia’s refining capacity. Russian diesel output is down about 30%. Behind the drones sits a layer of intelligence, mapping and AI, much of it American, that rarely gets discussed.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Every few days now, another Russian refinery goes up in flames, sometimes more than 2,000 kilometers from the front line. The coverage focuses on the fires: the drones, the targets, the damage. Much less is said about how a country with no long-range air force keeps finding its way through some of the densest air defenses on earth.
The evidence board
| | What the Strikes Have Done
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the scale.** Russian refineries were hit at least 194 times in the first half of 2026, an 11-fold jump from a year earlier, per Rochan Consulting. May set a monthly record with 16 successful strikes.
| CHATTER
---
**Exhibit B — the claim.** On October 4, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said the strikes had disabled 51% of Russia’s refining capacity. The figure couldn’t be independently verified.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the damage.** The IEA says Russian diesel output has fallen about 30%, with some drivers waiting up to 40 hours for fuel. The Kremlin banned diesel exports. Putin said the strikes cost Russia about 1% of GDP.
The quiet part
| | Where the Edge Comes From
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
In July, the Financial Times reported that U.S. intelligence helped Ukraine “chart the best paths” for its drones and “skirt air defences.” CBS reported that an American-made reconnaissance drone uses AI software to plan routes around known Russian air-defense sites, and has helped locate S-400 batteries.
| OUR THEORY
---
The drones are mostly Ukrainian-built. The intelligence, mapping and AI that guide them are increasingly American. That shifts modern warfare: the deciding edge is no longer how many missiles you own, but whose software decides where they fly.
Decoder
| | The One-Word Admission
---|---
| | “Partially.”— Vladimir Putin, asked on October 1 whether Ukraine’s refinery strikes had achieved their goal
---|---
What it says
The strikes have had some effect.
What it means
**Our theory:** leaders at war rarely admit damage at all. A one-word “partially,” along with a 1% hit to GDP and a diesel export ban, says the strikes are working. Even Washington has reportedly asked Kyiv, in September, to ease off the refineries, because they’ve become effective enough to move global diesel prices. The technology behind that effectiveness is now among the most valuable in defense.
Winners & losers
| | Who Gains From the New Way of War
---|---
| | WINNING
---
Defense software and AI
Targeting, route planning and electronic-warfare tools are now the edge.
| | WINNING
---
Fuel refiners outside Russia
Every Russian barrel not refined tightens global diesel supply.
| | LOSING
---
Traditional air defenses
Expensive systems are being outmaneuvered by cheap drones with smart guidance.
| ClassificationTransition
---
Wars used to be won by whoever had more hardware. In Ukraine, the edge increasingly comes from intelligence, AI and software, much of it American. The companies supplying it rarely make the headlines. Their technology is in the middle of the most-watched strikes in the world.
| The riddle · answer at the end of the fileA drone costs a fraction of a missile, yet it’s getting past air defenses worth hundreds of millions. What’s actually doing the work?
---
|
---
Riddle answer
**The software.** Cheap drones get through because something tells them exactly where the defenses are and how to fly around them. **Our theory:** in modern war, the most valuable technology isn’t what explodes. It’s what decides the route, and that’s where defense spending is heading next.

Peter, In politics, a lot of people think that the most important members of the team are the ones who write the biggest checks. That’s certainly how our opponent, Mike Lawler, operates. But we don’t do things that way. This is fundamentally a grassroots campaign, powered by tens of thousands of donations of $5, $10, or even $50 at a time. This is a team of ordinary people who are standing up to take back our country. According to our records, you haven’t made a donation yet. Today, we’re asking you to join that group in the arena. Cait’s coming up on her final legally mandated FEC deadline in just a few days, and we have some ambitious goals to hit before then. So we’re asking, very respectfully: [**Can you please make a donation to help Cait Conley beat Mike Lawler and flip NY-17? The amount doesn’t matter as much as the donation itself. Case File No DRT-ED-CAPE · Special File · One Number
One Number Has Warned Before Every Great Crash. It’s Now the Second-Highest in 150 Years.
The Shiller CAPE ratio stands at about 41, higher than before the 1929 crash and just below the dot-com peak. Ten stocks make up 37.8% of the market, and rates are above 5%. The AI boom may be real. The price is the problem.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Forget the headlines for a minute. Forget the AI demos, the record earnings calls and the trillion-dollar valuations. If you could look at just one number to judge how risky the stock market is right now, the one with the longest track record would tell you something most investors don’t want to hear.
The number
| | One Stat, 150 Years of History
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**The Shiller CAPE ratio** compares stock prices to ten years of inflation-adjusted earnings, which smooths out booms and busts. Its long-run average since 1881 is about 17. In early October 2026, it stood at about 41.
| 1929, before the crashCAPE about 32The Dow then lost close to 90%.
---
| Late 1999, dot-com peakCAPE 44.2The S&P; 500 lost 49% over the next two and a half years.
---
| TodayCAPE about 41The second-highest reading in more than 150 years.
---
The evidence board
| | What Sits Behind the Number
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Concentration.** The ten largest stocks make up 37.8% of the S&P; 500, mostly AI leaders.
| EVIDENCE
---
**History.** When the CAPE has been above 30, the following ten years have historically averaged under 4% a year, versus roughly 11% for all rolling ten-year periods since 1939. Robert Shiller has said readings like this “predict below-average returns over the following decade.”
| EVIDENCE
---
**Cost of money.** Unlike in 1999, rates aren’t falling. The 10-year Treasury yield is above 5%, near its highest since the early 2000s, which makes expensive stocks harder to justify.
Decoder
| | What the Bulls Say, and Why It Matters
---|---
| | “The companies are actually profitable this time.”— The most common defense of today’s valuations
---|---
What it says
This isn’t 1999, because AI leaders make real money.
What it means
**Our theory:** partly true, and the CAPE already accounts for it, because it measures price against real earnings. A great company can still be a bad investment at the wrong price. In 2000, Cisco, Microsoft and Intel were hugely profitable too. It took Cisco more than two decades to get back to its old high.
| ClassificationPressure
---
One number doesn’t predict the day of a crash. But it has rarely been this high, and every time it got close, investors who prepared did far better than those who didn’t. The question isn’t whether AI is real. It’s what you’re paying for it.
| The riddle · answer at the end of the fileIf the CAPE was this high only once before in 150 years, why do so many investors ignore it?
---
|
---
Riddle answer
**Because it’s bad at timing and good at warning.** The CAPE can stay high for years while prices keep rising, and people who sell early look wrong for a long time. **Our theory:** it isn’t a signal to panic. It’s a signal to have a plan for protecting your money before the market forces the decision.

### About Nellie Pou

### An explicit text, a guilty verdict, and a power dynamic we shouldn't ignore.
Today I want to talk about the telecommunications harassment case involving Ohio state Senator Jerry Cirino and [D.J. Byrnes](https://open.substack.com/users/737165-dj-byrnes?utm_source=mentions) , better known as [The Rooster](https://open.substack.com/pub/rooster?utm_source=mentions) . I was at the trial on day one and watched the livestream on day two. The Rooster was found guilty and received a $200 fine plus court costs.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..m3984Go6UOWgGI5XDuHDr2upuhwhNIoTBzoRcLEf-54?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=219625971)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..m3984Go6UOWgGI5XDuHDr2upuhwhNIoTBzoRcLEf-54?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=219625971)

---|---|---
The Rooster (DJ Byrnes)
I'm not going to explain every detail here. I covered both days over at my other publication, [The Angry Ohioan](https://open.substack.com/pub/theangryohioan?utm_source=mentions) where I focus exclusively on Ohio news. You can read the two-day write-up here:
The Angry Ohioan
[The Rooster Trial: Day One](https://substack.com/redirect/d62ec02f-967a-4529-a85b-16dc78c248d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Today was the first day of D.J. Byrnes's The Rooster telecommunications harassment trial involving Ohio state Senator Jerry Cirino. Byrnes is better known as the Rooster, and I decided to show up at Willoughby Municipal Court in solidarity. This is my firsthand account...
[Read more](https://substack.com/redirect/d62ec02f-967a-4529-a85b-16dc78c248d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
19 hours ago * 5 likes * 4 comments * The Angry Democrat
The Angry Ohioan
[GUILTY. The Rooster Trial Day Two](https://substack.com/redirect/66df758c-63ef-4df6-b086-a9241864f7a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The second and final day of D.J. Byrnes's telecommunications harassment trial concluded with a guilty verdict. Byrnes, better known as the Rooster, was found guilty in the case involving Ohio state Senator Jerry Cirino and received a very minimal sentence: a $200 fine plus court costs...
[Read more](https://substack.com/redirect/66df758c-63ef-4df6-b086-a9241864f7a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
2 hours ago * 1 like * The Angry Democrat and Matt Diemer
I think this case deserves a conversation in **The Angry Democrat** because it raises questions that go beyond Ohio. What text messages are acceptable to send to someone? Does the answer change when the recipient is a public official? Is this a freedom of speech and freedom of the press conversation, or is it harassment?
Before you read my take, keep three questions in mind:
1. **Do you agree with the guilty verdict? Why or why not?**
2. **Would your answer change if the same image had been sent to a female elected official, whether the sender was a man or a woman?**
3. **Do you think this was a sitting state senator flexing his power against the media?**

There is a lot of disagreement about this case. Some people are absolutely convinced this was protected speech. Others think it crossed the line. Here's where I landed...

Greg Abbott continues to launch attack ads spreading lies about me and my voting record, but I'm fighting back with the truth: I'm running to put money back into your pocket because Greg Abbott has been giving your money away to his corrupt donors.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ed09bee8-e99e-4fc9-bce3-b31e1acc18f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**The fact of the matter is property taxes have risen over 85% under Greg Abbott. He scammed $1 billion out of public schools. And he sold Texas landowners out to big data centers. I 've never voted to create an income tax in Texas, but I have voted to pay teachers more, expand access to healthcare, and put an end to our rising electric bill.**
If that sounds like the kind of values you'd want in a leader, then I'm your candidate. We all deserve a chance at achieving the American Dream. My plan as your next Governor of Texas is simple: I want to put money back in your pocket, save our neighborhood schools, and end the political corruption running rampant in our state -- it's not radical, it's common sense.
**[We're 10 days away from early voting, and we're knocking on doors, connecting with voters, and putting ads on air to beatback Greg Abbott's lies. But that requires money that I don't have. Ninety-five percent of the money I have raised comes from small dollar donations from people like you who remain committed to fighting for change in Texas. But we need to double down. If you believe Texas deserves new leadership and a governor who will fight for the needs of everyday Texans, will you please chip in $5 or whatever you can today -- even a dollar makes a difference -- to help us beat Abbott this November?](https://substack.com/redirect/ebd0f636-e57d-4b95-bfa5-ab406ab6f6db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE NOW ->](https://substack.com/redirect/ebd0f636-e57d-4b95-bfa5-ab406ab6f6db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And if Abbott wants to clear anything up, I'm ready when he is. I've called for a public debate, but he refuses to accept the challenge because he knows he'd have to defend a record that has left Texans behind while he's lined his pockets.
I'm running because Texans deserve a governor who they can trust and will put their interests first.
Let's get Greg Abbott out of the Governor's mansion.
-- Gina

clean_body: | = There's something you should know about EMILYs List, Peter: We don't wait for the rest of the political establishment to decide a race is worth winning before we back candidates. We look at the races that others are overlooking. We back Democratic pro-choice women who have what it takes to win, even when the national spotlight is somewhere else. And we believe in those women from the very beginning. That's exactly what we did with three extraordinary women running in the South this November: Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia's governor's race. Tanya Miller in Georgia's attorney general race. Nancy Lacore in South Carolina's 1st Congressional District. = Peter, we understand why so much of the national conversation is focused on a handful of high-profile races. But if donors only invest in the races everyone is already talking about, we're going to miss opportunities to build power in places where we've needed it for decades — and where we have the chance to make meaningful gains for Democrats. Georgia. South Carolina. States where Republicans have spent years consolidating power, restricting voting rights, and counting on Democrats to concede the fight before it even begins. We refuse to do that. That's why we were with Keisha, Tanya, and Nancy from the beginning. It's why we're still fighting for them today. But we cannot do this alone. Peter, **Yesterday, in a LIVE debate, the moderator asked Becca and her Republican opponent about the war in Iran, and things got interesting fast. 👀** The moderator noted that Congress has held **20** war powers votes since the war began, and that diesel in Vermont is now **$6.38** a gallon, up from under **$4** just a year ago. Becca said what she hears from farmers and small business owners all over the state is that the war is driving up fuel costs, and it has to end. She called it an illegal and unwarranted war, and reminded everyone that SHE brought a war powers resolution to the House floor back in April. **Then the moderator asked her opponent a simple question: would you have voted yes or no on the War Powers Resolution?** Her opponent’s answer: _**"I don't know exactly what that War Powers Resolution is."**_ The moderator asked again for a yes or no, explaining it would effectively take away President Trump's ability to continue military action in Iran without congressional approval...and he still couldn’t give an answer. **HARD YIKES. 😬** [_**If you're proud of Becca for standing strong instead of lying down like this administration would prefer, click here and chip in $5, $15, or even $25 today to keep her swinging!**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141056852/652383134/-744812874?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZjhiZTkzNi0xNGM0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_5ONuFBmg-QFg8OEjhW-rscpG6DuTWIBCQA9q8xs2dU=) **[SHOW BECCA YOU'RE PROUD!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141056853/652383135/-744812874?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZjhiZTkzNi0xNGM0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_5ONuFBmg-QFg8OEjhW-rscpG6DuTWIBCQA9q8xs2dU=)** The war wasn't the only place the two of them split. On healthcare, the moderator pointed out that Vermonters pay some of the highest premiums in the country. Becca said rural hospitals tell her it's Medicaid that keeps their doors open, and that the $1 trillion cut to Medicaid in the Republican tax bill has made things worse, with tens of thousands of Vermonters facing the loss of their healthcare. | | The House of Representatives passed the SAVE America Act to permanently secure our elections by: >> Requiring physical proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote; >> Aggressively purging noncitizens from registration lists; and >> Holding lawless bureaucrats criminally accountable. **But now, the bill is sitting on a shelf in the Senate.** As Senate Majority Leader, Republican Senator John Thune holds the absolute power to set the calendar and schedule the vote. **Instead of using every legislative tool available to put this bill on President Trump’s desk, leadership is letting the clock run out.** With the pivotal November elections right around the corner, we are completely out of time for political games. If the Senate does not act immediately, our election infrastructure remains wide open to mass vulnerabilities at the exact moment the country can least afford it. | | Hey Patriot,
---
Here’s the rundown.
September was our busiest and best month yet.
More doors knocked. More relationships built. More ballots chased. More momentum than we’ve **_ever had in a single month_**.
And because of that success, we’ve burned through our financial resources faster than planned.
**[We _cannot_ run out of money to keep ballot chasers on the ground at the worst possible time in this election cycle.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12071101/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfbXQtb3RvY2hfYnJfMjAyNjEwMDIv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjEwMDk/LbmNsYmdCU2xiYg/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM2ODhfd3I0JmFtb3VudD0xMDA/gask-zA/sav3eb48711)**

[KEEP BALLOT CHASERS WORKING](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12071101/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfbXQtb3RvY2hfYnJfMjAyNjEwMDIv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjEwMDk/LbmNsYmdCU2xiYg/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM2ODhfd3I0JmFtb3VudD0xMDA/gask-zA/sav3eb48711)

You’re one of Turning Point’s most dedicated supporters. When the rest of the list goes quiet, folks like you step up.
That’s why I’m reaching out to you directly.
Charlie Kirk built this movement from the ground up. He believed in the power of everyday patriots showing up, knocking on doors, and changing the direction of this country one conversation at a time. We lost him, but we are still carrying his torch.
**[Right now we need 500 ballot chasers](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12071101/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfbXQtb3RvY2hfYnJfMjAyNjEwMDIv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjEwMDk/LbmNsYmdCU2xiYg/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM2ODhfd3I0JmFtb3VudD0xMDA/gask-zA/sav3eb48711)** funded and deployed in the 8 critical states we have to win this midterm cycle.
These are the states that will decide whether we hold Congress or watch it slip away.
If we hit that number and keep the ground game funded, we have a real fighting chance. We can keep radical “**democratic socialists** ” — actual communists in all but name — out of power.
If we fail, we lose the majority. President Trump becomes a lame-duck president. We get more of the same disastrous policies. And for all practical purposes, the fight is over.
**This is it. This is the biggest moment in recent political history.**
We need patriots on the pavement right now. We need the resources to train them, equip them, and keep them in the field while early voting ramps up.
**[Help us keep Charlie’s mission alive and turn September’s momentum into November’s victory.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12071101/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfbXQtb3RvY2hfYnJfMjAyNjEwMDIv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjEwMDk/LbmNsYmdCU2xiYg/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM2ODhfd3I0JmFtb3VudD0xMDA/gask-zA/sav3eb48711)**
_Every dollar goes directly to training and deploying ballot chasers in the states that matter most._

[KEEP THE TORCH BURNING](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12071101/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfbXQtb3RvY2hfYnJfMjAyNjEwMDIv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjEwMDk/LbmNsYmdCU2xiYg/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM2ODhfd3I0JmFtb3VudD0xMDA/gask-zA/sav3eb48711)

We are out of runway. The only thing standing between us and a radical takeover is the ground game Charlie believed in — and the patriots willing to fund it right now.
**[Please don’t sit this one out.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12071101/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfbXQtb3RvY2hfYnJfMjAyNjEwMDIv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjEwMDk/LbmNsYmdCU2xiYg/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM2ODhfd3I0JmFtb3VudD0xMDA/gask-zA/sav3eb48711)**
For Charlie. For our country. For the America we still believe in.

Tyler Bowyer
Executive Director, Turning Point PAC

[KEEP THE TORCH BURNING](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12071101/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfbXQtb3RvY2hfYnJfMjAyNjEwMDIv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjEwMDk/LbmNsYmdCU2xiYg/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM2ODhfd3I0JmFtb3VudD0xMDA/gask-zA/sav3eb48711)

As permitted by law, TPPAC, Inc. maintains a non-contribution account for the purpose of influencing federal, state, and local elections. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, address, occupation, and employer of individuals whose contribution exceeds $200 in an election cycle. For contributions from federal committees, corporations, and labor unions - regardless of contribution amount - federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the committee’s name and address. State and local law may require us to collect and report additional information.

Contributions to this account may be used to influence federal elections by making independent expenditures in support of or in opposition to federal candidates. Additionally, in state and local jurisdictions that permit non-individual type (e.g., corporate) contributions directly to candidates and/or committees, contributions to this account may be used for both independent expenditures and direct contributions to candidates and/or committees, as permitted by state and local law.

Individuals, federal committees, corporations, and labor unions may contribute to TPPAC, Inc.’s non-contribution account without limit. Contributions by national banks, foreign nationals (without lawful permanent resident status), and other foreign entities (e.g., foreign corporations) are prohibited. Contributions to TPPAC, Inc.’s non-contribution account are not tax-deductible for federal income tax purposes.

**I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents.**

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home.

I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country.

After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser.

I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first.

Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors.

**I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country.**

Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump?

For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening.

But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question:

Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous?

In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public.

I was terrified.

I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence.

But silence costs more.

So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat.

Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue.

I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first.

Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences.

**That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild.**

Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him.

They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts.

It MUST reach the ballot box.

It MUST be organized.

And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power.

clean_body: Then I went public.| | | | = I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents. I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home. I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country. After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents. Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser. I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first. Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors. I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country. Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump? For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening. But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question: Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous? In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public. I was terrified. I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence. But silence costs more. So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat. Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue. I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first. Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences. That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild. Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him. They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts. It MUST reach the ballot box. It MUST be organized. And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power. = | | | = MAGA wants us exhausted. Minnesota has tried one-party control for 20 years, and here's where that got us:
At least $9 billion in fraud and stolen taxpayer money, rising crime, and failing schools.
They are going 100 miles per hour in the wrong direction.
Peggy Flanagan, a failed career politician who enabled the policies that got us here. Her way doesn't work. And yet we've been paying Peggy Flanagan with our hard-earned money for 20 years.
It's not the time to give her a promotion. It's time to fire her for good.
Right now, the "expert" pollsters say she has the edge in this race, but it's a toss-up that could come down to a few hundred votes on election night. Not only is Peggy as extreme as they come, but she was also Tim Walz's running mate.
She was the sitting Lieutenant Governor during the largest COVID-19 scam in the country - the Feeding Our Future scandal. She's done everything possible to distance herself from this debacle, and so far it's worked!
We can't let all the rampant, unprecedented fraud that took place under her watch go unnoticed. It's a national disgrace. That's why Tim Walz was forced to end his re-election campaign... Meanwhile, his right hand wants to be our next U.S. Senator.

ICE shoots another father. | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSkvWspXpNzcqkzSIoupdDWkL2pjwIimGUsMZ1ZguqiawQwc8Iht3aCrkdXpsjBpSLw1ZyD5bxKE_JcgYrCqbqGXOstTN9WZ65Qe2cHDjUvyhyrf3SY8s2AkAfLtVu9MIBXHg-IVyAA3pHLOvfk3OLxsTcegLeDoJXD4pTQiiFz0CPU_EfcaE6cZ9swKKoakfSY_uP40JT7zL7F8Qtn71_Yy_aU8gIREe4pNXVqUpHI-qcafbhZh2mINjzoOieveIUEu-sG2UXgB4nzhv7fm8v6YEWxjdB3H3SbSd8MSUlPUw/4uq/_jF_sl4rQb-Poaw4hqf18g/h0/h001.E410dPMKJykkcfsjeAKABbt1In7NthenouG8mtwzx7o)
---
Peter, Another ICE shooting. I wrote those words three weeks ago and here I am writing them again. Last night federal agents disguised in construction vests and face masks, hiding every marking that would identify them as law enforcement, fired seven rounds into a parked car in New York City with a 5-year-old boy in the back seat. Seven rounds. Into a car with a kindergartner inside. His father took a bullet to the neck and the child watched his dad slump in his seat. That child will be traumatized by what happened last night for the rest of his life, and the agency that did it to him spent today congratulating itself for a "targeted enforcement operation." [**This madness continues under Keith Self, or it stops under us and a Democratic majority. Chip in and help us win the power to rein in this rogue agency.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt83hdERQW2FFZP7A4JU-Z4L5R9x5e4NmSmFBFDt7R6jsHF7PownsRwrMu_Mv2Ly9jE0u2t9FUPYNllAPT3yJvkkjhlTjBRSagYmKjJ-e5U7afPQLeHSKrd1UjGs79EhjHUytcClMSS9QARq0RYjV6DiyvFCBIwEWm-6_J6EDTOJc5C2hAViT_cizS87ohKlxphZxVinuNoq5EFgLwIzR5S6J3egDFuDN27HNwwPdDBs2S1F7J8wBfP93hfc2tDqb0o7Bd4dk4ZV9HKnpIFKno-MNUImVl-7QYtLNIbwu7CadRp-8oLSi0ea7xtjn0K2g0HmKEyG21GWJy4FmZbfdL0v1YObJTFFL6MC1YYi2psqZ9/4uq/_jF_sl4rQb-Poaw4hqf18g/h1/h001.ezFyhKxk1qvxEqtVPb_7R9MW40TjMwO5Z7J75EgfgjI) Photos from the scene clearly show bullet entry holes from multiple sides of the vehicle - including 3 fired into the rear passenger side with a child in the back.

And just when you thought this agency had hit bottom, the sickening cover-up began.
When Congressman Adriano Espaillat showed up to see him, the guards at his door refused.
The father they shot got a few hours in the hospital before agents put him in an unmarked vehicle and sped away – apparently striking a bystander pushing his bike in the process.
---

---
This is how they handled Wilber Rafael Garces Perez in Austin three weeks ago, too.
He got shot, his wife got stonewalled, and he got moved to a detention site before anyone could question him.
Americans are sick of this.
Sick of the masks, sick of the gunfire on residential streets, sick of children in the line of fire.
And it is all deliberate.
When a contractor offered to build humane detention facilities, officials relayed that Stephen Miller flatly refused, he did not want humane. He wanted these facilities to be as inhumane as possible. Because the cruelty is the point.
---

---
Now agents reportedly have orders to drive arrest numbers higher as the election closes in.
This is a personal enforcement squad for the most corrupt president in American history, run by an administration stocked with crooks and war criminals.
I spent 20 years defending the land of the free, alongside men and women who gave everything for those words. Many of those who served with me came to this country as immigrants themselves, or were the children of immigrants. They sacrificed as much as any of us, and some gave their very lives in defense of our freedom.
