clean_body: ICE shoots another father. | | Peter, Another ICE shooting. I wrote those words three weeks ago and here I am writing them again. Last night federal agents disguised in construction vests and face masks, hiding every marking that would identify them as law enforcement, fired seven rounds into a parked car in New York City with a 5-year-old boy in the back seat. Seven rounds. Into a car with a kindergartner inside. His father took a bullet to the neck and the child watched his dad slump in his seat. That child will be traumatized by what happened last night for the rest of his life, and the agency that did it to him spent today congratulating itself for a "targeted enforcement operation." Photos from the scene clearly show bullet entry holes from multiple sides of the vehicle - including 3 fired into the rear passenger side with a child in the back. | And just when you thought this agency had hit bottom, the sickening cover-up began. When Congressman Adriano Espaillat showed up to see him, the guards at his door refused. The father they shot got a few hours in the hospital before agents put him in an unmarked vehicle and sped away – apparently striking a bystander pushing his bike in the process. | This is how they handled Wilber Rafael Garces Perez in Austin three weeks ago, too. He got shot, his wife got stonewalled, and he got moved to a detention site before anyone could question him. Americans are sick of this. Sick of the masks, sick of the gunfire on residential streets, sick of children in the line of fire. And it is all deliberate. When a contractor offered to build humane detention facilities, officials relayed that Stephen Miller flatly refused, he did not want humane. He wanted these facilities to be as inhumane as possible. Because the cruelty is the point. | Now agents reportedly have orders to drive arrest numbers higher as the election closes in. This is a personal enforcement squad for the most corrupt president in American history, run by an administration stocked with crooks and war criminals. I spent 20 years defending the land of the free, alongside men and women who gave everything for those words. Many of those who served with me came to this country as immigrants themselves, or were the children of immigrants. They sacrificed as much as any of us, and some gave their very lives in defense of our freedom. Masked agents shooting fathers in front of their sons spits in the face of every sacrifice we made. I will not stand for it, and neither should you. This election is a referendum on whether or not this chaos and violence continues. Keith Self and Ken Paxton have proven time and time again they are professional doormats for Trump. Hand them two more years and they will call it a mandate for more. Hey y'all,
I always say that potholes don't have partisan labels. Nobody driving over one cares whether a Democrat or a Republican fills it. They just want it fixed.
Over the past two years as mayor, we paved 31.5 miles of streets in Columbia, the most miles in any two-year period in our city's history. We planned carefully, we worked together, and we got it done. All without property tax increases and while balancing the budget.
That's the same approach I'll take to Congress. Staying focused on the problems that actually affect people's lives, and working with anyone who's serious about solving them. Not partisan theater. Not scoring points online. Just results.
TN-05 deserves a congressman who shows up and gets things done, just as I have for eight years as Columbia's mayor.

In the shadow of the Maine Senate debate Thursday night, the three contenders in Maine's gubernatorial election -- Republican Robert "Bobby" Charles, Democrat Hannah Pingree, and unaffiliated candidate Rick Bennett -- squared off in a lower key debate that hinged on the same question:
Who is to blame for everything getting worse in Maine while Gov. Janet Mills (D) was governor, Troy Jackson was Senate President, and Pingree was Mills' top policy guru?
For Charles, the answer was obvious. He spent Thursday's gubernatorial debate asking why Mainers should trust Pingree to fix the government she helped run as the chief policy architect of Mills' administration.
"It's like inviting the arsonist back to put out the fire," Charles said. "It makes no sense whatsoever to put us in a position where all the bad policies are just compounded again."
We can't arrest the frauds, but we can expose them. Sign up for The Robinson Report today!
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..MnwTeEdtTAaD4sKQG1CVwD_BKI5pDUuUIsDIIBRHQSE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=219430542)
Pingree, a former Maine House speaker who led Mills' Office of Policy Innovation and the Future, defended her work on housing and energy while repeatedly blaming President Donald Trump for making Maine's problems worse.
With the state of Maine facing a $1.3 billion forecasted budget shortfall, the [4th-highest electricity rates in the country](https://substack.com/redirect/9c6c8fa0-ae3e-4155-9790-268b662b9320?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), some of the highest [health insurance costs](https://substack.com/redirect/e3003d31-548c-4f57-b25d-31bb79c117ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and welfare dependency rates in the U.S., and rampant [welfare fraud, waste, and abuse](https://substack.com/redirect/3582de19-8572-4081-b363-0e02b3aa8dd9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), you would expect anyone even partially responsible for the policies that created the present Maine malaise to be laughed out of the governor's race.
Instead, Pingree -- the daughter of Democratic U.S. Rep. Chellie Pingree (ME-CD1) -- has led the three-person race in virtually every public opinion poll.
Charles emerged victorious from a competitive GOP primary field, but did not receive a warm post-victory embrace from his former Republican opponents, whereas Pingree, who only defeated former Maine CDC Director Nirav Shah thanks to the Ranked Choice Voting innovation, quickly enjoyed broad support from her former rivals.
On the margins of the partisan contest, former Republican State Sen. Rick Bennett, of Oxford, has waged a quixotic independent campaign that started when he cast [a few high-profile votes in the State Legislature](https://substack.com/redirect/7e98088d-48ad-4947-93df-292b2fdc7a61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), joining left-wing extremists on the wildly unpopular side of hot-button issues.
Bennett joined Charles in condemning Augusta's spending habits.
"The dirty truth is that nobody is minding the store," Bennett said.
But he sided with Pingree on keeping MaineCare expansion -- the single largest driver of Maine's ever-expanding budget binges.
Bennett also staked out a far-left position on illegal immigration enforcement, voicing support for the state retaining restrictions on cooperation with federal immigration agents.
The debate at Husson University's Gracie Theatre in Bangor, hosted by the taxpayer-subsidized Maine Public with NEWS CENTER Maine and the Portland Press Herald, exposed how much the exploding cost of living is driving every campaign's strategy.
Much as [the other debate Thursday night between U.S. Senator Susan Collins (R) and Democratic candidate Troy Jackson](https://substack.com/redirect/9c6c8fa0-ae3e-4155-9790-268b662b9320?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) focused on laying blame for the rising expenses crushing Mainers' checking accounts, so too was the gubernatorial debate a contest over who could convince voters that they have ideas that can ease the heavy burden of higher prices for, well, everything. Except maybe cannabis.
Charles called for cutting at least $1 billion from the budget, freezing state hiring, eliminating unfilled positions, ending subsidies and reviewing state spending from the ground up. He also promised to abolish the office Pingree ran.
"We're going to reduce the overall budget by reducing the fraud, and we now know from both federal investigations and state investigations we have major fraud," he said.
The state's oversight failures have already produced bills taxpayers may have to cover.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..MnwTeEdtTAaD4sKQG1CVwD_BKI5pDUuUIsDIIBRHQSE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=219430542)
Rather than investigate and prosecute welfare fraudsters, the Mills Administration snuck [a last-minute provision through the legislature](https://substack.com/redirect/91cf4857-bc5d-4f53-a6a7-68af8fb8de03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that would put Maine taxpayers on the hook if the Trump administration managed to defund MaineCare scammers.
A federal audit of MaineCare services for children with autism estimated [at least $45.6 million in improper payments in 2023](https://substack.com/redirect/5f21b401-047a-4ce4-91dd-e6e2a20e6787?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Every one of the 100 sampled enrollee-months contained at least one improper or potentially improper payment. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' inspector general recommended that Maine return approximately $28.7 million in federal funds. Those are findings of improper payments, not a determination that every dollar was obtained through criminal fraud.
Separately, DHHS records examined by The Robinson Report in April showed Gateway Community Services had repaid about $118,432 against more than $1.6 million in alleged overbilling. The records show that Gateway isn't the only Medicaid provider that is delinquent in repaying improperly claimed taxpayer resources.
The Mills Administration did [shut off funding for Gateway in December 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/b1dd674a-e79c-45b9-8ea0-b75a9d2a691d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but no charges have been filed against ex-CEO Abdullahi Ali, a Somali-American refugee with close ties to the Mills Administration and Democratic Party operatives.
Bennett proposed an inspector general's office reporting directly to the governor to investigate misspending and possible corruption. He also accused the executive and legislative branches of allowing spending to expand without adequate scrutiny.
"So we are spending in the state government well beyond the means of Mainers to pay," he said. "That's the reality."
Pingree's response to the budget crisis and the high cost of living was more government spending on housing, education and health care, along with property tax relief.
"Donald Trump's war in Iran, his tariffs, have put huge headwinds on our economy," she said.
On MaineCare, Charles accused the administration of expanding eligibility without adequately funding the providers expected to deliver care. In 2019, Mills [expanded MaineCare under the ACA](https://substack.com/redirect/3582de19-8572-4081-b363-0e02b3aa8dd9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including to nearly 100,000 able-bodied childless adults. She later expanded the welfare program again to include [a broader class of non-citizens](https://substack.com/redirect/46ce7036-fe1e-4ed4-9239-2c825f1f40ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
"So Mills-Pingree fundamentally, systematically mismanaged health care in Maine by expanding MaineCare but underfunding it," he said.
Bennett also faulted the state for failing to pay providers fairly and promptly, but said expansion should remain.
"People have grown to rely on it," he said, as a reason for keeping the welfare program.
Pingree argued that expansion had added 100,000 people to the welfare rolls and helped support rural hospitals, though she didn't explain how that claim comports with [the closure of Northern Light Inland Hospital in Waterville in 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/15e24052-dbbb-4385-b9ee-22402057a079?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Share The Robinson Report on Facebook!
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=219430542&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE5NDMwNTQyLCJpYXQiOjE3OTE1NzYzNzIsImV4cCI6MTc5NDE2ODM3MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.F3H6Nw1lAivbb-DljkIoTF7AYcsGQUj6HcqoQ7tjQJ4)
She proposed a public health insurance option and blamed federal policy -- that is, ObamaCare -- for adding pressure to the system.
On immigration, Pingree made her support for illegal aliens and open borders unmistakable.
"This is an issue where I would like to see ICE out of Maine, and I think the vast majority of Maine people agree with me," she said.
She accused U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents of harassing people traveling to work, school and hospitals, and said she would work with other governors and attorneys general to challenge unlawful enforcement actions.
Bennett also condemned the federal operation, describing agents as outsiders whose conduct had damaged communities and public trust.
"ICE has not earned the benefit of the doubt in the way that they've acted in Maine and hurting Maine people and Maine communities," he said.
Both defended [Maine's law limiting cooperation between local police and federal immigration authorities](https://substack.com/redirect/cd3b3bbb-51ab-4d49-846e-626420738008?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Bennett rejected Charles' description of it as a sanctuary-state law.
"I support that law. I would have signed that law had I been governor," Pingree said.
"I would work to ensure that we have the strongest law possible to protect people," she said, referring to criminal illegal aliens -- including drug traffickers and sex offenders -- that ICE has targeted for removal.
Charles called for repeal, arguing that restrictions on communication between local, state and federal agencies undermine public safety.
"State and local and federal law enforcement should always be talking to each other," he said. "That increases public safety."
The former assistant secretary of state for international narcotics and law enforcement affairs also said agents should wear body cameras and that masks undermine public trust.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..A7vDWdbMDAJhjIQjlahf6DBiS3eftW4Z5Ce6OkD5NzI?)
Pingree also reminded viewers that she and Bennett had worked together to [establish the Office of New Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/e89a044d-a088-4bdd-a98b-4bf56f9b0b3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a controversial new office that will largely exist to help non-citizens access welfare benefits.
The ONA emerged from a bill introduced by Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland), the former assistant executive director at Gateway Community Services who [announced she would not seek re-election](https://substack.com/redirect/26114d20-fd18-4328-881f-b89dd717bffb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) amid state and federal investigations into Gateway's alleged welfare fraud.
The current policy analyst for ONA, [Ekhlas Ahmed](https://substack.com/redirect/cb4128f7-fe52-4b0b-a2ae-53eab9a28809?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), is also a former employee of Gateway Community Services.
The ONA has gotten off to a rocky start, with Pingree's pick for the office's director -- Tarlan Ahmadov -- [being forced to resign from the position](https://substack.com/redirect/80b7e140-19ae-45eb-9d50-7969415102f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after The Maine Wire exposed his record of anti-Armenian rhetoric.
Charles was the only candidate on the stage who took a strong stance on the scourge of Chinese organized crime that has afflicted the state under the Mills Administration, with [Asian transnational criminal organizations converting hundreds of homes and commercial buildings](https://substack.com/redirect/156514f4-2492-402d-8092-e633d972bb3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) into toxic black-market cannabis sites.
The Republican viewed the drug and human trafficking problem as part of the state's housing crisis, proposing to reclaim homes converted into illegal growing operations.
"I will detoxify the 400 Chinese grow houses and resell them," he said.
The proposal touched a problem documented in the Maine Wire's investigations of Chinese organized crime: residential properties converted into marijuana factories, with hazardous chemicals potentially complicating their return to the housing market.
In [one Monmouth case reported in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/0a5565cd-6a74-4c09-8312-5b56be7238c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a woman said she and her grandchildren suffered respiratory irritation after touring a former grow house that had also been linked to shipments of Chinese-made pesticides and fungicides.
Electricity brought the debate back to Pingree's record inside the Mills administration, where she was a vocal advocate for wind turbines and solar panels -- two power-generation industries that drive up electrical costs with the benefits largely flowing to out-of-state or foreign corporations.
For Pingree, like her congresswoman mother, forcing Mainers to endure higher electricity costs is necessary to change global climate trends in a more favorable direction.
Asked how a Pingree administration would differ from Mills after years of rising housing and electricity costs, as well as the closure of health care facilities, Pingree claimed that she didn't agree with Mills on every issue. But she couldn't explain away her public and well-documented support for the policies, like the [net energy billing Solar Tax](https://substack.com/redirect/afd5a267-8b28-418b-8435-ac546d17e8e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and subsidized wind power, driving electricity prices higher.
"I will say I had the honor of working for Governor Mills for the last six and a half years, but I didn't agree with her on every issue," Pingree said.
She cited tribal sovereignty as a disagreement with Mills, then defended the administration's housing work. On electricity, she pointed to storm recovery and natural gas prices, while again blaming Trump's tariffs and war in Iran for worsening costs.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..MnwTeEdtTAaD4sKQG1CVwD_BKI5pDUuUIsDIIBRHQSE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=219430542)
Her answer did not address the expense of Maine's expanded net energy billing program, which subsidizes qualifying solar and other distributed generation. Nor did she explain why neighboring New Hampshire hasn't seen exploding energy prices as the result of international conflicts or trade policies.
The state's own Office of the Public Advocate projected that the expanded program would [cost more than $234 million in 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/afd5a267-8b28-418b-8435-ac546d17e8e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Charles argued for [ending subsidies and expanding access to hydroelectric power, natural gas, biomass and small modular nuclear reactors](https://substack.com/redirect/9852cf38-ddbc-48fd-96bc-7cb0fbbe8f5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
"On the energy side of the equation, I want to end the subsidies because they're not working," he said. "Just look at your bills. Subsidizing solar and wind isn't working."
He also urged Pingree and Bennett to join him in asking Mills to reconvene the Legislature, provide schools with energy assistance and suspend the state gas tax.
Pingree's property tax proposal drew opposition from both rivals.
She called for doubling the homestead exemption and amending the Maine Constitution to allow higher taxes on second homes owned by out-of-state residents.
"So I will acknowledge we do need to open up the Constitution," she said. "That is a big thing to do, but we've amended our Constitution many, many times before, and it would require bipartisan support."
Charles opposed the proposal. Bennett said it would delay relief without addressing spending.
"The proposal she has pushes the can down the road some more and I don't think it's viable," Bennett said.
For housing, Pingree proposed $100 million a year for production and infrastructure, along with a 90-day deadline for environmental permits. Charles favored reducing regulations and expanding manufactured housing, while Bennett proposed state-backed assistance to reduce down payments and monthly mortgage costs.
Charles ended with another attack on Pingree, questioning state funding awarded to a nonprofit he said had ties to her family.
The charge followed [his earlier demand for records involving organizations that had worked with her husband, filmmaker Jason Mann](https://substack.com/redirect/ed8ea926-97a8-4944-a9de-155ae6e1398f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The Island Institute claimed its films were privately funded.
Pingree used her closing statement to return to Trump, but inadvertently gave a perfect epitaph to Janet Mills' legacy.
"Mainers are fed up," she said. "Families are working harder and still falling behind."

Republican Robert "Bobby" Charles, Democrat Hannah Pingree, and "Independent" Rick Bennett clashed Thursday evening in a debate that was largely overshadowed by the U.S. Senate contest. Oct 9 | | | | | | | | | | | In the shadow of the Maine Senate debate Thursday night, the three contenders in Maine's gubernatorial election -- Republican Robert "Bobby" Charles, Democrat Hannah Pingree, and unaffiliated candidate Rick Bennett -- squared off in a lower key debate that hinged on the same question: Who is to blame for everything getting worse in Maine while Gov. Janet Mills (D) was governor, Troy Jackson was Senate President, and Pingree was Mills' top policy guru? For Charles, the answer was obvious. He spent Thursday's gubernatorial debate asking why Mainers should trust Pingree to fix the government she helped run as the chief policy architect of Mills' administration. "It's like inviting the arsonist back to put out the fire," Charles said. "It makes no sense whatsoever to put us in a position where all the bad policies are just compounded again." We can't arrest the frauds, but we can expose them. Sign up for The Robinson Report today! Pingree, a former Maine House speaker who led Mills' Office of Policy Innovation and the Future, defended her work on housing and energy while repeatedly blaming President Donald Trump for making Maine's problems worse. With the state of Maine facing a $1.3 billion forecasted budget shortfall, the , some of the highest and welfare dependency rates in the U.S., and rampant , you would expect anyone even partially responsible for the policies that created the present Maine malaise to be laughed out of the governor's race. Instead, Pingree -- the daughter of Democratic U.S. Rep. Chellie Pingree (ME-CD1) -- has led the three-person race in virtually every public opinion poll. Charles emerged victorious from a competitive GOP primary field, but did not receive a warm post-victory embrace from his former Republican opponents, whereas Pingree, who only defeated former Maine CDC Director Nirav Shah thanks to the Ranked Choice Voting innovation, quickly enjoyed broad support from her former rivals. On the margins of the partisan contest, former Republican State Sen. Rick Bennett, of Oxford, has waged a quixotic independent campaign that started when he cast , joining left-wing extremists on the wildly unpopular side of hot-button issues. Bennett joined Charles in condemning Augusta's spending habits. "The dirty truth is that nobody is minding the store," Bennett said. But he sided with Pingree on keeping MaineCare expansion -- the single largest driver of Maine's ever-expanding budget binges. Bennett also staked out a far-left position on illegal immigration enforcement, voicing support for the state retaining restrictions on cooperation with federal immigration agents. The debate at Husson University's Gracie Theatre in Bangor, hosted by the taxpayer-subsidized Maine Public with NEWS CENTER Maine and the Portland Press Herald, exposed how much the exploding cost of living is driving every campaign's strategy. Much as focused on laying blame for the rising expenses crushing Mainers' checking accounts, so too was the gubernatorial debate a contest over who could convince voters that they have ideas that can ease the heavy burden of higher prices for, well, everything. Except maybe cannabis. Charles called for cutting at least $1 billion from the budget, freezing state hiring, eliminating unfilled positions, ending subsidies and reviewing state spending from the ground up. He also promised to abolish the office Pingree ran. "We're going to reduce the overall budget by reducing the fraud, and we now know from both federal investigations and state investigations we have major fraud," he said. The state's oversight failures have already produced bills taxpayers may have to cover. Rather than investigate and prosecute welfare fraudsters, the Mills Administration snuck that would put Maine taxpayers on the hook if the Trump administration managed to defund MaineCare scammers. A federal audit of MaineCare services for children with autism estimated . Every one of the 100 sampled enrollee-months contained at least one improper or potentially improper payment. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' inspector general recommended that Maine return approximately $28.7 million in federal funds. Those are findings of improper payments, not a determination that every dollar was obtained through criminal fraud. Separately, DHHS records examined by The Robinson Report in April showed Gateway Community Services had repaid about $118,432 against more than $1.6 million in alleged overbilling. The records show that Gateway isn't the only Medicaid provider that is delinquent in repaying improperly claimed taxpayer resources. The Mills Administration did , but no charges have been filed against ex-CEO Abdullahi Ali, a Somali-American refugee with close ties to the Mills Administration and Democratic Party operatives. Bennett proposed an inspector general's office reporting directly to the governor to investigate misspending and possible corruption. He also accused the executive and legislative branches of allowing spending to expand without adequate scrutiny. "So we are spending in the state government well beyond the means of Mainers to pay," he said. "That's the reality." Pingree's response to the budget crisis and the high cost of living was more government spending on housing, education and health care, along with property tax relief. "Donald Trump's war in Iran, his tariffs, have put huge headwinds on our economy," she said. On MaineCare, Charles accused the administration of expanding eligibility without adequately funding the providers expected to deliver care. In 2019, Mills , including to nearly 100,000 able-bodied childless adults. She later expanded the welfare program again to include . "So Mills-Pingree fundamentally, systematically mismanaged health care in Maine by expanding MaineCare but underfunding it," he said. Bennett also faulted the state for failing to pay providers fairly and promptly, but said expansion should remain. "People have grown to rely on it," he said, as a reason for keeping the welfare program. Pingree argued that expansion had added 100,000 people to the welfare rolls and helped support rural hospitals, though she didn't explain how that claim comports with . Share The Robinson Report on Facebook! She proposed a public health insurance option and blamed federal policy -- that is, ObamaCare -- for adding pressure to the system. On immigration, Pingree made her support for illegal aliens and open borders unmistakable. "This is an issue where I would like to see ICE out of Maine, and I think the vast majority of Maine people agree with me," she said. She accused U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents of harassing people traveling to work, school and hospitals, and said she would work with other governors and attorneys general to challenge unlawful enforcement actions. Bennett also condemned the federal operation, describing agents as outsiders whose conduct had damaged communities and public trust. "ICE has not earned the benefit of the doubt in the way that they've acted in Maine and hurting Maine people and Maine communities," he said. Both defended . Bennett rejected Charles' description of it as a sanctuary-state law. "I support that law. I would have signed that law had I been governor," Pingree said. "I would work to ensure that we have the strongest law possible to protect people," she said, referring to criminal illegal aliens -- including drug traffickers and sex offenders -- that ICE has targeted for removal. Charles called for repeal, arguing that restrictions on communication between local, state and federal agencies undermine public safety. "State and local and federal law enforcement should always be talking to each other," he said. "That increases public safety." The former assistant secretary of state for international narcotics and law enforcement affairs also said agents should wear body cameras and that masks undermine public trust. ? Pingree also reminded viewers that she and Bennett had worked together to , a controversial new office that will largely exist to help non-citizens access welfare benefits. The ONA emerged from a bill introduced by Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland), the former assistant executive director at Gateway Community Services who amid state and federal investigations into Gateway's alleged welfare fraud. The current policy analyst for ONA, , is also a former employee of Gateway Community Services. The ONA has gotten off to a rocky start, with Pingree's pick for the office's director -- Tarlan Ahmadov -- after The Maine Wire exposed his record of anti-Armenian rhetoric. Charles was the only candidate on the stage who took a strong stance on the scourge of Chinese organized crime that has afflicted the state under the Mills Administration, with into toxic black-market cannabis sites. The Republican viewed the drug and human trafficking problem as part of the state's housing crisis, proposing to reclaim homes converted into illegal growing operations. "I will detoxify the 400 Chinese grow houses and resell them," he said. The proposal touched a problem documented in the Maine Wire's investigations of Chinese organized crime: residential properties converted into marijuana factories, with hazardous chemicals potentially complicating their return to the housing market. In , a woman said she and her grandchildren suffered respiratory irritation after touring a former grow house that had also been linked to shipments of Chinese-made pesticides and fungicides. Electricity brought the debate back to Pingree's record inside the Mills administration, where she was a vocal advocate for wind turbines and solar panels -- two power-generation industries that drive up electrical costs with the benefits largely flowing to out-of-state or foreign corporations. For Pingree, like her congresswoman mother, forcing Mainers to endure higher electricity costs is necessary to change global climate trends in a more favorable direction. Asked how a Pingree administration would differ from Mills after years of rising housing and electricity costs, as well as the closure of health care facilities, Pingree claimed that she didn't agree with Mills on every issue. But she couldn't explain away her public and well-documented support for the policies, like the and subsidized wind power, driving electricity prices higher. "I will say I had the honor of working for Governor Mills for the last six and a half years, but I didn't agree with her on every issue," Pingree said. She cited tribal sovereignty as a disagreement with Mills, then defended the administration's housing work. On electricity, she pointed to storm recovery and natural gas prices, while again blaming Trump's tariffs and war in Iran for worsening costs. Her answer did not address the expense of Maine's expanded net energy billing program, which subsidizes qualifying solar and other distributed generation. Nor did she explain why neighboring New Hampshire hasn't seen exploding energy prices as the result of international conflicts or trade policies. The state's own Office of the Public Advocate projected that the expanded program would . Charles argued for . "On the energy side of the equation, I want to end the subsidies because they're not working," he said. "Just look at your bills. Subsidizing solar and wind isn't working." He also urged Pingree and Bennett to join him in asking Mills to reconvene the Legislature, provide schools with energy assistance and suspend the state gas tax. Pingree's property tax proposal drew opposition from both rivals. She called for doubling the homestead exemption and amending the Maine Constitution to allow higher taxes on second homes owned by out-of-state residents. "So I will acknowledge we do need to open up the Constitution," she said. "That is a big thing to do, but we've amended our Constitution many, many times before, and it would require bipartisan support." Charles opposed the proposal. Bennett said it would delay relief without addressing spending. "The proposal she has pushes the can down the road some more and I don't think it's viable," Bennett said. For housing, Pingree proposed $100 million a year for production and infrastructure, along with a 90-day deadline for environmental permits. Charles favored reducing regulations and expanding manufactured housing, while Bennett proposed state-backed assistance to reduce down payments and monthly mortgage costs. Charles ended with another attack on Pingree, questioning state funding awarded to a nonprofit he said had ties to her family. The charge followed . The Island Institute claimed its films were privately funded. Pingree used her closing statement to return to Trump, but inadvertently gave a perfect epitaph to Janet Mills' legacy. "Mainers are fed up," she said. "Families are working harder and still falling behind." Support The Robinson Report with a paid subscription today! You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. SpaceX agreed Thursday to buy Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz book, up to 14 megahertz of paired low-band, the Journal has it near $8 billion cash, and called it the last piece for complete U.S. phone coverage. Friday the tape did the math. Verizon fell about 10%, worst day since 2002. AT&T about 10%, worst since 2000. T-Mobile 13%, worst since 2013. SpaceX climbed about 1%.
* **Winners?** SpaceX and the subscriber. Low-band punches walls. Evercore says it now has the outline of a real network. Carr called the fight good news and flagged over $100 billion of spectrum in two years.
* **Losers?** Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile. Munster says Elon claims he does not want a phone, then bets a Starlink handset shows up -- a bigger problem for Samsung than Apple. JPMorgan's "limited near-term risk" did not save the stocks.
* **Next?** FCC still has to bless Grain. A full terrestrial grid takes years and capital, so the dividend names do not die on Monday but they will re-rate down every time Starlink Mobile prints a coverage map.

"Last week we were in a rural school out in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, and then we went to a school attended mainly by the Amish kids, coming out of a very closely knit religious and family background." George H.W. Bush (1989)
Somewhere in Albany, somebody printed an invoice and mailed it to Shady Lane School in Clymer, to Pleasant View in Heuvelton, and to Dygert Road out by the Canajoharie settlement. Three little one-room Amish schoolhouses. Three schools that take not a single dollar of public money -- not for buses, not for books, not for lunch. The bill came to $118,000.
The reason? Fifty-nine of their children are not vaccinated.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eba2b902-542b-43e1-9ade-e6aad922820a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And here is the part I had to read twice. Under the State of New York's own position in the Second Circuit case, every school day an unvaccinated child sits in that classroom is a fresh violation -- up to $2,000, per child. Not once. Every day. The violation is not that anyone got sick. The violation is attendance itself.
Dygert Road got billed $52,000 for 26 kids. Pleasant View, $46,000 for 23. Shady Lane, $20,000 for 10. On any given school day, those three schoolhouses are carrying $118,000 of exposure. Run that out over a 180-day school year and you're north of $21 million -- owed by families who already told the state they cannot pay the first bill. Their attorney, Aaron Siri, told the New York Post the only way any of it ever gets paid is if the state takes their land.
Think about how we got here. These families had a religious exemption for decades. In June 2019, Albany repealed it -- Andrew Cuomo signed the bill after the measles outbreak centered on New York City, the worst in more than twenty-five years. A law written for a city outbreak now generates daily invoices for farm schoolhouses that never saw a case. Kathy Hochul has left that repeal sitting right there in force for her entire tenure as governor. The fines started coming down in December 2022. The families sued the next June. A Second Circuit panel ruled against them, the Supreme Court sent the case back, and on June 30 of this year the same panel "reconsidered" and called their arguments without merit. Now Joseph Miller, Jonas Smucker, and Ezra Wengerd are asking the Supreme Court to let them live by the faith they have lived by their whole lives.
Fifty years ago, the Supreme Court ruled in Wisconsin v. Yoder that the Amish could not be forced to send their children to high school -- that this country would honor a people who educate their own, work their own land, and keep to themselves. That was the deal. Now the same state government that acknowledges their right to run their own schools has decided those schools are only permitted to exist if they administer Albany's full shot schedule first. Build the schoolhouse with your own hands, pay your own taxes, ask for nothing -- and the state still sends the bill, one for every unvaccinated child, every single day.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b9da71e-1bb9-41e0-a909-82b2a5c3434d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And it is not just three schools. Their attorneys tell the Post that every Amish school in New York is in the same position, and the health department refused to say how many others have been fined. There are about 25,000 Amish in New York. Their lawyers say the threat of an exodus is real: if they lose at the Supreme Court, they leave. Not stop attending. Not quietly comply. Leave -- the way their ancestors left countries that also knew better than they did how Amish children should be raised.
Meanwhile, consider the company they're keeping in this fight. These are the same people who spent years screaming my body, my choice. Where did that crowd go? When a quiet Amish father says he wants to decide what goes into his own child's body, Albany doesn't hand him a protest permit -- it sends the collection notice. The principle, it turns out, was never my body, my choice. It was my choice, your bill.
Lara Trump is right that money is the weapon here. They cannot drag the Amish into court in handcuffs for praying. They cannot issue a press release scolding people who have no press, no lawsuits of their own making, no lobby. So they fine them. They fine them until they sell the farm, or until they leave the state -- and some families are already talking about leaving. A fine you can't pay is not a penalty. It's an eviction with extra steps.
Ask yourself honestly: if they can do this to people who keep to themselves, farm their land, run their own schools, and ask nothing from the government -- what exactly do you think they will do to you?
I read those numbers and I had to read them twice. Informed consent is supposed to mean something. Religious liberty is the very first freedom in the Bill of Rights -- not a favor the governor hands out when it suits her, and not a line item she collects on when it doesn't.
The Supreme Court should take this case, because the question it presents is not about vaccines. It's about whether a state can price a family's faith at $2,000 a day and wait for the barn to sell.
Kathy, your sign says "Keeping New Yorkers Safe." Drop the fines. Give these families their exemption back.
Leave the Amish alone.

Today, October 9, the federal government did something gun owners have wanted for ninety years: it stopped requiring Americans to register suppressors, short-barreled rifles, and short-barreled shotguns with the ATF. No more Form 4. No more fingerprints and the months-long wait. For most of the country, buying a suppressor now looks like buying any other firearm. A quick background check at the counter, and you walk out.
But not in Mississippi.
When the ATF issued its guidance applying the court's ruling nationwide, it carved out roughly fifteen states whose own laws still demand federal registration. Mississippi is on that list. In twenty-seven states, residents walked out of gun shops that same day with nothing but a standard background check. Our neighbors in Louisiana are among them. Mississippians are not.
And here is what should make every Mississippian angry. The only reason we were left behind is a single sentence in our own code. Section 97-37-31 makes owning a suppressor a crime unless you are "duly authorized under federal law." Because our statute chains us to the federal permission slip, the ATF is keeping the Form 4 requirement alive here even as it abandons it everywhere else. Washington got out of the way. Mississippi's own politicians are holding the handcuffs.
Our leaders love to call Mississippi one of the most pro-Second Amendment states in the country. Here is their test. This is not a fight with the federal government. The federal government already surrendered. The barrier is entirely ours, and it can be removed with a few lines of legislation. There is no court to wait on, no bureaucrat to persuade, no act of Congress required. Just the will to act.
So let us find out who means it. Every elected official who claims the pro-gun mantle, from legislators to statewide officers to candidates for higher office, should say publicly, this week, that Section 97-37-31 must be repealed. Silence now is an answer all its own.
And Governor Tate Reeves should lead. He should not make Mississippi gun owners wait months for the regular session to grind into gear. He should call a special session and put this repeal at the top of its agenda. In the meantime, he can direct the Department of Public Safety and state law enforcement not to enforce a registration requirement the rest of the country has already discarded. That is what executive leadership looks like when a constitutional right is on the line.
None of this is hard, and that is what makes the moment so clarifying. For years our politicians have told us they would defend our gun rights if Washington ever threatened them. Washington just did the opposite. It handed those rights back, and the only thing standing in the way is a law written in Jackson. If Mississippi's leaders mean what they have always said, they will act now. Not next session. Not next year. The rest of the country is already free. Mississippi should not be the state that made its own citizens wait.

I want to express my profound gratitude for having you by my side.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1601&source=&t=1&akid=4363%2E124072%2EB90bec) | | | | | | Peter, I’m not reaching out to everyone today – just a select few, including you.
---
| | My team was going through our supporter records, and yours stood out in the crowd. You’re one of my most attentive grassroots supporters. You’ve been getting these emails for a while now, and we see you're keeping up with the latest on this election. I want you to know that I know how engaged you’ve been with our campaign and how much I appreciate it. [**_Today, I’m asking you to take the next step._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1601&amount=5&t=9&akid=4363%2E124072%2EB90bec) **Here’s why:**
---
| | Grassroots fundraising has stalled recently, and it couldn’t come at a worse time. Republican super PACs have poured tens of millions into North Carolina to defeat me, and President Trump and JD Vance have both come to smear my name at rallies alongside my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley.
---
| | We need to turn this around fast – and the first step is getting our fundraising back on track. [**_Will you chip in $5 right now to help us reach today's goal? The stakes could not be higher._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1601&amount=5&t=10&akid=4363%2E124072%2EB90bec)
---
| | North Carolina is the best chance Democrats have to flip one of the four red seats we need to take back the Senate. **If we lose here, we lose our shot at flipping the majority.** The only way to avoid that is by building the resources to compete with the GOP's false attacks.
---
| | **Unlike my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley, I’m not a Washington DC insider who can rely on his billionaire connections to buy this Senate seat. I’m depending on people like you giving what you can, when you can, at crucial moments like this.**
---
| | _With 25 days left until the election, Peter, I need you._
---
| | **Since time’s running out, my team wanted me to reach out to engaged supporters like you – so I’m personally asking:** [**_Will you please chip in your first $5 donation to my campaign today so we can respond to GOP attacks, flip North Carolina’s seat and help Democrats secure the Senate majority?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1601&amount=5&t=11&akid=4363%2E124072%2EB90bec)

Roy

Minnesota has tried one-party control for 20 years, and here's where that got us:
At least $9 billion in fraud and stolen taxpayer money, rising crime, and failing schools.
They are going 100 miles per hour in the wrong direction.
Peggy Flanagan, a failed career politician who enabled the policies that got us here. Her way doesn't work. And yet we've been paying Peggy Flanagan with our hard-earned money for 20 years.
It's not the time to give her a promotion. It's time to fire her for good.
Right now, the "expert" pollsters say she has the edge in this race, but it's a toss-up that could come down to a few hundred votes on election night. Not only is Peggy as extreme as they come, but she was also Tim Walz's running mate.
She was the sitting Lieutenant Governor during the largest COVID-19 scam in the country - the Feeding Our Future scandal. She's done everything possible to distance herself from this debacle, and so far it's worked!
We can't let all the rampant, unprecedented fraud that took place under her watch go unnoticed. It's a national disgrace. That's why Tim Walz was forced to end his re-election campaign... Meanwhile, his right hand wants to be our next U.S. Senator.

name: Rev. Hodari Williams
subject: It’s nice to meet you, Peter!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Hello Peter, it’s nice to meet
you!

I’m Reverend Hodari Williams, Justice Democrats’ new Executive Director.
It’s an honor to join Team JD and build on Alexandra Rojas’ massive
success over the last nine years transforming the Democratic Party through
this organization.

What you’ve built together is nothing short of extraordinary, and I am so
grateful to Alex for her near-decade of leadership. She’s passing the
baton to me after JD’s most successful election cycle EVER, and I can’t
wait to see what we accomplish next.

As a pastor, for almost two decades I have opened my church doors to
politicians who overpromised and underdelivered. Those politicians’ lack
of courage and power meant I also opened those same doors to families
facing eviction, unable to afford food and afraid for the futures of their
children.

Leading this next chapter of Justice Democrats is an opportunity to move
upstream from triage to transformation — organizing working-class
communities like mine so they can take back their power from corporations,
billionaire oligarchs, and the politicians they buy.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261009.UxtPuJ&refcode=em20261009-38339&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38339%2E1203867%2E10pRC5 ]Before I share more about my background, I’ve got to ask: will you help
us close out the 2026 cycle on a strong note with a grassroots
contribution of $5?

I was born and raised in Lakewood, New Jersey, in a home where the
struggles for justice and equality were kitchen table issues. My parents
were activists and community organizers, and the civil rights movement and
its continued legacy nurtured my development. From a young age, I saw my
calling in service for the disenfranchised and movements of liberation,
organizing my community at various points when local government was
leaving us behind.

After graduating from college, I joined the NAACP as a field organizer for
voter rights and empowerment, and went on to work for their Religious
Affairs office in Atlanta, Georgia, where I coordinated a national
faith-based program of civic engagement, direct action, and justice
initiatives. There, I brought faith groups and leaders across every
background together to chart out a collaborative approach to civil rights
and the shared issues affecting their communities.

That work took me across the Black Belt in the South, where I witnessed
eye-opening pockets of extreme poverty and inequity — from cities that
were the historic battlegrounds for civil rights to rural communities
erased from the national consciousness — in the world’s wealthiest
country. The experience only deepened my commitment to the movement.

My work for human rights expanded globally when I traveled to Kenya as a
program coordinator with the Presbyterian Church USA. In Nairobi, I worked
with the Green Belt Movement to support their work combating deforestation
and using environmental justice as a tool for economic empowerment and
self-determination.

When I got back to the States, I became the Pastor for Elmwood United
Presbyterian Church’s historic congregation in New Jersey, beginning
nearly a decade of justice-focused ministry. There, I led the multi-site
congregation in organizing direct action campaigns following the police
murder of Trayvon Martin and Michael Brown, and also established a cafe to
feed five thousand families a year.

Since 2017, I’ve served as Senior Pastor at New Life Presbyterian Church
in South Fulton, GA, where I’ve focused on growing the church into a
community hub and resource for the greater Atlanta region. We’ve developed
and expanded food security initiatives, implemented counseling and
community support services, established a primary school to fill local
education gaps, and led community development initiatives on affordable
housing, youth programming, family-centered community space, and
neighborhood transformation.

All of those experiences brought me here to Justice Democrats, an
organization that is recruiting and supporting bold, diverse candidates
for Congress who have the political courage to deal with the crises
impacting marginalized and disenfranchised communities. I’m really excited

clean_body: [1]Justice Democrats Hello Peter, it’s nice to meet you! I’m Reverend Hodari Williams, Justice Democrats’ new Executive Director. It’s an honor to join Team JD and build on Alexandra Rojas’ massive success over the last nine years transforming the Democratic Party through this organization. What you’ve built together is nothing short of extraordinary, and I am so grateful to Alex for her near-decade of leadership. She’s passing the baton to me after JD’s most successful election cycle EVER, and I can’t wait to see what we accomplish next. As a pastor, for almost two decades I have opened my church doors to politicians who overpromised and underdelivered. Those politicians’ lack of courage and power meant I also opened those same doors to families facing eviction, unable to afford food and afraid for the futures of their children. Leading this next chapter of Justice Democrats is an opportunity to move upstream from triage to transformation — organizing working-class communities like mine so they can take back their power from corporations, billionaire oligarchs, and the politicians they buy. [ ]Before I share more about my background, I’ve got to ask: will you help us close out the 2026 cycle on a strong note with a grassroots contribution of $5? I was born and raised in Lakewood, New Jersey, in a home where the struggles for justice and equality were kitchen table issues. My parents were activists and community organizers, and the civil rights movement and its continued legacy nurtured my development. From a young age, I saw my calling in service for the disenfranchised and movements of liberation, organizing my community at various points when local government was leaving us behind. After graduating from college, I joined the NAACP as a field organizer for voter rights and empowerment, and went on to work for their Religious Affairs office in Atlanta, Georgia, where I coordinated a national faith-based program of civic engagement, direct action, and justice initiatives. There, I brought faith groups and leaders across every background together to chart out a collaborative approach to civil rights and the shared issues affecting their communities. That work took me across the Black Belt in the South, where I witnessed eye-opening pockets of extreme poverty and inequity — from cities that were the historic battlegrounds for civil rights to rural communities erased from the national consciousness — in the world’s wealthiest country. The experience only deepened my commitment to the movement. My work for human rights expanded globally when I traveled to Kenya as a program coordinator with the Presbyterian Church USA. In Nairobi, I worked with the Green Belt Movement to support their work combating deforestation and using environmental justice as a tool for economic empowerment and self-determination. When I got back to the States, I became the Pastor for Elmwood United Presbyterian Church’s historic congregation in New Jersey, beginning nearly a decade of justice-focused ministry. There, I led the multi-site congregation in organizing direct action campaigns following the police murder of Trayvon Martin and Michael Brown, and also established a cafe to feed five thousand families a year. Since 2017, I’ve served as Senior Pastor at New Life Presbyterian Church in South Fulton, GA, where I’ve focused on growing the church into a community hub and resource for the greater Atlanta region. We’ve developed and expanded food security initiatives, implemented counseling and community support services, established a primary school to fill local education gaps, and led community development initiatives on affordable housing, youth programming, family-centered community space, and neighborhood transformation. All of those experiences brought me here to Justice Democrats, an organization that is recruiting and supporting bold, diverse candidates for Congress who have the political courage to deal with the crises impacting marginalized and disenfranchised communities. I’m really excited to be a part of this with you, Peter. And I’m really excited for what comes next, breaking new frontiers, and continuing to organize working class communities across the country being left behind by our corporate class. You’ll be hearing more from me as we fight to win our last three general election races this November and start looking ahead to 2027 and beyond. [ ]For now, if you can contribute $5, 10, 25, or whatever you can spare to kick off this new chapter at Justice Democrats, I would be so grateful. All these dead heat polls and updated ratings tell me two things:
1. We can win this race.
2. The attacks from Sen. Marshall and his super PAC allies are about to get much worse.

subject: Each day until November 3rd

body:
This week, I’ve been working alongside our organizers and volunteers to mobilize voters across the Seattle and King County area.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261009-6815-footer&t=1&akid=6815%2E420207%2E9a6Sd0)
Peter, today is an incredibly important day. So is tomorrow, and the next day, and every single day between now and November 3rd. With the midterm elections coming up, these next three and a half weeks are crucial.
Last weekend, I was in California canvassing with Connie Chan in San Francisco before joining with Bernie Sanders to rally for three fantastic progressive candidates: Randy Villegas, Aisha Wahab, and Jane Kim.
This week, I’ve been working alongside our organizers and volunteers to mobilize voters across the Seattle and King County area. I’m working not just to win re-election myself, but to elect bold progressive candidates up and down the ballot.
Next week, I’ll continue traveling across the country to support my endorsed candidates, with stops in Texas and Florida, followed by a whirlwind swing through New York, Michigan, and Minnesota. I’m taking every opportunity I can to support our slate of people-first progressives, including Abdul El-Sayed, Peggy Flanagan, and more. Then it’s back to Seattle for the final few days of GOTV!
[**It’s a lot, right? And it’s such critical work — so we don’t allow the extremist MAGA Republicans to maintain control of Congress and lose our chance to hold this corrupt, authoritarian administration accountable. So Peter, can you pitch in $20.26, $3, or anything at all today to fund my critical election year work?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/55136?c0=pj-em-20261009.XVdlfY&refcode=em20261009-6815&t=2&akid=6815%2E420207%2E9a6Sd0)
**[Contribute $20.26](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/55136?c0=pj-em-20261009.XVdlfY&refcode=em20261009-6815&t=21&akid=6815%2E420207%2E9a6Sd0)**
Our progressive movement has a clear vision for how to improve peoples’ lives if we retake the majority this November. We’ll use our oversight power to hold Trump and ICE accountable, and pass critically important legislation on everything from health care to immigration to the minimum wage and more. But everything hinges on what we do in this final stretch.
It’s going to be a busy next few weeks.
And next year will be even busier when Congress is back in session and Democrats, fingers crossed, are in the majority. I know we can grow our movement and continue expanding support for Medicare for All, humane immigration reform, and more across the country.
This is what the people want and this is what I will keep fighting for, now and through November 3rd (and, yes, even after that). [**Can you chip in $20.26 or $3 to support my work? Every contribution helps fund my fight against corporate special interests, Big Pharma, and Trump’s MAGA Republican allies.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/55136?c0=pj-em-20261009.XVdlfY&refcode=em20261009-6815&t=22&akid=6815%2E420207%2E9a6Sd0)
In solidarity,
Pramila

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: She called the governor's office from the crash scene.
body:
Plus: Trump, Iran and LA. Hear what he really said. | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/r_DMFC8fXhM?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
If you hurt someone with your car, your first thought is whether they're okay. Mimi Stewart, the highest-ranking member of New Mexico's Senate, told police she's a state senator, that she'd called the governor's office, and that she needed to go home. The crash was in January 2024, and the body cam video only became public this week. It shows how some people in Santa Fe think the rules work for them.
**Plus:** Trump said Iran could "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego. We play the sentence that came right before it, and you can decide what he meant.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/l6xFQI4pb3l?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
🚔 **ON POLICE BODY CAM: "I'M THE PRESIDENT OF THE STATE SENATE"**
Stewart was driving home from a reception at the governor's mansion on the first day of the 2024 session when her car rolled over a man's foot.
She tells the officer her title. He has no idea what she's talking about, and his answer is our favorite moment on the tape.
She also has a few things to say about the man on the gurney. We stop the video and go through them, and Mark explains why he thinks this is exactly what's wrong with Santa Fe.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/vxUBvJA3Oqz?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🇺🇸 **TRUMP SAID IRAN COULD "TAKE OUT" LOS ANGELES. HERE'S WHAT HE SAID FIRST.**
The headlines said Trump would let Iran hit LA and San Diego. We play the full clip from his Nebraska rally so you can hear it for yourself.
We explain why moments like this are the reason so many Trump voters stopped trusting the press.

💰 **GREGG HULL WANTS TO END NEW MEXICO'S INCOME TAX. DEB HAALAND'S ANSWER IS...TRUMP.**
Hull rolled out a plan to phase out the state income tax, starting with the people who earn the least. Mark likes it and thinks Hull should go further.
Of course Haaland called the plan "the Trump playbook," and Mark explains why that answer keeps New Mexico losing doctors and young people to Texas, Arizona and Colorado.
---

| | Friend,

**Yesterday, I voted NO on another King County tax increase.**

The Council approved a new sales tax without sending it to voters, without a clear spending plan in place, and on the very same day we appointed a new Inspector General to root out corruption in programs similar to the one this tax is meant to fund.

**That 's not good enough for me. [Support my campaign _here_ if it's not good enough for you either!](https://us.list-manage.com/166rbfUjjkA?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)**

Families across King County are struggling to afford housing, groceries, gas--and you guessed it--taxes! Government should not reach deeper into their pockets before proving it can responsibly manage the money it already has.
\------------------------------------------------------------
**_" Before asking King County families to once again pay more, we ought to get our own house in order." _
-Councilmember Reagan Dunn
[DONATE NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/AurPg9E27gl?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)**
\------------------------------------------------------------
And after recent findings of potential waste, fraud, and abuse involving programs funded by the Department of Community and Human Services, _stronger financial accountability must come first._
**[Read about my vote here | _MyNorthwest: King County Council approves sales tax increase without seeking voter approval_](https://us.list-manage.com/18cI8mkYAb9?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)**
Friend, I'm doing everything I can to keep life affordable and taxes low for King County families, but sometimes it can feel like a very lonely role. **_Would you join me in opposing higher taxes by [making a contribution of $25, $35, or even $75](https://us.list-manage.com/B0MRg6b8yRf?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166) to my campaign TODAY?_**

Could a Supreme Court retirement be Trump’s next plan to lock in power forever? | |
---
Peter, Justice Samuel Alito made headlines recently when he pledged not to retire before the new Congress was seated. **But his colleague Clarence Thomas has been conspicuously quiet. He’s two years older than Alito, and has served on the Court for far longer.****_His_****retirement could be the one that’s imminent.** **[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqv6Sp4Aez7krlw2a7I8s9sOF-OmC2W1Mh_rAp2bVziB_nrt5DGN6oP7z4nCiAQgd8GlI3R_iGvUzLG_KBkqVBVuqdKvUBPHPyEx5Aj7E5cI73jxbPWauaACPNVso3j8wfhDgTsWnq2G89U0xHaHjH-gUNeHRNCTA98mxwG9Mfe3jwFOOrixui2zDJJ0AQn_jQC8YgmwFbXA_wilkbQxTNZmWrov_vpHhnQyoRumJFuJP21Ig09KhAeXvA7ipIXtbridFssIbWnzw5rIllvhUqqwXiUteOGlyJvLzLuZHiGMTQ/4uq/scdXLxFhTaGIsEX2kfZr-Q/h0/h001.DMUtD6eipTzpxkPCOooqYYlW5Cj-VUuIjf3Un3Kj1BE)** Both Thomas and Alito helped build a Supreme Court that has consistently stolen power from working people and handed it to wealthy special interests. Rumors of their respective retirements have been flying all summer long. **If Trump is given the opportunity to replace either or both of these justices, he could lock in corrupt, extremist power for decades to come.** That becomes a lot easier for him if Thomas retires before the midterm elections shake up the balance of power in Congress. **That’s why United for Democracy is preparing for a major Supreme Court confirmation fight, and fast. We can’t let the wealthy elites keep rigging the Court and our system in the shadows.** **[We’re standing up a people-powered coalition to stop a confirmation fight in its tracks the minute a retirement is announced. Can you rush a donation today to make sure we can fight back ahead of midterms and during the lame duck session?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqv6Sp4Aez7krlw2a7I8s9sOF-OmC2W1Mh_rAp2bVziB_rcYUUo2M3YstxDcnBS8CFwLmaYd-MCDVSMxpVUJFDaWXNdyW1AAOpI5KojMkA22-XttUiQJMucI0yM39f2oP6lkYngZRa-Al62AWkZtHnQJCBqHp6j-kNzISe9XxfRpPmPaUMZ4wcjBy5lY15rDg8iSB1k8tXyWLuobyz2E7YOQ1ij7wezUSWzrBpPRDA33qLdfnm0CuijWVSs7PpDgRhJd-S4CuB-27nlVkUIaAoWNQCXBvN1BHUHDeprmxJx9eQ/4uq/scdXLxFhTaGIsEX2kfZr-Q/h1/h001.2JWJahkOrOPG9E6bM0yHmdf2eEXzkSQmS8UiO0ggv4k)** **** [**DONATE**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqv6Sp4Aez7krlw2a7I8s9sOF-OmC2W1Mh_rAp2bVziB_lx-G2loU6tvSGlla0OigDaU6CLdlLRj48KsYULiZCwPNw8_43agm59QZlVwKaBlAgJz1J3aEvLajq92O2RU2HFx_5YJYoqJtxaczasQYlYnLftPz59JJvA3yqkz_Z5tseLCqhPtUUal7c2vmIZNgKM__481-zCQTXTP7mb3O7JsrTO3OD6yO5LWGkz36id-tRU6j0rRfQKLPNWEJ8b371slLnCMx3a1mKLxZuNBdhP7t1uEkNGR-qxM7j1exiZjTQ/4uq/scdXLxFhTaGIsEX2kfZr-Q/h2/h001.kZ-6thPRAmmZDwQNjAbIXEmVgd4EGPq8kjupxNXliZQ) **** **Justice Thomas was seen on Capitol Hill this summer having mysterious meetings with lawmakers.** He wouldn’t say who he was meeting with, or what they were meeting about. Court watchers believe he may have been preparing with them for his retirement. **Trump, his billionaire cronies, and the shadowy elites who helped capture the Court already have a list of young, extremist replacements they’ll try to force through.** The fight could come right for us in November, or it could come early next year. But we’re already gearing up to respond. clean_body: Could a Supreme Court retirement be Trump’s next plan to lock in power forever? | | Peter, Justice Samuel Alito made headlines recently when he pledged not to retire before the new Congress was seated. But his colleague Clarence Thomas has been conspicuously quiet. He’s two years older than Alito, and has served on the Court for far longer.Hisretirement could be the one that’s imminent. Both Thomas and Alito helped build a Supreme Court that has consistently stolen power from working people and handed it to wealthy special interests. Rumors of their respective retirements have been flying all summer long. If Trump is given the opportunity to replace either or both of these justices, he could lock in corrupt, extremist power for decades to come. That becomes a lot easier for him if Thomas retires before the midterm elections shake up the balance of power in Congress. That’s why United for Democracy is preparing for a major Supreme Court confirmation fight, and fast. We can’t let the wealthy elites keep rigging the Court and our system in the shadows. ** Justice Thomas was seen on Capitol Hill this summer having mysterious meetings with lawmakers. He wouldn’t say who he was meeting with, or what they were meeting about. Court watchers believe he may have been preparing with them for his retirement. Trump, his billionaire cronies, and the shadowy elites who helped capture the Court already have a list of young, extremist replacements they’ll try to force through. | | | This is a photo of my brother, Anthony DeLustro. Anthony spent more than 20 years serving citizens as an NYPD cop, hunting down dangerous drug dealers and busting up drug dens. On 9/11, he helped evacuate hundreds of people from one of the buildings just before it collapsed. Since that day, he’s been battling cancer and Ground Zero Lung from the toxic fumes.We really thought Anthony had been through the worst of it. And when he told us he was taking a police job in a small South Carolina town so he could spend his golden years close to his grandkids, I was so relieved.

| | | How could I have known he was about to face the greatest danger of his life?I’m not talking about a drug dealer or a terrorist or even cancer...**...but a local prosecutor hellbent on destroying my brother for defending himself when he was the victim of a road rage incident.** Let me explain.The day Anthony was attacked, he was off duty. He and his wife had stopped for lunch after spending the morning at a “Coffee With A Cop” community event.And as they tried to pull out of the crowded restaurant parking lot......another driver, in a fit of road rage, jumped out of his car and began screaming threats at my brother. Anthony tried to calm him down.But the man attacked him, striking him over and over.My brother could see the situation was spiraling out of control. He pulled out his badge and told the man he was under arrest.But instead of complying......the man knocked the badge out of Anthony’s hand.Then he got in his car and tried to flee, dragging my brother with his vehicle and running over his legs.In that moment, Anthony knew he was about to be crushed to death in front of his own wife.So he fired a single shot into his attacker’s arm, bringing the car to a stop.Anthony’s quick thinking saved his life.But the road rage driver who attacked him died at the scene. When I got the call that Anthony had been assaulted and was in the hospital with serious injuries, I couldn’t believe what had happened.I was so relieved he was alive. **But my relief turned into shock when my brother was arrested and charged with murder.** He hadn’t even recovered from his injuries when the local prosecutor dragged him in front of a judge and had him locked up in jail.He’s already spent 10 months behind bars.And he’s facing up to **30** **years** in prison.My friend, Anthony is 64 years old.If he’s convicted...**...he’ll likely spend the rest of his life locked up--and die in prison--for defending himself.** [_**That's why I'm writing you--someone I've never met--to ask you to help my brother.**_](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckcuOmzAUhp_G7Ih847ZgkQqoKiVVFU2nS-tgHyee2oBsk75-xXT6ArP99X3nov_XVV3Bebfcv0PAPmarYlIP9FuCJ0LH2APjauMatujSqjjldcloSTsFOrsnKgmF6Y02wHSBPWs6VjVd3cji0SOzojZVDZIbJmG2VtTdjIZ30lZWVIXrj3mM0o4zypg41WxuqWixtZS1c9MSScFjzKeI2z57p2HJkH7bNWo86TUUvn_kvCUizoRPhE8J9R7xBAuaNR8E4ZNHbyzh0wZVJbqmpaWVb-FtloyIac9BpXWPGokYbuMr4fURBTRuD0QM4_X87fIRaggbuPtCxPBxd6u-DF_VZbwMk7qNr-qdVsN4-Vn-OJe3l-m_uS4Zl3yseJnKfzKjRezN9sd571LdEEnvAZx_fyt_solnz_8GAAD__7DclBc)

| | | Because what they’re doing to Anthony is an outrage. I might not be a cop...but to me, if a police officer puts you under arrest, you don’t resist.And you certainly don’t physically attack the officer, then try to flee the scene.My brother may have been off duty. But you know that as an off-duty officer, he had the authority--and even the responsibility--to make an arrest to protect the public. What does this prosecutor expect off-duty officers to do--just let angry, violent offenders beat them up, resist arrest, and then walk away like nothing happened?

| | | My friend, Anthony doesn’t deserve this.He’s a good man who’s well-respected by his fellow officers. He served as a cop for four decades and never once faced discipline. He has a spotless record full of awards and commendations.So to watch my brother’s life be torn apart like this is just heartbreaking.It’s been hard on his family too. Several years ago, Anthony and his wife took their two granddaughters into their home. They’ve been raising them ever since. You can imagine the pain it’s caused these poor girls to have their grandfather locked up and treated like a common criminal.My friend, we were almost out of hope.And then we found out about the **Law****Enforcement Legal Defense Fund**. clean_body: My brother saved lives on 9/11. Now he faces 30 years in prison. Never in a million years did I think I would be writing an email like this. | | | | Dear Friend, in a million years did I think I would be writing an email like this. | | | This is a photo of my brother, Anthony DeLustro. Anthony spent more than 20 years serving citizens as an NYPD cop, hunting down dangerous drug dealers and busting up drug dens. On 9/11, he helped evacuate hundreds of people from one of the buildings just before it collapsed. Since that day, he’s been battling cancer and Ground Zero Lung from the toxic fumes.We really thought Anthony had been through the worst of it. And when he told us he was taking a police job in a small South Carolina town so he could spend his golden years close to his grandkids, I was so relieved. | | | | | How could I have known he was about to face the greatest danger of his life?I’m not talking about a drug dealer or a terrorist or even cancer......but a local prosecutor hellbent on destroying my brother for defending himself when he was the victim of a road rage incident. Let me explain.The day Anthony was attacked, he was off duty. He and his wife had stopped for lunch after spending the morning at a “Coffee With A Cop” community event.And as they tried to pull out of the crowded restaurant parking lot......another driver, in a fit of road rage, jumped out of his car and began screaming threats at my brother. Anthony tried to calm him down.But the man attacked him, striking him over and over.My brother could see the situation was spiraling out of control. He pulled out his badge and told the man he was under arrest.But instead of complying......the man knocked the badge out of Anthony’s hand.Then he got in his car and tried to flee, dragging my brother with his vehicle and running over his legs.In that moment, Anthony knew he was about to be crushed to death in front of his own wife.So he fired a single shot into his attacker’s arm, bringing the car to a stop.Anthony’s quick thinking saved his life.But the road rage driver who attacked him died at the scene. When I got the call that Anthony had been assaulted and was in the hospital with serious injuries, I couldn’t believe what had happened.I was so relieved he was alive. But my relief turned into shock when my brother was arrested and charged with murder. He hadn’t even recovered from his injuries when the local prosecutor dragged him in front of a judge and had him locked up in jail.He’s already spent 10 months behind bars.And he’s facing up to 30 years in prison.My friend, Anthony is 64 years old.If he’s convicted......he’ll likely spend the rest of his life locked up--and die in prison--for defending himself. | | | Because what they’re doing to Anthony is an outrage. I might not be a cop...but to me, if a police officer puts you under arrest, you don’t resist.And you certainly don’t physically attack the officer, then try to flee the scene.My brother may have been off duty. But you know that as an off-duty officer, he had the authority--and even the responsibility--to make an arrest to protect the public. What does this prosecutor expect off-duty officers to do--just let angry, violent offenders beat them up, resist arrest, and then walk away like nothing happened? | | | | | My friend, Anthony doesn’t deserve this.He’s a good man who’s well-respected by his fellow officers. He served as a cop for four decades and never once faced discipline. He has a spotless record full of awards and commendations.So to watch my brother’s life be torn apart like this is just heartbreaking.It’s been hard on his family too. Several years ago, Anthony and his wife took their two granddaughters into their home. They’ve been raising them ever since. You can imagine the pain it’s caused these poor girls to have their grandfather locked up and treated like a common criminal.My friend, we were almost out of hope.And then we found out about the LawEnforcement Legal Defense Fund. You know the LELDF is a national group that’s helped dozens of innocent officers clear their names when they’re wrongly accused by radical prosecutors.And they’ve agreed to help Anthony too.Not only are they getting my brother the legal defense he deserves -- they’re also raising money to pay for the best attorneys and expert witnesses available. Which brings me to the reason I wrote you today: Because the truth of it is, the legal bills are already overwhelming. And we haven’t even gotten to trial!Anthony and his wife have already drained almost their entire life’s savings fighting to free him. So any amount you can give today will help.And because LELDF is a non-profit organization, your gift is completely tax-deductible. After the four decades serving his community, the cancer, and the injuries from his attack, Anthony deserves to spend his retirement years in peace with his family -- NOT locked up behind bars for the rest of his life.But that’s exactly what will happen unless friends like you step up on his behalf.Thank you for taking the time to read my email today. And please, keep my brother in your prayers. Frank DeLustro P.S. Anthony didn’t know it at the time, but the road-rage maniac who attacked him had a criminal record. Maybe that’s why he was so eager to flee the scene after my brother arrested him. | | | 2560 Huntington Ave. Suite 203, Alexandria, VA, 22303 | Pop Acta Media | Republican Task Force PO Box 461 Fort Collins, CO 80522 |

The most recent, high-profile instance of jihadist terrorism occurred last week when [Omani flydubai pilot Hamam al-Hammami](https://substack.com/redirect/56cbe4b9-1e33-4c23-8b6f-c23c2bd3fba5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tried to murder his Indian co-pilot, Smith Machchhar, so he could fly the plane into the Ben-Gurion Airport in Israel. Elise Stefanik (R-NY)](https://substack.com/redirect/533573d2-9036-4872-b9b6-4955766b659f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) questioned Harvard's then-President Claudine Gay on whether campus faculty calling for the "genocide of Jews" violated the school's code of conduct, Gay weakly responded, "[It can be, depending on the context](https://substack.com/redirect/cc4dd05e-513c-4803-b516-196af00c2dd0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." Soon after the hearing, Gay resigned in disgrace.
Vapid Hollywood actors talk about "Freeing Palestine!" while parading around in tuxedos with their private armed security guards.
