name: Gina Hinojosa for Texas
subject: “Our governor took billionaire money”
body:
He hasn’t backed a Democrat since the 1990s. Here’s what changed.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, take a look at what Texas voters are saying about the Republican Party:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261009_3_nyt.RT2F6V&refcode=em20261009-2378&amount=5&t=1&akid=2378%2E299639%2E5SDGUx)
**He voted for Donald Trump in 2024. This November, he’s voting for Gina Hinojosa. And he’s not alone.**
He’s a school superintendent in East Texas, and the last time he voted for a Democrat was back in the 1990s. But he watched Greg Abbott take billionaire money to force through private school vouchers, draining the public schools rural Texas depends on.
“Our governor took billionaire money and then used it to beat Republicans that us Republicans elected,” he said.
He’s done with a governor who hands tech companies whatever they want and leaves working families to fend for themselves.
Gina is hearing it everywhere she goes: from rural families living next to Abbott’s data centers, from lifelong Republicans who never imagined voting for a Democrat, from parents watching their schools drop to four-day weeks.
**That’s why this race is now a toss-up. We’re within reach of taking back Texas.**
But Abbott knows it’s close, too. He’s outspending us 6 to 1 and flooding Texas with ads to bury our message.
**[We can’t let him drown us out in these final weeks, Peter. clean_body: A federal law requires translating ballots, but not it all languages| | | | | | Section 203 of the 1965 Voting Rights Act has required certain states and local governments to provide voting ballots, registration forms and other election materials in more than just English. But not all languages are covered by Section 203's protections. We want to hear from voters in your area to get their feelings on the topic. Will you take our one-question poll right away? | | | Team: Should ballots be available in more languages to make sure all citizens can vote? By clicking a response below your answer will be automatically recorded: | | | = | | = | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities. = = Contributions or gifts to Integrity First Voter Action Project are not tax deductible as charitable contributions or as business expenses under IRC Section 162(3). By now, the impact of data centers on the communities in which they're built is well documented. These centers put unprecedented strain on limited water and energy resources, driving up costs for the rest of us. clean_body: | | | | Just a few weeks ago, the movement to save our public lands received a crushing blow: it was revealed that the Trump administration is quietly working to hijack over 17,000 acres of public lands across the West, including Oregon, to build data centers. By now, the impact of data centers on the communities in which they're built is well documented. These centers put unprecedented strain on limited water and energy resources, driving up costs for the rest of us. Last week, in an effort to block Trump's latest scheme to defile our public lands, I tried to fast-track passage of my bill that would ban the development of data centers on public lands. Senate Republicans blocked it. Republicans would rather let Trump do what he wants than lift a finger to protect our beloved public lands. Let me be clear: our public lands belong to you – the taxpayer. Not corporations, and especially not Donald Trump. But Republicans just proved they are all in on Trump's plan to build data centers on our public lands, and maybe even our national parks. This is just one more reason we need to elect a strong Democratic majority in the Senate this November that can fight back against the Republican agenda to sell off our public lands.= = Onward, Ron | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Ron Wyden instantly: | = | = | = | = ---|---|---|--- | | Paid for and authorized by Wyden for Senate. | This email was sent by Wyden for Senate P.O. The Fourteenth Amendment was written for freed slaves. Within twenty years, it was working for railroads.
On May 10, 1886, the Supreme Court heard 'Santa Clara County v. Southern Pacific Railroad' -- a dull dispute over California's property taxes on railroad fences. Before argument began, Chief Justice Morrison Waite reportedly told counsel the Court would not hear argument on whether the Fourteenth Amendment's equal protection clause applies to these _corporations_. "We are all of the opinion that it does." Those words never appeared in the ruling, which turned on state tax law. They appeared in the headnote -- the summary written by the Court's reporter, J.C. Bancroft Davis, a man with railroad ties of his own. Headnotes carry no legal force. This one had better publicity.
Three years later, the Court made it doctrine: corporations are _persons_ under both due process and equal protection. Meanwhile the amendment's intended beneficiaries watched it slip away. Legal historians -- Howard Jay Graham's tally, revisited in a recent Virginia Law Review study -- count 288 Fourteenth Amendment cases heard from 1868 to 1912. Only 19 involved African Americans...

Your electric bill pays the retainer. | | | Oct 9| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | The Fourteenth Amendment was written for freed slaves. Within twenty years, it was working for railroads. On May 10, 1886, the Supreme Court heard 'Santa Clara County v. Southern Pacific Railroad' -- a dull dispute over California's property taxes on railroad fences. Before argument began, Chief Justice Morrison Waite reportedly told counsel the Court would not hear argument on whether the Fourteenth Amendment's equal protection clause applies to these corporations. "We are all of the opinion that it does." Those words never appeared in the ruling, which turned on state tax law. They appeared in the headnote -- the summary written by the Court's reporter, J.C. Bancroft Davis, a man with railroad ties of his own. Headnotes carry no legal force. This one had better publicity. Three years later, the Court made it doctrine: corporations are persons under both due process and equal protection. Meanwhile the amendment's intended beneficiaries watched it slip away. Legal historians -- Howard Jay Graham's tally, revisited in a recent Virginia Law Review study -- count 288 Fourteenth Amendment cases heard from 1868 to 1912. Only 19 involved African Americans... Hey there.

It’s Haley, Jocelyn Benson’s Digital Director. I know you’re probably

to the chase:

Can we count on you to chip in $5 to Jocelyn Benson’s campaign today?

I know that question was more direct than usual, but with 25 days until
Election Day, we can’t afford to mince words.

As Jocelyn’s Digital Director, part of my job is keeping a close eye on
our fundraising numbers and making sure we’re on track to raise the
resources it’ll take to win this race.

I know you probably don’t want to spend your Friday afternoon hearing
about spreadsheets and projections, so I’ll keep this simple: October is

I filmed something this week that I would really like you to watch when you have a quiet two minutes. I did it at my kitchen table because like so many of you, my family had to make difficult decisions around our kitchen table. In 2013, my dad died of cancer. During his illness, my parents relied heavily on Social Security Disability to get through it. I moved home to help my parents and be there for my Dad. I know firsthand how health care costs can bankrupt a family and the emotional toll it takes. Programs like Social Security and Medicaid are not abstractions to me. They helped my family get through the worst stretch of our lives. That is why I have fought the way I have in Washington on healthcare.
1. We increased Medicaid funding by more than 30 percent since I took office.
2. We delivered billions more for local hospitals across the Hudson Valley and the country.
3. We went after the scam artists ripping off the system and taking resources away from families who actually need them.
4. I have voted against my own party when I thought they were wrong on it.
5. I signed a Democratic discharge petition in December to force a vote on extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits because I thought letting them lapse would hurt Hudson Valley families.
6. I voted for the extension in January. I was one of seventeen Republicans who did.

I am telling you all of this because Cait Conley has been running ads attacking my record on exactly this issue, and the ads are not true. I know how campaigns work. I know you cannot answer every attack, and I know most of them are not worth the oxygen. This one is different. This one is about the single most personal issue in my life, and the ads she is running are telling Hudson Valley voters a version of my record that does not match what I actually did or what I actually believe. So I decided the right way to answer them was not with a thirty-second attack ad of my own. It was to sit down at our kitchen table and share with you what I actually experienced.
Two minutes. Tom Anthony calls Boulder’s climate suit against Suncor hypocritical

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
as Boulder schools close amid a cost-driven exodus; and economists
Antoni and Heim argue Gen Z’s financial strain comes from
subsidized, regulated sectors — not capitalism — warning socialism

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, October 9, 2026.

– Team RMV

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

WEISER AND MARX SHARE RARE STAGE, BUT ADVANCE QUESTIONS YIELD FEW
SURPRISES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY TORI STORK, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Colorado’s two major-party candidates for governor shared the stage
Thursday at a Colorado Chamber of Commerce luncheon in Denver,
offering business leaders a chance to hear Democrat Phil Weiser and
Republican Victor Marx address the state’s mounting economic
challenges.

But anyone expecting a spirited debate encountered something
considerably more subdued.

Both candidates received the questions verbatim ahead of the event,
Weiser confirmed in a post-event interview. Combined with the seated
format and two-minute response limits, the advance preparation made
the forum feel more like a series of rehearsed responses than a
substantive debate.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

WEISER’S BLUEPRINT: WHAT HIS HEALTH PLAN WON’T SAY BEFORE ELECTION
DAY
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Gubernatorial candidate Phil Weiser’s health plan ties key
commitments to a single-payer study whose results won’t arrive until
after voters have already cast their ballots._

*
VAGUE COMMITMENTS WITH NO SPECIFICS: Weiser’s Healthy Colorado Plan
calls its first pillar, Primary Care for All, “a systemwide
mandate” without saying what it would require, whom it would bind,
or what statute would create it, and provides no cost estimate for any
part of the plan.

*
TIED TO A STUDY VOTERS WON’T SEE FIRST: Weiser pledges to act on
guidance from a Colorado School of Public Health study examining
single-payer model legislation drafted by the Colorado Foundation for
Universal Health Care, called Colorado Cares, but that report isn’t
due until Dec. 31, after the election.

*
UNANSWERED QUESTIONS ON THE RECORD: RMV asked the Weiser campaign in
August whether his commitment extends to the single-payer model, what
Primary Care for All would mandate, and what any of it would cost; the
campaign did not respond by the requested deadline.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

DENVER MASK BAN DREW A FEDERAL SUIT AFTER COURTS BLOCKED 4 SIMILAR
LAWS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_The DOJ sued Denver over its ban on masked, unidentified law
enforcement, calling it an unconstitutional attempt to regulate
federal officers, after courts blocked similar laws in four other
jurisdictions._

*
A LEGAL THEORY WITH A TRACK RECORD: DOJ argues Denver’s ordinance
unlawfully regulates the federal government under the Supremacy
Clause, the same theory courts have already used to block nearly
identical laws in California, Philadelphia, New York and Virginia,
with Milwaukee also facing suit.

*
THE ORDINANCE APPLIES BROADLY, BUT FEDERAL AGENTS ARE THE TARGET:
While Council Bill 26-0125 defines “law enforcement personnel” to
include local, state and federal officers alike, DOJ’s complaint
cites sponsors’ own statements, including one councilwoman
describing it as preparation for ICE’s arrival, as evidence of its
true aim.

*
COMPETING CLAIMS OVER OFFICER SAFETY: The complaint cites alleged
doxxing incidents against ICE officers in the Denver area as
justification for masking, while the ordinance’s sponsors had
earlier argued in a January presentation that masking functions as an
intimidation tactic rather than a safety measure.

featuring the anti-Trump slogan “No Kings."_

__

YOUNG GUNS: MEET THE NEXT GENERATION OF COLORADO REPUBLICANS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
BY HEIDI GANAHL | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 9

_The knock on Colorado Republicans for years has been the same one: an
aging bench, a shrinking footprint, a brand that can’t connect with
younger voters in a state that keeps drifting left. That critique
might need updating._

__

ANTHONY: BOULDER SUES SUNCOR OVER CLIMATE WHILE LEASING 12,000 ACRES
TO CATTLE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
BY TOM ANTHONY | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 8

_As a Christian I get use of some ancient wisdom to toss around as I
see fit. I defer to Matthew 7:5, “You hypocrite, first take the log
out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck
out of your brother’s eye.”_

__

submit@rockymountainvoice.com.

In 1845, Congress mandated that Election Day would be the first
Tuesday after the first Monday in November. This was intentionally
designed for an agrarian society: it allowed farmers a full day to
travel by horse to the county seat after Sunday church services, but
took place safely after the fall harvest and before harsh winter snows
set in.

An Ordinary Office Park in Austin. What’s Designed Inside Ends Up in Your Phone.
Texas has poured nearly $700 million into chips, Samsung is building Tesla’s AI chip nearby, and one of the world’s leading chip designers just expanded its biggest U.S. site in Austin. The factories get the headlines. The designers often get the money.

Ask most people where the chips in their phone come from and they’ll say Taiwan, or maybe California. Few would say Texas. But some of the most important chip work in America now happens in unremarkable office buildings around Austin, behind badges and security desks, by engineers whose work ends up in devices billions of people use every day.

---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the state’s bet.** Texas passed its own CHIPS Act in 2023, putting nearly $700 million into semiconductor research, design, manufacturing and workforce training.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the designers.** In February 2026, Texas awarded a $4.16 million grant to expand the Austin campus of one of the world’s leading chip-design companies, its largest U.S. site, with a $71 million investment and more than 320 new jobs. Its CEO called Austin “a rapidly growing center for advanced chip design.”
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the factories.** Samsung has made chips in Austin for decades and is now producing Tesla’s next AI chip on trial lines at its new fab in nearby Taylor, under a $16.5 billion contract.

| | Designers vs. Manufacturers
---|---
| | “Austin is a rapidly growing center for advanced chip design.”— Statement accompanying a Texas semiconductor grant, February 2026
---|---
What it says
More chip engineering is moving to Texas.
What it means
**Our theory:** the factories get the attention because they’re huge and expensive. But the blueprints are where the leverage sits. A chip design can end up in hundreds of millions of phones, laptops and cars, made by many factories. Whoever owns the design gets paid on every one of them, without owning a single factory.

**Often the designer.** A factory has to spend billions on equipment and compete on price. A designer can license the same blueprint to many manufacturers and earn on every unit shipped. **Our theory:** that’s why some of the most profitable companies in tech are ones that never touch a production line.

name: Brig. Gen. Steve Anderson (Retired)
subject: Fort Hood
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
#
Peter —
Nidal Hasan murdered 13 people at Fort Hood on November 5, 2009, and wounded more than 30 others. Most were unarmed soldiers waiting for medical checkups before they deployed. A military jury convicted him in 2013 and sentenced him to death.
**But that isn’t extreme enough for Pete Hegseth.** This week he announced that the execution would be livestreamed — the first time our government has _ever_ broadcast one to the public — and President Trump signed off on it.
I spent 31 years in uniform. I served 15 months in Iraq as the senior logistician. The enemy we fought there, al-Qaeda in Iraq, became ISIS. Filmed killings were how they recruited and how they spread terror. It was barbaric, and it was done to fight against everything this country stands for. An American Secretary of Defense copying the ISIS format makes me ill.
The families of those 13 killed that day at Fort Hood carried a loss for 17 years that cannot be measured. The soldiers and civilians in that building watched their friends gunned down. Very few Americans can understand what that does to a person.
Now the Secretary of Defense is taking the worst day of their lives and building a production on top of it that would make the Romans at the Colosseum blush. They will relive that day through an over-the-top Trump production whether they tune in or not.
VoteVets has talked to people who were there. So I can say with confidence that not everyone who survived Fort Hood thinks a livestream or big public show at Fort Hood is justice. We must raise our voices.
[**Peter: Add your name to demand Pete Hegseth and the Pentagon cancel the livestreamed execution.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/Sep_Fort_Hood_em/?source=em261009-1-misc&refcode2=35685.3013755.AcDCZi&akid=35685%2E3013755%2EAcDCZi)

clean_body: Peter — Nidal Hasan murdered 13 people at Fort Hood on November 5, 2009, and wounded more than 30 others. Most were unarmed soldiers waiting for medical checkups before they deployed. A military jury convicted him in 2013 and sentenced him to death. But that isn’t extreme enough for Pete Hegseth. This week he announced that the execution would be livestreamed — the first time our government has ever broadcast one to the public — and President Trump signed off on it. I spent 31 years in uniform. I served 15 months in Iraq as the senior logistician. The enemy we fought there, al-Qaeda in Iraq, became ISIS. Filmed killings were how they recruited and how they spread terror. It was barbaric, and it was done to fight against everything this country stands for. An American Secretary of Defense copying the ISIS format makes me ill. The families of those 13 killed that day at Fort Hood carried a loss for 17 years that cannot be measured. The soldiers and civilians in that building watched their friends gunned down. Very few Americans can understand what that does to a person. Now the Secretary of Defense is taking the worst day of their lives and building a production on top of it that would make the Romans at the Colosseum blush. They will relive that day through an over-the-top Trump production whether they tune in or not. VoteVets has talked to people who were there. So I can say with confidence that not everyone who survived Fort Hood thinks a livestream or big public show at Fort Hood is justice. We must raise our voices. | Thank you. Brig. Gen. body:

[ ](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261009-3.OKs1I6&refcode=em-20261009-3&t=1&akid=2085%2E1086043%2ExBj82h)
Hey Peter, it’s Governor Josh Shapiro, and I wanted to send you a quick note from the campaign trail.
_(Yes, I’m back on the trail directly after our debate — no days off!)_
You might think that now that the debate is over, the “hard part” is done and we can coast through these final weeks of the race.
**But that couldn’t be further from the truth.**
We can’t coast in the state where our elections come down to a percentage point -- _or less._
We can’t coast in the state that voted for Donald Trump and every statewide Republican on the ballot less than two years ago.
**[That’s why, in the wake of this week's debate, I’m really hopeful we can make today our best fundraising day yet. Peter, will you rush a donation-- split evenly between our campaign and Wes Moore -- to help us capitalize on our momentum and finish this race strong?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261009-3.OKs1I6&refcode=em-20261009-3&t=2&akid=2085%2E1086043%2ExBj82h)**

Bitcoin Swung Below $84,000 This Week. Some Investors Got Paid Either Way.
Bitcoin’s wild swings scare most holders. But BlackRock now runs a fund that turns that volatility into monthly income, targeting 15–25% a year. Here’s how investors earn from Bitcoin’s moves without betting on the price, or even owning a coin.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Bitcoin fell below $84,000 this week after failing again to break above $87,000. For people who own it, that kind of swing is stressful. For a growing group of investors, it’s exactly the point. They’ve found ways to earn income from Bitcoin’s volatility without needing it to go up, and in some cases without owning a coin.
The evidence board
| | Volatility Has Become a Product
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the swings.** On October 7, Bitcoin dropped about 3–3.5% to roughly $83,300 in a single session. The largest Bitcoin ETF traded 35.6 million shares that day.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the Wall Street version.** In June 2026, BlackRock launched a Bitcoin premium-income ETF that sells call options on part of its holdings and pays the premiums out monthly. It targets a 15–25% annual yield. Similar funds from other issuers are already trading.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the trade-off.** Selling options caps part of the upside: if Bitcoin surges, the fund gives up some of the gain. Fees are also higher than for plain Bitcoin funds.
The mechanism
| | How You Get Paid for Bitcoin’s Mood Swings
---|---
| | STEP 1
---
Volatility creates demand
When prices swing hard, traders pay more for options to protect themselves or bet on moves.
| | STEP 2
---
Someone sells that protection
The seller collects the premium upfront, regardless of where the price goes next.
| | STEP 3
---
The premium becomes income
Repeated month after month, those premiums can add up to a steady stream of payments.
Decoder
| | The Biggest Asset Manager’s Signal
---|---
| | “Targets a 15–25% annual yield.”— BlackRock’s Bitcoin premium-income ETF, launched June 2026
---|---
What it says
You can earn income from Bitcoin without betting on the price.
What it means
**Our theory:** when the world’s largest asset manager builds a product around Bitcoin’s volatility, that volatility has become a recognized source of income. But a fund is a one-size-fits-all approach. Traders who know when to sell options, and when not to, can be much more selective about the premiums they collect.
| ClassificationTransition
---
Bitcoin is still volatile, and that isn’t changing. What’s changing is how investors use it. Instead of guessing where the price goes, a growing number get paid for the swings themselves. It’s a different way to approach crypto, and it doesn’t require owning any.

**The seller of the options.** Whoever sells protection collects the premium upfront, whichever way the price moves. **Our theory:** that’s why volatility, the thing that scares most crypto investors, is becoming a source of income for the ones who know how to trade it. Every strategy has risks, though, and options are no exception.

_Democrats Fight to Protect Hoosiers from Rising Utility Bills_
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141065460/652410909/964933876?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNTQ1NTY4MC0yZmM0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=q-EtPgxlNfTMFRjCh2v1zi_O3TXfQg2xF6keuqX4mvU=&emci=72911dae-2bc4-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=c5455680-2fc4-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=4925535) AES Indiana customers face higher monthly bills because Republican-appointed utility regulators approved a $71 million rate hike. This will go into effect in January even as state regulators rehear the case. Democrats have proposed state-level oversight on utility sales to private equity firms and ending sales tax on utilities. These firms are focused on maximizing returns for investors rather than providing affordable services for Hoosiers. Indiana families shouldn’t have to choose between paying utility bills and buying groceries. Democrats are standing up for ratepayers, while Republicans stand by as costs climb. _Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy or programs from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks. Hi friend, Deb here.
I want to give you a brief update on where we are in the fight to protect New Mexico's land, water, and sacred places, **[but first, will you chip in $5 or more to help me keep fighting to protect the places that make New Mexico so special?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1547-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13084%2E400544%2EuNhMRg)**
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1547-fr-nd&t=3&akid=13084%2E400544%2EuNhMRg)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1547-fr-nd&t=4&akid=13084%2E400544%2EuNhMRg)
---
Here's why protecting New Mexico's sacred lands is so important to me:
**FIRST:** I learned from a young age that we all have a responsibility to care for our planet. I grew up fishing with my dad and running through the New Mexico desert with my cousins. Those experiences gave me a deep appreciation for our state's natural wonders and the places where my ancestors built their lives in the high desert.
**THEN:** That love for New Mexico’s land and water is what led me to Congress, where I fought to protect the places that are part of who we are. And it’s what I carried with me to the Department of the Interior, where I worked to protect more land and water than any administration in our nation’s history.
**BUT NOW:** All that progress is being undone by this administration. Donald Trump is moving to slash protections for sacred lands, including the lands surrounding Chaco Canyon and Bears Ears, and reopen them to mining and oil and gas drilling — **putting New Mexico's public lands and sacred places on the chopping block.**
Friend: Governors are the first line of defense against the Trump agenda, especially when it comes to standing up to brazen attacks. As governor, I will be a fierce defender of New Mexico’s land, water, and sacred places. But I can’t win this race or protect our home alone.

Fellow Conservative,

Last week, Senate Democrats handed us the perfect closing argument for this election.

_In a single vote, every Senate Democrat — all 47 of them — blocked two of the most popular pieces of legislation in America._

**Voter ID. And a ban on Congressional insider stock trading.**

_Not one Democrat crossed over._

The Stop Insider Trading Act would have banned members of Congress from trading individual stocks using insider knowledge. It already passed the House — with 13 Democrats voting for it. It had broad bipartisan support from the American people who are furious that politicians profit while they serve.

Republicans paired it with a nationwide voter ID requirement — **photo ID to vote in federal elections, proof of citizenship to register. More than 80% of Americans support it.**

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: Shame alone is not enough
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Last week, many people across this country began to lose eligibility for Medicaid and food assistance programs like SNAP and WIC because of Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
#
It is unbelievably cruel that, in the richest country in the world, healthcare and food assistance would be ripped away from the working people to pay for tax cuts for the wealthiest people on the planet.
But that is what is happening right before our eyes.
Last week, many people across this country began to lose eligibility for Medicaid and food assistance programs like SNAP and WIC because of Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
This legislation represents the largest loss of healthcare in U.S. history. It is economic injustice in its most extreme form. It is a uniquely American tragedy, and we must all loudly speak out and organize against it.
I joined Senator Chuck Schumer to introduce a bill last week that would reinstate federal funding for New York’s Essential Plan and restore care for nearly half a million people impacted by these drastic cuts to Medicaid. I am proud to be leading that fight in Washington – but our collective fight must also happen far beyond the halls of Congress. It must happen directly in our communities.
Every single Republican legislator who voted for this catastrophe of a bill should feel ashamed of themselves. **But shame alone is not enough. We must make sure this vote costs Republicans their majority.**
[ If you are able, please make a donation of $5 or more to directly support three Democratic candidates I have endorsed who are running to unseat Republicans who voted for Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20261009.tjEzII&refcode=em20261009-12426-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12426%2E2526796%2ECh8-Gy)
In 25 days, we must prove what happens when politicians vote to line the pockets of billionaires and big corporations at the expense of working people like us.
On November 3rd, we can unseat two House Republicans – Rep. David Valadao and Rep. John McGuire – both of whom voted to pass Trump’s bill. Together, we can replace them with progressive candidates I have endorsed for the U.S. House who will fight to restore and expand healthcare access for working people: **Democrats Randy Villegas in CA-22 and Tom Perriello in VA-05.**
And in the Senate, we can replace Florida’s Republican Senator Ashley Moody, who supported these cuts, with **Angie Nixon.**
These heartless cuts to Medicaid and food assistance are a stark reminder that elections have consequences. From life-saving medication to the food on a working mom’s table, this is what we are fighting for when we mobilize our communities to the polls. By organizing together in these next 25 days, you and I can elect more progressives to Congress who will champion policies like a living wage, universal childcare, and guaranteed health care.

clean_body: Last week, many people across this country began to lose eligibility for Medicaid and food assistance programs like SNAP and WIC because of Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act. It is unbelievably cruel that, in the richest country in the world, healthcare and food assistance would be ripped away from the working people to pay for tax cuts for the wealthiest people on the planet. But that is what is happening right before our eyes. Last week, many people across this country began to lose eligibility for Medicaid and food assistance programs like SNAP and WIC because of Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act. This legislation represents the largest loss of healthcare in U.S. history. It is economic injustice in its most extreme form. It is a uniquely American tragedy, and we must all loudly speak out and organize against it. I joined Senator Chuck Schumer to introduce a bill last week that would reinstate federal funding for New York’s Essential Plan and restore care for nearly half a million people impacted by these drastic cuts to Medicaid. I am proud to be leading that fight in Washington – but our collective fight must also happen far beyond the halls of Congress. It must happen directly in our communities. Every single Republican legislator who voted for this catastrophe of a bill should feel ashamed of themselves. But shame alone is not enough. We must make sure this vote costs Republicans their majority. In 25 days, we must prove what happens when politicians vote to line the pockets of billionaires and big corporations at the expense of working people like us. On November 3rd, we can unseat two House Republicans – Rep. David Valadao and Rep. John McGuire – both of whom voted to pass Trump’s bill. Together, we can replace them with progressive candidates I have endorsed for the U.S. House who will fight to restore and expand healthcare access for working people: Democrats Randy Villegas in CA-22 and Tom Perriello in VA-05. And in the Senate, we can replace Florida’s Republican Senator Ashley Moody, who supported these cuts, with Angie Nixon. These heartless cuts to Medicaid and food assistance are a stark reminder that elections have consequences. From life-saving medication to the food on a working mom’s table, this is what we are fighting for when we mobilize our communities to the polls. By organizing together in these next 25 days, you and I can elect more progressives to Congress who will champion policies like a living wage, universal childcare, and guaranteed health care. In solidarity, Alexandria | ---|--- | | | ---|---|---|--- Email us: mailto: speak@ocasiocortez.com

Peter, we’re going to level with you.
We know you’re probably reading the headlines about our Senate race in North Carolina and feeling pretty good about our chances here. You might even be up-to-date on the latest polling.
**But it would be foolish for anyone to think we have this thing in the bag.**
We haven’t sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate from our state since 2008 – _since Barack Obama won his first presidential election._
President Trump has won North Carolina each of the three times he’s run.
Trump even handpicked Michael Whatley, a longtime GOP party leader, to run for this open Senate seat because of how important holding it is to defending his Senate majority.
**The momentum behind our campaign is surging, but we can’t leave anything to chance. Republicans have poured millions into this race to tip the scales in Whatley’s direction, and taking our foot off the gas right now would be the worst thing we could do.**
[**_Please, Peter, will you chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help us keep up our momentum, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1602&amount=5&t=8&akid=4354%2E124072%2E454OvU)

body:
Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. | | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141066538/652413986/2030301141?refcode=260925_troy_logger&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGU0OWUwZjctMzJjNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=GUOloZ9IByMaaAPmu4YRWQFrmgFYK2ZTZJrjruzSTdc=)
---
Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government.

And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it.

My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger.

**[Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the most important Senate race in the country.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141066539/652413987/2030301141?refcode=260925_troy_logger&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGU0OWUwZjctMzJjNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=GUOloZ9IByMaaAPmu4YRWQFrmgFYK2ZTZJrjruzSTdc=)**

---
[ _**DONATE TO DEFEAT SUSAN COLLINS AND FLIP THE SENATE!**_ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141066540/652413988/2030301141?refcode=260925_troy_logger&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGU0OWUwZjctMzJjNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=GUOloZ9IByMaaAPmu4YRWQFrmgFYK2ZTZJrjruzSTdc=)
---
Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.

When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.

After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power.

So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.

I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

Listen up, patriot...

I need to tell you about the worst 4 minutes of my life.

Last November, my neighbor's son fell off his bike. Hard.

Head wound. Blood everywhere. The kid was screaming.

His mom was frozen in panic.

I ran over to help...

And realized I had nothing.

No pressure bandages. No trauma supplies. Just some old Band-Aids in a drawer somewhere.

I stood there, helpless, watching a 9-year-old bleed while we waited for the ambulance.

12 minutes felt like 12 hours.

The paramedic later told me: "If that cut had been 2 inches to the left, those 12 minutes could have killed him."

That's when I learned the brutal truth:

The American Red Cross reports that 59% of injury deaths could have been prevented with proper first aid BEFORE the ambulance arrived.

Read that again.

More than half of people who died from injuries would still be alive if someone nearby had been prepared.

And according to the CDC, 44% of Americans don't even have a proper first aid kit in their home.

That ends today.

I spent the last year working with combat medics and EMTs to create something different.

Not another drugstore bandage collection...

But a real trauma kit that handles serious injuries when seconds count.

[The 1stHour Trauma First Aid Kit](https://em.ultimatepreptime.com/campaigns/xk127xtz1s9f6/track-url/ke2783b826e16/e7e60311637937086b55a0cfd9282076fbaf4eaa)

This is what's inside:

→ Combat tourniquet (stops life-threatening bleeding in seconds)
→ Israeli trauma bandage (battlefield-proven wound compression)
→ Compressed gauze (handles deep wounds)
→ CPR rescue mask (when every breath counts)
→ EMT scissors (cuts through anything)
→ Splint roll, burn gel, emergency blanket
→ Plus 75 more military-grade items

All organized in a compact, waterproof bag.

Normally $139.

Today? Just $49.

[Claim Your Trauma Kit at 65% OFF](https://em.ultimatepreptime.com/campaigns/xk127xtz1s9f6/track-url/ke2783b826e16/e7e60311637937086b55a0cfd9282076fbaf4eaa)

But here's the catch:

I only have 81 units left at this price.

Once they're gone, this deal disappears forever.

And honestly?

In an emergency, this kit could mean the difference between holding pressure on a wound and watching helplessly.

Between stabilizing an injury and making it worse.

Between a close call and a funeral.

You don't get a second chance to be prepared.

[Grab Your Kit Now - Only 81 Left](https://em.ultimatepreptime.com/campaigns/xk127xtz1s9f6/track-url/ke2783b826e16/e7e60311637937086b55a0cfd9282076fbaf4eaa)

I still think about that November day.

The kid was fine, thank God.

But I promised myself I'd never be unprepared again.

And I'm here to make sure you don't have to learn this lesson the hard way.

subject: This is a call for violence.
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20261009-2810-foote&t=1001&akid=2810%2E342411%2EZ_LJyt ]Squad Victory Fund

taken over by Somali Immigrants. There is Violence, Murder, and Mayhem all
over the State. The people of Minnesota must fight back. You have been
robbed, and abandoned by your State Government. Your Governor is an
incompetent thief who doesn’t want to get involved. He just wants to get
out of town with as much as he can steal, and then, lead a quiet life. The
Somalians should not be allowed to get away with what they are doing. They
view you as weak and stupid people. Fight back Minnesota, fight back! If
you need, the Federal Government will come to your rescue. Governor Tim
Walz, and Mayor of Minneapolis, Jacob Frey, must immediately ask for
Federal help — and leave the rest to us! President DONALD J. TRUMP'

Peter, it’s
Rep. Ilhan Omar. I’m pissed off.

It’s been almost a full year of Trump putting Somali-Americans and my
great state of Minnesota in his crosshairs. It resulted in ICE storming
into my city, racially-profiling people who look like me, brutalizing my
neighbors, and murdering two of my constituents.

Now he’s claiming that Somali-Americans are bringing “violence, murder and
mayhem” to my state and that people should “fight back.” He even says that
“they view you as weak and stupid people” — fascist rhetoric painting
Somali-Americans as different from any other American. Us vs. Them. He
finishes by adding, “If you need, the Federal Government will come to your
rescue.”

After the horrorshows that were January 6th and ICE’s occupation, it’s
clear that this is a direct call to violence for Trump’s supporters, with
a promise that ICE and the White House will back them up.

This man is a danger to my constituents. He is a danger to this country.
He is a danger to the entire world. And we have to stop him.

In a little over three weeks, the American people have a chance to send a
resounding message of disapproval to the deranged MAGA alliance currently
in charge. A chance to take power out of their hands and into the hands of
our progressive movement.

If we win, we will veto Trump’s agenda. We will block his appointments. We
will investigate his corruption. And we will use the power of the Congress
to rein in this criminal.

Squad Victory Fund as we organize against Trump’s fascist agenda ahead of
Election Day. Minnesotans stand against this racist garbage, and with your
help, we will prove that we stand together in peace in the face of hate,
division, and calls for violence.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261009-movement.Jr9Jc4&refcode=em20261009-2810&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1022&akid=2810%2E342411%2EZ_LJyt ]Contribute ››

In solidarity,

Ilhan Omar

Peter — I’m reaching out with some good, but urgent news: in three
different House districts, we just tested a special strategy to connect with
voters about their energy bills and the effect their representatives were having
on costs. We ran the before-and-after data, and the results were shocking — we improved polling for pro-environment candidates by four points. Consistently.
In all three districts. It’s a total game-changer. Enough to turn this election into a landslide. But Peter — early voting is already underway in many places. We’re
running out of time to scale our strategy up to make the kind of impact we
need. We need your help in this critical phase so we can head into Election Day stronger than ever, as we continue to knock on doors and help close the gap in close House and Senate races. https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/dmyWFLGWX_ 🗾 Here’s our roadmap to winning for the environment in the midterm elections — and where you fit in, Peter. In battleground districts, our research shows that 51% of undecided voters consider the cost of utilities like electricity and
heating to be the most important issue when deciding who should represent them
in Congress. These are the voters we’re working so hard to reach before the midterms. In order to win, we need these voters to cast their ballots for candidates who will prioritize everyday
people over corporations, commit to investing in clean energy, provide a
backstop against Trump’s unchecked federal power, and advance strong
environmental policies. Here’s our roadmap to making that happen:

📍 We’re meeting voters where they are. We’re knocking on 300,000 doors in Michigan and Ohio, where both House and
Senate races are extremely close. We’re reaching voters in key districts across
the country by contacting them at their front doors, by mail, by text, and
through digital media to maximize our reach. Pitch in $15 or more today to help power LCV Victory Fund’s work to reach out to voters >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/4L4XBd~

📍We’re helping people get to the polls and “chasing” their ballots if needed.We’re helping voters navigate election barriers to mail-in voting and conducting
targeted “ballot chases” to ensure ballots are returned on time. Your contribution of $15 or more makes this work possible ahead of November’s midterms >> https://links.messages.lcv.

📍We’re using tried-and-tested messagingto guide the conversation with undecided voters to get them to turn out, cast
their ballot, and have their voices for lower energy costs heard, whether we’re
reaching them by mail, phone, or at their front door. LCV Victory Fund relies on the support of people like you to hire and train canvassers to persuade voters to show up and vote for climate champions >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/bxyvTV~ HELP WIN IN NOVEMBER https://links.messages.lcv. We know this approach works and our efforts are only getting stronger. Since 2025, LCV Victory Fund and our state affiliates have helped deliver key
races for climate and clean energy champions in Georgia, New Jersey, and
Virginia by leaning into local energy affordability messaging and turning out
targeted voters. Your contribution of $15 or more helps LCV Victory Fund: ✅ Mobilize the 51% of undecided voters who are fed up with their energy bills
rising higher and higher while oil and gas companies are raking in record
profits.

races that can provide a backstop against Trump’s unchecked federal power.
✅ Reach voters by calling, knocking on doors, texting, and running ads to make
sure people know what’s at stake in November. But our ability to continue mobilizing voters depends on your support, Peter. body:
Farmers didn't cause this. Washington did.
Farmers didn't cause this. Washington did.

| | | | |
---
Peter,
Farmers across this district are calling it the [worst crisis in decades](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/J3-euX7zGcrvCZI6adcTaQ~~/AAUS1hA~/GUCh3n984IkN8m7FMPLyYQwAKTpf-qb7BDluq18RqmafR5yp3xlrMuOxZ5wXMJmpC9LvAv3kNhYJmsmtS0seTueB-ogRc7VMmxEmZMMVXmXWJm77eJ0RMMMlcWG8WY9g_SZkku14NfODlbg69HiTs3HuvUbggF6NahQ1FCbDfJIoBL-PFXZ7uhUbhIYXTBc7). And they're right.
The war in Iran is driving up input costs on everything from fuel to fertilizer. Tariffs are piling on top of that, squeezing farmers who are already stretched to the breaking point. Together, they're creating a crisis that Tennessee farmers did not cause and cannot afford.
My opponent supports the war. He praised the tariffs as "very effective." I don't know which farmers he's been talking to, but it's not the ones I've sat down with in every corner of this district.
I oppose the war in Iran. I oppose these tariffs. I'm running to serve Tennessee farmers and families, not the policies that are wrecking their bottom line.
New polling puts this race at 41-46. Five points, with less than a month to go and 11% of voters still undecided. That gap closes when voters hear the truth about what's actually happening to the people who feed this country, and it takes real resources to make sure they do.

Tom Shattuck, Steve Robinson, Jon Fetherston and the panel recap Collins and Jackson's Senate debate. Graham Pollard and Seamus Othot join as the panel covers Jackson's claim that Collins backed the Iran war for profit, her "you owe me an apology" reply, and what they call a quiet night for Jackson spin after the exchange. They also walk through his answers on Maine's health-insurance and electricity costs versus New Hampshire, and continue Jon Fetherston's field reporting on provider care complaints in Lewiston.

You want to know the secret to running a good campaign — or my secret, anyway? Meeting folks all across the state and _listening._

🗣️ That’s why even as this race heats up, I’ve taken every opportunity to talk to Kansans about why I’m running, _listen_ to what’s on their minds and all the ways Washington is failing them and explain how I’ll champion them in the Senate.

🚗 We’ve traveled to schools and churches, farms and local businesses, the Kansas State Fair and a memorable chili cook-off. We even held a block party at my childhood home — talk about a full-circle moment.

🤝 I’m proud to have received endorsements from two former Republican Kansas governors over the past month. These leaders know that this isn’t about red vs. blue.
Our Senate race is about the future of our country and about giving Kansans a leader who will put our state first.
